## Purpose

Tracks every place where we shipped less than the PRD spec — intentionally and with our eyes open — so that:
- Future-Claude knows exactly what's stubbed and what's real
- Pre-launch QA has a single checklist of things to verify before release
- Future workstreams (or polish passes) have a definitive list of follow-ups
- We never lose track of "we said we'd come back to this"

This document is appended to, not rewritten. Entries are immutable once added; resolutions are tracked by changing status, not by deletion.

This document is the companion to:
- `kiwi_prd_v1.0_locked.md` — the spec we're building against
- `kiwi_remediation_progress.md` — current code state and workstream status
- `kiwi_pre_launch_checklist.md` — infrastructure prerequisites
- `kiwi_workflow_playbook.md` — the per-workstream process

When a deferred item is finally picked up, mark its status **RESOLVED** with a `[WSn]` reference to where it landed. Don't delete it.

---

## How to read entries

Each entry has the following structure:

- **ID:** `D-WSn-NNN` — sequential per workstream (e.g., `D-WS3-001` = first deferral logged in WS3)
- **Title:** one-line descriptor
- **Tags:** one or more of:
  - `[STUB]` — a placeholder that returns empty/no-op until real implementation lands
  - `[SIMPLIFIED]` — shipping a less complete UX than PRD spec; works but not polished
  - `[DEFERRED]` — explicit decision to push to a later workstream or pre-launch
  - `[ASSUMPTION]` — a reading of the PRD that hasn't been explicitly confirmed; documented for transparency
  - `[TODO]` — small task that didn't fit cleanly into a sub-phase
- **Source:** PRD section ref + sub-phase where the decision was made
- **Current state:** what's actually shipped today
- **Target state:** what PRD §X specifies (or what "done" looks like)
- **Owner:** which workstream or phase picks it up — `WS6`, `WS7`, `pre-launch`, etc.
- **Notes:** anything future-Claude needs to find, verify, or watch out for

---

## Status legend

- 🟡 **OPEN** — currently deferred, not yet picked up
- 🟢 **RESOLVED** — picked up and shipped per spec
- 🟠 **PARTIAL** — partially picked up (e.g., backend done, UX still simplified)
- ⚫ **OBSOLETE** — no longer needed (PRD changed, scope changed)

### D-WS7-035 — Per-plan-generation override of household / wants leftovers / plan length without writing back to UserPreferences

- **Tags:** `[MOBILE]` `[WIZARD]` `[UX]` `[WS7-5]`
- **Source:** WS7-2-F final ruling (May 21, 2026) — Hans, ratifying that the household range stays 1–30: *"for now, leave it at 30 and we can log a deferral to evaluate if we want to override default prefs set during onboarding or in profile user prefs when a user gets a new meal plan (I vote NO), but allow a per plan generation change to the default without overriding the user's default"*.
- **Status:** ✅ RESOLVED — built in **Cookbook Phase B Block 4** (July 10, 2026). Ruled May 21, 2026; built July 10, 2026. **Scope extended well beyond the original three fields** (see "As built").
- **Hans's direction (May 21, 2026):** onboarding and profile defaults persist as the user's saved defaults; the plan-generation flow allows per-run overrides of `householdSize`, `wantsLeftovers`, `planLengthDefault`; **overrides do NOT write back** — they apply only to the in-progress generation. Verbatim: *"the requirement is: user sets prefs during onboarding and later in user preferences (profile section). those settings persist for the user. if the user changes the defaults during plan generation, those prefs influence the plan they're generating but don't override user prefs."*
- **As built (July 10, 2026):** both wizard screens (Set-Prefs and Tell Kiwi) **hydrate from stored `UserPreferences`** on open, allow **per-run edits**, and **never write back**. Identical structure on both, for consistency:
  - **Always visible:** plan length, household size ("Cooking for").
  - **Collapsed disclosure "Adjust saved prefs for this plan"** (closed by default; inline collapsible-card idiom — **no Accordion component was built**): cuisines, weekly pacing, dietary restrictions, discovery meals, sauce preference, max cook time, cook-time coverage (coverage gated on a cap being set).
  - **Screen-specific:** the wizard keeps its notes field expanded; Tell Kiwi keeps its free-text box plus an always-visible plan-length chip row — Tell Kiwi evolved from "name exact meals" into "describe the week and Kiwi plans it", so plan length can no longer be silently defaulted to 5.
  - **`wantsLeftovers` Switch REMOVED** from both screens and dropped from `WizardPreferencesInput` / `TellKiwiInput` (see D-WS7-190).
  - **Precedence:** per-run override WINS, stored pref is the fallback. The server-side resolver uses a `!== undefined` presence check (**NOT `??`** — see D-WS7-198). Test-pinned both directions plus explicit-null.
  - **Hydration was net-new:** neither screen read `/me/preferences` before (both used a hardcoded `INITIAL_FORM`). A `getPreferences` query was added to both, loading-gated, with graceful degradation — on prefs-read failure the overrides are omitted and the server uses stored values.
  - **No write-back is enforced by a source-level guard test** (neither screen imports or calls `patchPreferences`).
- **Owner:** WS7-5 (Wizard save commit + two-step expansion); built at Cookbook Phase B Block 4.
- **Downstream amendment:** honoring per-run overrides end-to-end required amending the Block-2 expand-stage design → **D-WS7-198**.
- **Pattern reference:** PRD §5.7 / §6.8 already established this for `wantsLeftovers` ("Default from preferences (or off)").
- **Notes:** ⚠️ Hans explicitly voted **NO** on write-back — this protects a user who picks a one-off household size (e.g. 30 for Thanksgiving) from having their saved defaults silently shifted.

### D-WS7-052 — Re-evaluate `bumpPlanRevision` over-invalidation cost

- **Tags:** `[PERFORMANCE]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-4 commissioning, May 24, 2026 (Ruling 8).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN
- **Owner:** WS9 polish.

### D-WS7-057 — Windows Prisma migrate operations documentation

- **Tags:** `[OPS]` `[DOCS]` `[WS7-4-C]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-4-C Phase 3 audit, May 26, 2026 (Anomaly A2) — recurring across WS6/WS7.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN (documentation work).
- **Current state:** each occurrence is recovered ad-hoc; the workflow lives only in chat memory across WS6-6c, WS7-4-A, WS7-4-C.
- **Target state:** `docs/operations/prisma-migrate-windows.md` or a CLAUDE.md section, optionally a `migrate:apply` script (`migrate deploy && generate`). **Owner:** WS9 polish (or WS7-CLOSE if batching docs). Not blocking — developer experience only.
- **The failure and its recovery, to document:** `migrate dev` hangs against Neon from Windows because the **shadow-DB creation path doesn't tolerate cold start**, and orphaned child node processes keep holding Postgres advisory locks after the wrapper is killed. Symptoms: unresponsive >5 min, an orphan `node.exe` in `tasklist`, advisory-lock errors on retry. Recovery: `taskkill /F` the orphan node PIDs → `prisma migrate deploy` (no shadow DB) → `prisma generate`, each via `pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server exec`.

### D-WS7-058 — My Plans list shows duplicate Instances from repeated Use-This-Plan taps

- **Tags:** `[UX]` `[PLANS-TAB]` `[WS7-4-D]` `[WS7-5]`
- **Source:** WS7-4-D c12 audit, May 27, 2026 — Hans's device test showed multiple copies of the same Template in My Plans after repeated "Use This Plan" taps.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Correct-by-design at the data layer; the UX-grouping decision deferred to WS7-5+.
- **Behavior:** each tap creates a new `MealPlanInstance`. Demote-prior-actives correctly maintains the "exactly one `isActiveThisWeek`" invariant (status stays orthogonal per Q-P1-6) and My Plans shows every non-archived Instance — so N taps yield N rows. c12 confirmed demote is correct at all three call sites (use-template, create-with-active, PATCH flipping inactive→active), running in the same transaction before the new active is created.
- **Options:** **(a) collapse duplicates** — group by template, most recent + an "N more" expander; **(b) filter by status** — hides past + draft but not same-status duplicates; **(c) leave as-is** — each Instance is a discrete plan; **(d) block at write** — 409 if a non-archived Instance of that template exists.
- **Recommendation:** product/UX call at WS7-5 commissioning — (a) if duplicates are sometimes valid but should be grouped, (d) if a duplicate is always wrong; (a) needs a PRD §8 decision on whether each tap should create a separate Instance at all.
- **Owner:** WS7-5 commissioning. Commission with D-WS7-027 + D-WS7-059 — same Plans-tab routing surface.

### D-WS9-005 — ChangeMealSheet import drops plan context (was candidate E)

- **Tags:** `[SHEETS]` `[IMPORT]` `[BUG]`
- **Source:** WS9 task-flow audit, June 12, 2026; logged July 3, 2026.
- **Status:** ✅ **RESOLVED AND BUILT — WS9 Block 3f-3, August 4, 2026** (device-verified across all three paths). ⚠️ **The July 5 ruling was WRONG and was NOT built as written.**
- **What it was:** "Bring in something new" omitted `addToPlanId` while AddMealsSheet threaded it, so importing a replacement from the Change-Meal path abandoned the swap and landed on Meal Detail instead of swapping the row.
- ⚠️ **CORRECTION 1 — THE FILE CITATION WENT STALE AND WOULD HAVE SENT A BUILD CHAT TO A DELETED FILE.** `ChangeMealSheet.tsx` had been merged into `SwapMealSheet.tsx` in 3d Part 4 (D-WS9-018), where the gap actually lived. **A file citation survives the refactor that moved its target — re-derive against live code, never carry forward.**
- ⚠️ **CORRECTION 2 — THE RULED FIX WAS THE WRONG FIX; BUILDING IT AS WRITTEN WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A DEFECT.** It said to thread `addToPlanId` **mirroring `AddMealsSheet`** — but **`AddMealsSheet` is the APPEND context and Change Meal is the REPLACE context**, and the append mutator has no `planItemId` parameter, so the fix would have **added the imported meal and left the old one in the slot**: the user asks to swap and gets a duplicate.
  - **Built instead:** the post-save nav resolver **extended, not duplicated**, with a third outcome `plan-replace`; precedence **`replace > append > detail`**, explicit and commented. Replace routes through the change-meal-for-plan-item path — server delete+create, day preserved, matching PRD §8.4.2 — with `planId` + `planItemId` threaded through the swap sheet, chooser, all three import screens and the builder; **"Create manually" from the swap context takes the same replace path.** **Two-write partial failure is deliberate:** if the meal save succeeds and the swap fails, a **blocking Alert** surfaces and **navigation does not happen**, so the old meal stays in the slot rather than the user landing somewhere that implies success.
  - ⚠️ **Phase 1b added a structural guard, and the reason is the durable part:** the resolver now accepts `mealId` and returns `detail` when present, because **"an edit never becomes a slot replace" was REAL but rested entirely on the save handler's edit-from-plan-context branch returning early** — one refactor from silently breaking. ⚠️ **The generalizable question: not *"is this true?"* but *"what ENFORCES this?"* — a verified behavior inherited from caller structure is a coincidence with a good track record.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-018 · D-WS9-110 · PRD §8.4.2 · BUG-058 (same sheet, 3f-4).

View → **Edit** is the R-B1Q1/D-WS9-004 plan-scoped ingredient editor ("just this time," MealPlanItem-level — the *same* 3f editor, no second build); **Change Recipe → REMOVED** (recipe tweaks are covered by editing ingredients — "chicken piccata is chicken piccata"; §8.4.3 deleted); Compost → **Remove from plan** (label only, this surface).

Picking one swaps into the slot preserving the day assignment (§8.4.2 create-new + soft-delete-old). ### D-WS9-019 — AI cost + latency efficiency program (pre-generation, model tiering, caching)

- **Tags:** `[AI]` `[COST]` `[LATENCY]` `[STRATEGY]`
- **Source:** WS9 Session 7 (July 6, 2026), from Hans's device testing: ~$0.22 per Prep-the-Week AI call, and AI-heavy steps (plan gen, grocery gen, prep sequencing) have long visible waits.
- **Status:** ⏸ DEFERRED — folded into the **WS7 recipe-catalog strategy arc** (Hans: "we can put it there"). Owner: **WS7 (strategy arc)**.
- **The concern (Hans):** an ads-in-loading-states revenue offset was considered and **explicitly parked** — the preferred direction is *"AI ahead of time and do more stuff on the server for most usage, [so] the loading will be much faster and we'll be back to the 'magic, not AI'"* experience.
- **The levers (sketch, unvalidated):** (1) **background pre-generation** — run prep sequencing at plan save/activate rather than at Prep & Cook tap, same for grocery lists, so the result waits in the DB; (2) **precomputed catalog** — serves most meal requests from the DB instead of live calls (why this entry lands in that arc); (3) **model tiering** — mechanical transforms (prep-step interleaving is largely scheduling math) may run on Haiku, reserving Sonnet for judgment-heavy generation; (4) **prompt caching**.
- **Scope boundary:** loading-state *presentation* stays WS9; making the waits shorter or disappear is this entry.
- **What it is:** no cost/latency budget discipline exists; every AI-heavy step runs live at tap time on the premium model, so cost is linear with usage and waits are user-visible.
- **Caching (July 8):** the standard ~5-min cache window is **too short for normal live usage** — users don't re-fire a prompt within 5 minutes — so caching does little at tap time, **but it is a real lever for bulk pre-generation**, where same-prefix calls run back-to-back. **Caching and pre-generation are ONE strategy: pre-generation manufactures the burst pattern caching rewards.** Both live plan-gen prompt bodies are **already cache-structured by construction** (static instruction prefix, single `{{var}}` at the bottom) — no restructuring needed. **VERIFY at build (these numbers change):** write-premium + deep read-discount (~10% directionally), byte-identical-prefix only, a ~1-hour tier at higher write cost, a ~1K token floor; enabled in the API-call code via `cache_control`, not per-prompt in `aiPrompts.ts`.
- **July 8 addendum #2 (Hans-approved):** (1) **Batch API for all upfront/bulk jobs** — verified against Anthropic docs July 8: Message Batches discounts **both input and output** 50% for async (≤24h) work and **stacks with caching**; since catalog seed / freshness drops / pre-generation are *output-heavy* while caching discounts input only, **batch is the bigger lever — route every non-user-blocking generation job through it.** (2) **Prep-the-Week amortization onto the catalog** — generate the prep sequence once per catalog plan (the macros-at-seed-time pattern) rather than per user-week; per-plan caching already exists (`PrepWeekStructure`, keyed by plan + revision drift, PRD §13.4.6), so this is moving that cache from instance to template level. **Known blocker: prep output is servings-dependent** (aggregation consumes per-instance servings; narration embeds concrete quantities). Options for the Phase C audit to price: (a) template-level generation at base servings + a cheap Haiku scale pass, (b) quantity-tokenized narration scaled deterministically, (c) amortize structure only. Plans modified after adoption fall back to live generation. Cross-ref `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §5.3/§5.7.
- **July 8 addendum #3 — read-only LLMCallLog cost audit ✅ COMPLETE.** ⚠️ **Thin/dev-only sample — findings PROVISIONAL:** 1,627 rows, June 12–July 8, one non-null userId (Hans's own testing), $15.68 lifetime — enough to rank the *shape* of the problem, **not to assert production $/day.** (1) **`prep.narrate_steps` is the #1 target on all three axes** — ~$0.18/call on v7 (4–7× any other Sonnet key), **p50 77s / p95 112s**, and the only key with failures; **baseline to beat: ~$0.18/call, p50 77s.** Its v2→v7 input growth (8.5k→32k tokens) is the July 2 aggregation fixes doing their job — **deliberate product improvement, so prompt-trimming is NOT the lever; addendum #2 is evidence-confirmed as the fix.** (2) **`nutrition.ingredient_estimate` is the volume king** — 62% of calls at $0.0019 each; a catalog / deterministic-macros play. (3) wizard latency (16–19s) **rides the catalog** — no separate build. (4) `costEstimateUsd` is consistent with token counts — the column is trustworthy. **Failure probe (§27):** all 7 `validation_failed` rows land Jul 2–4, **zero in the Jul 5 and Jul 8 sessions** — consistent with BUG-022's maxTokens fix (Jul 4). **NO BUG MINTED** (annotate-don't-mint, Hans-ruled; CC's candidate entries folded here rather than fragmenting the program); headroom past 16384 stays tracked as D-WS7-189; **mint a bug only if a post-Jul-4 `validation_failed` appears.** **Hans-ruled sequencing (locked):** (1) Prep-the-Week amortization + Batch API at cookbook Phase C; (2) catalog + deterministic macros for the nutrition volume; (3) wizard latency via catalog serving; **no standalone caching block** — caching pays only inside the bulk jobs, so it lands wherever those land. **Re-run the committed audit script before committing budget beyond lever 1.**
- **July 8, 2026 addendum #2 (Hans-approved, cost-strategy session — additive with the Phase A caching annotation above):** two levers ADDED to the program's scope. (1) **Batch API for all upfront/bulk jobs** — verified against Anthropic docs July 8: the Message Batches API discounts BOTH input and output tokens by 50% for async (≤24h) processing, and it stacks with prompt caching. Because the catalog seed / freshness drops / pre-generation jobs are *output-heavy* (writing full recipes and prep sequences) and caching discounts input only, batch is the larger discount for those jobs — route every non-user-blocking generation job through it. (2) **Prep-the-Week amortization onto the catalog** — the "common combinations" unit is the catalog plan itself: generate the prep sequence once per catalog plan (the macros-at-seed-time pattern, WS7-8b) instead of per user-week at ~$0.22/call. **Project-knowledge Phase 0 pre-check (July 8):** per-plan caching already exists (`PrepWeekStructure`, keyed `planId` + `lastGeneratedFromPlanRevisionId` drift, PRD §13.4.6) — amortization = moving that cache from `MealPlanInstance` to `MealPlanTemplate` level. **Known blocker:** prep output is servings-dependent (`prepWeekAggregation.ts` consumes per-instance servings; narration embeds concrete quantities — the WS7-8b servings-arc surface). Mitigation options for the Phase C commissioning audit to price: (a) template-level generation at base servings + cheap Haiku scale pass per household, (b) quantity-tokenized narration scaled deterministically (pairs with the existing mobile `quantityHighlight` machinery), (c) amortize structure only + deterministic quantity text. Plans modified after adoption (meal swaps) fall back to live generation. CC verifies on the live repo at Phase C commissioning: what in `structureJson` is servings-dependent, `prepWeekAggregation.ts` input shape, whether the sequencer prompt separates structure from quantities. Cross-ref: `kiwi_caching_pregeneration_resume.md` (updated same pass) + `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §5.3/§5.7.

### D-WS9-020 — Monetization model: trial-then-paywall (RULED at creation)

- **Tags:** `[BUSINESS]` `[MONETIZATION]` `[STRIPE]` `[FEATUREGATES]`
- **Source:** Business-plan session, July 8, 2026 (`kiwi_business_plan.md` v0.2 §3/§5).
- **Status:** ✅ RULED (the model) / ✅ **ALL FOUR SUB-DECISIONS RULED September 27, 2026 (D-WS9-267 rails + no-card; D-WS9-270 read-only + no AI, abuse guard accepted)** — implementation is Stripe S1/S2 on `next` (roadmap row 9; scope `claude/kiwi_stripe_scope.md` v2).
- **The ruling (Hans, July 8, 2026):** Kiwi is **trial-then-paywall, NOT freemium. A 14-day full-premium free trial**, then subscribe; **no permanent free tier.** The trial's AI cost is marketing dollars — the user proves to themselves the app fits their life, then they're sticky; 14 days spans two full plan→shop→prep→cook cycles, and week 2 is where stickiness shows.
- **Why:** freemium made 97% of accounts pure cost — at 3% conversion, 10K accounts netted only ~$1,300–1,500/mo even post-catalog, versus ~1,300 subscribers ≈ $9K/mo net under trial-paywall (funnel math: business plan §5).
- **Open sub-decisions (rule at Stripe commissioning, not before):** (1) card-upfront vs no-card trial (~40–60% vs ~8–25% trial→paid); (2) post-trial state — recommended: non-converters keep read-only access to what they created, no new generation; (3) checkout rails — native IAP intro offers (store-enforced one trial per account, 15% cut) vs web/Stripe (~97% net, needs its own trial-abuse guard) vs both; (4) trial-abuse guard design if web rails are chosen.
- **Consequences (no code now):** a permanent-tier `FREE_MAX_PLANS` cap is mooted — the gate structure reshapes into trial mechanics at auth+Stripe, where the everyone-is-premium stub retires. **With no free tier, public launch is gated on billing rails** unless soft launch runs as an explicit "free early access" period on the current stub, converting to trials when Stripe lands.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-019 (trial economics assume catalog-era costs) · `kiwi_business_plan.md`.

### D-WS9-028 — Tried & True rail fetch shape: 3 client queries, reshape at WS7-11 (RULED at creation)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[3A]` `[PERF]` `[API]` `[WS7-11]`
- **Source:** WS9 Block 3a Phase 1 (July 13, 2026). CC surfaced it as an **UNVERIFIED trade** rather than settled (§27), naming the alternative itself.
- **Status:** ✅ **RULED** (Hans, July 13, 2026) — **keep the client fetch; reshape when WS7-11 changes the data anyway.**
- **The structural finding:** the rail needs plans across **three badges** (hosting / featured / top_rated), but **`GET /home`'s `planDiscoveryCards` is SINGLE-badge**, keyed to the user's selected filter — **it structurally cannot produce a cross-occasion rail** — so the rail fetches client-side: **3 plan queries**, cache-shared with the Plans tab. *(Not a regression — the retired discovery card already fired 2.)* **The alternative CC named:** a dedicated **`triedTrueRail` field in the `/home` payload**, cheap because the home route was already open this block.
- **The ruling: DON'T do it yet — the reason is sequencing, not cost.** ⚠️ **WS7-11 (D-WS7-202) is about to change what this rail DISPLAYS** (D-WS9-027's missing meta). **The rail's data contract gets rebuilt one workstream out; optimizing the fetch SHAPE immediately before the PAYLOAD changes is the wrong order** — you'd move the Hosting-first ordering + cross-badge dedup server-side (working, 4 tests) only to revisit it weeks later.
- **What it costs meanwhile (named honestly):** on a **cold start** the flagship screen makes **1 payload call + 3 plan queries** before the rail renders — acceptable because the rail is **below the fold**, **does not block the make lane**, the queries are **cache-shared with the Plans tab**, and **the cost was never measured**: a suboptimal-looking pattern, not an observed problem.
- **→ Reshape at WS7-11**, with the real meta fields in hand. **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-027 · D-WS7-202.

### D-WS9-032 — The plan-options/preview flow is PAUSED: it (plus BUG-030 and "steps don't exist until save") is ONE problem, solved by a batch plan-generation-&-lifecycle arc (RULED at creation)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[3C]` `[ARC]` `[GENERATION]` `[LIFECYCLE]` `[BUG-030]` `[ROADMAP]`
- **Source:** WS9 3c device testing, July 15, 2026. Hans found the R5 flow "full of friction and confusing," then **correctly identified that the redesign, BUG-030 and "steps missing on drafts" are all symptoms of one root cause.**
- **Status:** ✅ **RULED** (Hans, July 15, 2026). **The plan-options flow is PAUSED; a new arc is defined next, ahead of resuming 3c.**
- **The realization (load-bearing):** the whole R5 flow — commit-gates, the expensive "View details," bullets-not-details cards, the peek-gate, the memoize-the-expand seam — is **scaffolding around ONE thing: the app generates plan details LAZILY and PER-USER.** Expansion is expensive → gated behind commit steps; "steps don't exist until save" because generation is deferred to save-time; **BUG-030** (🔴 P1 — back out, re-tap, AI re-runs, dupe plan+meals) because the draft lifecycle is **lazy, per-user, re-entrant.** Hans hit its sibling from a 2nd entry point (rail → Use plan → back), so it isn't wizard-specific.
- **⚠️ Why the "middle path" (build final UI now, swap data source later) was REJECTED here.** It's right when the interim seam is **clean** (a fetch swap under unchanged UI, as with D-WS9-028's rail). **Here the interim seam is load-bearing scaffolding around the exact thing being replaced**, so building it, device-testing a flow with known-wrong data timing, then tearing it out = **building the transitional complexity twice.** Hans: *"this probably requires a comprehensive arc to solve it all."*
- **Hans's target plan-options model (built AFTER the arc, to the finished world):**
  1. Expanded card → **rows with small meal images**, not bullets.
  2. **Tap the card → the real Plan Review screen** (shared with everyday use), NOT a wizard-private preview.
  3. Buttons: **"Save for Later" / "Use This Week"** (the 3b template precedent).
  4. **State-driven action bar:** the component that (when saved) shows Prep & Cook / Grocery List / Get Groceries Online shows **Save for Later / Use This Week while the plan is an unsaved draft**, flipping once saved. **One component, two states.** An already-saved plan never re-offers the save options.
  5. **Back from Plan Review → the 3-candidate results.**
  6. **Edit-guard** on an unsaved draft: *"To customize this plan, save it to your library for this week or later."*
  7. **Comment out** the standalone `wizard-plan-details` screen; **defer deletion** until the new flow is confirmed good.
- **The ARC (ahead of resuming 3c):** (1) **batch pre-generation** of meals + plans + full details **including steps** → stored, not lazy; (2) **draft lifecycle rationalized** — idempotent, no orphans (**BUG-030's real fix + BUG-023's deferred server sweep**); (3) **then** 3c's plan-options flow builds to the finished world.
- **⚠️ Sequencing:** the arc **pauses WS9 mid-3c** (breaks one-workstream-at-a-time — accepted). Already-built 3c work (Tell Kiwi restyle, wizard restyle, Surprise-me, BUG-035 fixes) **commits and keeps**; only the plan-options/preview flow waits. **Ship BUG-036's one-liner as a hotfix** so Surprise-me is testable meanwhile. **After the arc, resume at 3c's plan-options flow and run 3c→3g without a hiccup** (Hans's explicit ask).
- 🔴 **SUPERSEDED IN PART — September 16, 2026, by Hans's D-WS9-191 mockup rulings: the points that said *tap a card → the real Plan Review*, *a state-driven action bar with an unsaved-draft state*, and *an edit guard on an unsaved draft* NO LONGER APPLY. The chooser card carries Use This Week · Save for Later · Not For Me directly; a plan is only ever reviewed AFTER it is saved, on the existing Plan Review; the unsaved-draft state does not exist. Point 7 (comment out `wizard-plan-details`, delete after the new flow is device-confirmed) STANDS.** The batch pre-generation arc and BUG-030's lifecycle fix are unaffected.
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-030 · BUG-023 · BUG-036 · D-WS9-031 · D-WS9-028 · roadmap · **D-WS9-191** (supersedes points 2–4).

### D-WS9-037 — Coverage threshold: aggressive/store-biased provisional default, tunable, structural graceful-degrade; Block 3's 600-seed pilot calibrates (RULED at Block 2 commissioning)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[BLOCK-2]` `[BLOCK-3]` `[TUNABLE]` `[STORE]`
- **Source:** Block 2 commissioning, July 16, 2026, resolving the §3.2 OPEN threshold.
- **Status:** ✅ **RULED provisional (Hans)** — structural graceful-degrade **SHIPPED in Block 2**; exact value 🟡 **OPEN, calibrated by Block 3's pilot.**
- **The chicken-and-egg:** the pilot that measures the real number is **Block 3**, which runs *after* Block 2 — so Block 2 needs the threshold as a **tunable parameter** (not hardcoded — load-bearing) plus a safe provisional default.
- **The ruling (Hans): aggressive / bias-to-store-hits** — trust the store as soon as it can satisfy a request. The **600-meal seed run is part of getting live**, so real users hit a substantial store; and pre-gen is a **latency win as much as cost**, captured sooner by an aggressive threshold.
- **The structural safety net (why aggressive can't produce thin plans):** the read path degrades on **actual coverage, not the flag** — the compose call fills any gap **live regardless of the threshold**, so a thin store just yields more live fallback rather than scrappy plans. Closes the sequencing gap (read path ships before the seed).
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-033 §3.2 · §4 Block 3 · §5 (measure-don't-estimate).

- **Source:** Block 2 B-1 review, July 16, 2026; CC Flag 2, Hans-ruled.
- **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN (deferred, out of Block 2 scope)** — direction RULED.
- **The mechanism today:** repeat-avoidance (`excludeMealIds` via `recentMealIds`) is **id-based only.** A forked store meal gets a **different id** in the user's library than the store original, so the original can be re-offered even though the user "already had it." No lineage link between store meal and forked copies.
- **⚠️ Hans's ruling DIRECTION (flips the naive default):** do NOT build aggressive "never repeat" logic. The risk is NOT "user sees a repeat" — it's **"user gets the best burger of their life and then never sees it again."** A loved meal recurring is a **feature, not a bug.** Lineage-tracking, when built, must bias toward **letting good meals recur** — especially Saved / highly-Rated / Favorited ones. Ties to WS7-11's three tiers: a **Favorite recurring is desirable** (forward-looking staple intent), not something to dedup away.
- **Deferred scope:** lineage-tracking is out of Block 2. When picked up (WS7-11-adjacent, post-launch polish), build recurrence as **preference-aware** (recur loved meals, vary the rest), not blanket avoidance.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-038 · WS7-11 three-tier Saved-Rated-Favorite.

### D-WS9-040 — Block 3 CATALOG-QUALITY GATE: the seed harness must produce meals at wizard-meal quality, PROVEN at pilot scale before the 600-meal push (RULED at Block 2 device-test close)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[STORE]` `[BLOCK-3]` `[ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION]` `[LAUNCH-BLOCKING]`
- **Source:** Block 2 device-test, July 17, 2026 (Hans's Test-1 finding), ruled at Block 2 close.
- **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — Block 3 acceptance criterion; ruled, unbuilt.
- **The finding:** the **12 hand-seeded curated catalog meals** composed correctly (no 422 after BUG-040) but are **poor as meals**: all steps show **1-minute** timings, **no step-ordering optimization**, and "Big Greek Salad" is **just a salad with no protein** — not a dinner. Wizard candidates are robust by comparison.
- **⚠️ Critical distinction:** the weak meals are the **early hand-seeded fixtures**, NOT products of the Block 3 harness (which doesn't exist yet). This proves the **fixtures are weak**; it proves **nothing yet** about the harness. **Do not conflate "the 12 fixtures are bad" with "the catalog approach is bad."**
- **The ruling — Block 3's pilot gains a QUALITY gate, not just a cost gate:** it **must prove catalog meals hit wizard-meal quality BEFORE scaling to 600.** Ramp **10 → 20 → more**, inspecting each step. **Quality checklist (minimum):** (a) **protein-complete** — a dinner is a meal, not a side/salad alone; (b) **real per-step timings**, not uniform 1-minute stubs; (c) **step-ordering optimization** (prep-first / heat-last, the sequencing the wizard applies); (d) complete graph seeded (meal + dishes + ingredients + steps); (e) structured dietary/allergen tags + hard-filter retrieval. **Scale to 600 is GATED on passing this checklist at pilot scale.**
- **Mechanism to investigate at Block 3 Phase 0:** are the fixtures **hand-authored stubs** that skipped the wizard's step-optimization + protein pass, or does the **seed path skip a stage** the wizard applies? **The harness must route generated meals through the same quality-producing pipeline the wizard uses, not a thinner seed path.**
- **Efficiency note:** Hans's instinct — "generate plans, save all the meals" — is right on breadth but wasteful in shape (harvesting meals from whole plans pays for composition logic that's thrown away). Ruled out in favour of direct meal-generation with a byte-identical cached prefix — see **D-WS9-041**.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-033 §4 Block 3 · D-WS9-038 · D-WS9-037 · D-WS9-019 · BUG-018 · `kiwi_plan_generation_arc_scope.md` §Block 3.

### D-WS9-041 — Block 3 harness GENERATION SHAPE: direct meal-generation (Option A), not plan-harvest — try-and-adjust, escalate to plan-harvest only on pilot-quality failure (RULED at Block 3 commissioning, post-Phase-0)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[STORE]` `[BLOCK-3]` `[HARNESS]`
- **Source:** Block 3 Phase 0 read-only audit, July 17, 2026.
- **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — Block 3 build directive; ruled, unbuilt.
- **The question (from D-WS9-040):** generate MEALS DIRECTLY (shared byte-identical cached prefix) or generate whole PLANS and harvest (fidelity-by-reuse, but pays for ranking + slot-assembly it throws away)?
- **Phase 0 finding that decided it (✅ VERIFIED):** **every wizard meal-quality property is meal-scoped — none require plan-level context.** Per-step timings + phase metadata come only from the per-meal finalize-steps call; step ordering is computed **at cook-time** from persisted `phaseType`/`estimatedMinutes`/`isTimingSensitive`, so the harness need only persist correct metadata; protein-completeness has **no wizard gate at all** (soft prompt bias only). The one plan-level property is **soft cross-week variety** — composition, not per-meal quality, and it still happens live at wizard time.
- **The ruling (Hans): OPTION A — direct meal-generation.** (a) Phase 0 proved plan-harvest buys **no quality the direct approach can't get**; (b) direct-gen is the **only** shape keeping the `cache_control` prefix byte-identical, which is what makes the §5 ~10× economics work; (c) cheapest per meal. **Explicitly try-and-adjust:** start with A, run the D-WS9-040 quality gate, **escalate to plan-harvest only if pilot meals fall short** — with evidence, not pre-emptive cost. A is the reversible choice.
- **What the harness must do per meal for A to match wizard quality:** (1) produce dishes + ingredients + roles passing the expand-ingredient schema — **non-empty `unit`** (the DB-wide `"each"` convention for count-only items; this is the BUG-040 reject-to-live gate); (2) run a **finalize-steps-equivalent AI call** with real `estimatedMinutes` + `phaseType` + `isTimingSensitive` — **the load-bearing stage, sole source of cook-quality**; (3) persist as a store meal (`isPublic:true`, not archived, dinner, `sourceType:"batch_generated"`, meaningful tags) with **steps attached to the DISH** — ⚠️ the cook-time sequencer reads dish-owned steps ONLY, and the curated fixtures stored meal-owned steps that Cook Mode silently ignores (a second fixture defect beyond the timing stubs). Cache discipline per §5 is not optional. Add a **protein/entrée completeness check the wizard lacks** to avoid the next Greek-salad.
- **Allergen handling (amends D-WS9-038's "correctness requirement" framing):** allergens are **user-reviewed suggestions, not a medical safety gate** — a slipped allergen is a trust/frustration failure, not unknowing exposure. **The harness STAMPS structured allergen data on every batch meal** — **scale-coupled**, so it must happen during the run (re-deriving 600 meals later = a full re-run). The **hard retrieval filter is DEFERRED** — **not scale-coupled** (a cheap shortlist exclude clause, addable anytime). Interim guard remains the compose prompt.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-040 · D-WS9-038 · D-WS9-037 · D-WS9-019 · BUG-040 · BUG-018 · `kiwi_plan_generation_arc_scope.md` §4 Block 3.

### D-WS9-098 — Groceries index sort is PAGE-LOCAL (client re-sorts one ≤20-row page, not the full set)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[BLOCK-3e]` `[GROCERIES]` `[MOBILE]` `[SORT]`
- **Source:** WS9 3e Part 1 (§1.2), July 31, 2026.
- **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — no user impact at current data volumes; fix before a user can plausibly exceed 20 lists.
- **The gap:** the Groceries tab sorts **client-side over a single fetched page** — the fetch sends no `limit`, so the server clamps to **20** and the client re-sorts those rows. ⚠️ **For a user with more than 20 non-archived lists this is SILENTLY WRONG: A–Z alphabetizes only the 20 most-recent and omits older lists entirely** — it looks like a complete alphabetical list and is not.
- ✅ **What is NOT wrong (a stale-canon correction):** sort **direction and field are correct** — `createdAt` is an ISO string on the client, so `localeCompare` is sound. ⚠️ **The screen plan's long-standing "both sorts are no-ops that sort by title" claim was STALE — the sorts genuinely branch, and the no-op "By plan" option was dropped in B6.** Third instance this arc of canon asserting a state the artifact does not have.
- **The fix when needed:** move the sort **server-side**, or raise/paginate the limit.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-099 · WS9 flow ruling R3 · `kiwi_ws9_screen_plan.md` (the stale claim).

### D-WS9-100 — Grocery provenance `meal.findMany` is user-scoped BY INVARIANT, not by query

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[BLOCK-3e]` `[GROCERIES]` `[API]` `[DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH]`
- **Source:** WS9 3e verification turn (§3b), July 31, 2026 — chat-Claude asked, CC verified and flagged rather than fixed.
- **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — **low risk, not a live leak.** Logged so the invariant is written down rather than assumed.
- **The state:** the per-item meal-provenance label resolves titles via a one-shot `meal.findMany` on the collected source meal ids. ⚠️ **That query carries NO `userId` filter.**
- **Why it is safe today (the invariant, verified):** the source ids come from the list's own item sources and the list was fetched scoped to `{ id, userId }`; a user's grocery-list sources only ever reference that user's own meals — generation writes sources from the user's plan meals, store slots are **forked to user-owned at materialize**, swaps **fork-on-acquire.** **A cross-user title leak is not reachable while that invariant holds.**
- **Why it's still worth logging:** this is **defense-by-invariant, not defense-in-depth.** The invariant lives across three subsystems (generation, materialize, swap); any change letting a non-owned meal id reach a source row turns a silent assumption into a cross-user leak **through a UI label** — a hard place to notice it.
- ⚠️ **If the filter is ever added, a bare `userId` equality is WRONG:** catalog/public meals carry `userId: null`, so it needs `{ OR: [{ userId }, { userId: null, isPublic: true }] }`. (Plan-item meals are forked to user-owned, so bare `userId` would *likely* suffice — **"likely" is why this is a logged decision and not a drive-by fix.**)
- **Cross-ref:** WS9 3e Part 2 · D-WS9-099.

### D-WS7-062 — Scheduled draft sweep wants job infrastructure (lazy fallback shipped)

- **Tags:** `[INFRA]` `[WIZARD-DRAFT]` `[WS7-5a]` `[SWEEP]`
- **Source:** WS7-5a build, May 28, 2026. Hans preferred a scheduled sweep for abandoned wizard drafts; the prompt told CC to verify job infra first and fall back to lazy-sweep.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Lazy fallback is shipped and correct for WS7-5a product intent; the scheduled upgrade is the open decision.
- **Finding (VERIFIED by code read):** the api-server has **no scheduler / job-runner / cron infrastructure** — no queue or cron dependency, only comments about a future cron. Single Express app, no worker process.
- **What shipped (lazy sweep):** a per-user delete of drafts older than 30 days, as a side-effect of the wizard-drafts read; per-user scope keeps it bounded, failures swallowed so the read still proceeds.
- **The gap it leaves:** it only reclaims for users who *re-open the wizard* — a user who abandons and never returns leaves the row indefinitely. Harmless pre-launch, unbounded accumulation at scale.
- **Options (Hans to rule):** BullMQ + Redis (heaviest, most capable), in-process `node-cron` (lightest, dies with the process / no horizontal scale), or pg_cron (DB-side, no app infra). Each is a real infra commitment beyond the sweep logic — hence deferred rather than built unprompted.
- **Owner:** post-WS7 infra decision (one scheduler choice also solves the "permanent-deletion cron is post-MVP" gap). Not WS7-5b.

- **Tags:** `[MACROS]` `[PLAN-REVIEW]` `[PRODUCT]` `[WS7-5]` `[POST-WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5a close, May 28, 2026, spun out of D-WS7-060.

- **The long-term model Hans described:** a true per-day-intake view — each assigned day shows that day's *summed* macros (breakfast + lunch + dinner ≈1800 kcal, not one meal's ~600), plus a weekly-average-per-day rollup, plus the unassigned-meal bucket shown separately. Requires a Plan Review UI refactor, not just a divisor change.
- **Why deferred:** it changes the whole macros surface, not one number; the audience is planning dinners, not tracking diet-adherence, so the precision is lower-value pre-launch. Hans: "log a deferral for after WS9 to determine the long term plan."

### D-WS7-065 — Wizard-activation ingredient category inference is a deterministic first-pass

- **Tags:** `[MACROS]` `[GROCERY]` `[DATA-QUALITY]` `[WIZARD]` `[WS7-5b-server]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-server build, May 28, 2026 — recording the known coarseness of the deterministic-inference-at-activation ruling.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN, deferred to a future master-data reconciliation pass. Not a bug; the acknowledged tradeoff.
- **The mechanism:** a keyword matcher maps ingredient names to the **seeded** vocabulary — `Produce | Protein | Dairy | Pantry | Bakery | Frozen` (matched exactly to the seed; no invented strings), fallback `"Pantry"`.
- **The coarseness:** no "Spices" / "Condiments" / "Oils" category exists in the seeded vocab, so **all spices, condiments, oils, vinegars and uncommon ingredients land in `"Pantry"`** — correct (it's the catch-all) but coarse; proteins all collapse to `Protein`. Acceptable pre-launch; grocery lists are still usefully grouped.
- **Why deterministic, not AI:** activation must not block on or pay for an AI call.
- **The forward-compatible fix (build-it-right, §5):** the rules array is structured so a future master-data reconciliation pass — analogous to the WS6 6c-4 `purchaseUnit` AI writeback — can re-categorize after the fact without touching the activation transaction (add keywords or invert the lookup; no call-site changes). Pairs with the nullable-until-reconciled purchase-pack fields.
- **Owner:** future data-quality / master-data reconciliation pass (post-WS7). Not 5b-mobile.

### D-WS7-067 — Wizard-activate `$transaction` write volume wants batching (timeout raised as interim insurance)

- **Tags:** `[PERF]` `[WIZARD]` `[ACTIVATION]` `[WS7-5b-server]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-server smoke-fix, May 29, 2026. The first end-to-end real-Prisma run threw P2028; root cause **verified by measurement** (§27).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — interim timeout fix shipped; durable batching fix deferred to WS9.
- **What happened:** activate materializes the draft into a whole meal graph inside one interactive `$transaction`. **The unit tests stub Prisma, so they proved orchestration only — never real transaction behavior.** First live smoke hit **P2028**: the tx ran **5034ms against the default 5000ms** budget. Timeout confirmed by Prisma's own clock; the "missing await" hypothesis **ruled out** by a full await-audit — do not re-investigate.
- **Interim fix:** (1) **hoisted ingredient upserts OUT of the transaction** — ingredient rows are write-once reference content, so orphans on a later rollback are harmless and reused next activation; trims ~25–40 RTTs from the critical section. (2) **raised the budget** to 60s (maxWait 20s) — the post-hoist run measured the real un-clamped tx at **17,063ms** on 17 dishes, and the initial 30s pick gave only ~1.76× headroom because the first measurement was clamped at 5034ms and under-counted true work. 60s ≈ 3.5× over observed, absorbing dish-count variance.
- **The durable fix (WS9):** most remaining round-trips are per-row ingredient creates (~135) and per-step creates (~84). **Convert both loops to `createMany`** — collapses ~219 RTTs into 2 batched writes, cutting tx duration far more than any timeout number can. **The 60s budget is the band-aid until it lands.**
- **Why the timeout shipped anyway:** the smoke gate needed a genuinely-green end-to-end run; batching is a perf-durability improvement, not a correctness gate.
- **Residual UNVERIFIED (§27):** only 14- and 17-dish shapes measured; a 20+-dish tail case could approach 60s. Batching removes this risk class entirely.
- **Owner:** **WS9.** Not 5b-mobile.

### D-WS7-072 — Stale wizard-draft cleanup (resume interstitial offers un-saved drafts from prior sessions)

- **Tags:** `[UX]` `[WIZARD]` `[WS7-5b-mobile]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-mobile FIX BLOCK Phase 1, May 30, 2026 (device-test finding 4). After "Save for Later," the resume interstitial offered "pick up where you left off" with what looked like the just-saved plan. **Verified by DB inspection (§27): NOT a save-path bug** — save + activate correctly flip `isWizardDraft → false`; the offer was a *different*, stale draft row from an earlier "View Plan Details" tap that was never saved.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — diagnosed, no code change in the fix block.
- **Mechanism:** every "View Plan Details" tap fires a wizard expand, writing a fresh draft row (30-day TTL, lazy-swept on the drafts read). Trying several candidates leaves the others as live drafts; same inputs → similar AI titles → the offer looks like the saved plan.
- **Fix candidates (WS9):** (a) shorter TTL for never-touched drafts, (b) auto-discard a session's other drafts when one is saved/activated, (c) better interstitial disambiguation (timestamp / "1 of 3 from your last attempt"). **NOT a `decideWizardResumeUi` change** — it correctly trusts the server list.
- **Owner:** **WS9.** Relates to D-WS7-062 and D-WS7-063.

### D-WS7-073 — Server expands the client-submitted wizard candidate with no server-side candidate registry

- **Tags:** `[SECURITY]` `[WIZARD]` `[WS7-5c]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5c Block A addendum, May 31, 2026 — surfaced while VERIFYING input-chaining (Hans's concern that the AI might "rebuild" a different plan than the user previewed). **Chaining is correct and identity is server-stitched**; the trace also confirmed the route trusts the client-echoed candidate.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — VERIFIED, accepted non-issue for MVP, no fix in 5c.
- **Mechanism:** the expand route takes the candidate from the request body. Candidates are stateless by design — no re-validation against a "candidate I actually generated" registry — so a tampered client could post `mealTitles` no build call returned and the server would expand them. The WS7-5a stateless-candidate trust-boundary ruling restated: "Call #2 expands the plan the user saw" holds only as far as "the client didn't tamper."
- **Why non-issue for MVP:** no incentive to tamper against your own plan generation; no multi-tenant exposure. Relevant only if candidates ever carry server-trusted state (pricing, entitlements) or abuse/cost-control needs a "real candidate" gate.
- **Fix candidates (WS9):** (a) sign the candidate on issue and verify on expand; (b) short-lived server-side registry keyed by candidateId; (c) re-derive mealTitles from the candidate's generation inputs.
- **Owner:** **WS9** (hardening).

### D-WS7-075 — Defer wizard step-generation off the blocking Save path (background/lazy materialize)

- **Tags:** `[LATENCY]` `[WIZARD]` `[SAVE]` `[SCHEMA]` `[WS7-5c]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5c-tail finalize fix, June 1, 2026 — two options for the ~51s finalize-steps call at Save: (A) parallelize finalize per-meal (**shipped**), or (B) defer steps off the blocking path. A read-only confirmation pass (§27) established B is materially larger.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — A shipped instead (tidy, lower-risk); B logged as the deeper future win.
- **Why B is bigger (EVIDENCED):** the expanded-plan schema requires `steps` `.min(1)`; the materializer re-parses against it and writes one step row per step inside the `$transaction`. Naive deferral hits that gate — B requires EITHER loosening to `.min(0)` + skipping the step-write loop + a backfill at first cook-view, OR splitting materialize to persist the graph with placeholder steps and write real steps via a background worker. Both land a new **"plan exists but isn't cookable yet"** data-model state. Plus an UNVERIFIED secondary question: whether the cook-view tolerates a dish with zero step rows.
- **Payoff:** Save drops further (no finalize call on the blocking path), beyond the per-meal-parallel win that took finalize ~51s → ~17s wall-clock.
- **Owner:** **WS9** (or a dedicated WS7 sub-phase if Hans wants the deeper Save win before WS7-CLOSE). Not MVP-blocking — A made Save acceptable.

### D-WS7-077 — Build call (call #1) absolute latency vs PRD §5.4 — remaining fix levers

- **Tags:** `[LATENCY]` `[WIZARD]` `[BUILD]` `[FIRST-IMPRESSION]` `[WS7-5c]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5c-tail, June 1, 2026 — Hans flagged 3-candidate generation as slow (~25-30s) on a first-impression surface. A read-only investigation (§27) **MEASURED** the build call at ~24s flat for 5 weeks; the "5-10s a week ago" memory maps to a now-deleted legacy catalog-pick Build whose output was ~⅓-⅕ the size. **Latency tracks output tokens ~linearly across all Sonnet tool prompts in this DB.**
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — ONE lever shipped; the rest deferred.
- **Levers (MEASURED, ranked):**
  1. ✅ **DONE — cut dead `meals[]` field** from the candidate schema + prompt body. Zero consumers (grep-verified). ~150-300 output tokens → ~2-5s.
  2. **3→2 candidates** via the `wizard.candidate_count` SystemSetting (no-code flip, ~⅓ output drop, ~6-8s). **DECLINED by Hans** — keep 3 so the plan-choice UI still feels like a choice on the first-impression surface.
  3. **Streaming** — render the first candidate at ~8s while the rest stream. The REAL fix, but multi-day (SDK streaming + SSE route + incremental UI + partial-tool_use parser). **Parked** for WS9 alongside prompt-slimming; would also let the §5.4 "10-15 seconds" copy hold.
  4. **Sonnet→Haiku** — NOT recommended; Build's cross-candidate distinctness requirement is Sonnet's strength / Haiku's weak axis.
- **Interim handling (Hans's call):** set expectations via loading-state messaging (§1.8 "Kiwi is thinking…" / §5.4 reassurance copy) rather than forcing latency down now. PRD §5.4 copy redline queued for WS7-CLOSE.
- **Owner:** **WS9.** Not MVP-blocking.

### D-WS7-079 — Grocery list should refresh/reconcile when the plan changes after generation

- **Tags:** `[GROCERY]` `[PLAN-MUTATION]` `[RECONCILIATION]` `[WS7-5d]` `[WS7-7]`
- **Source:** WS7-5d Block 3 device test, June 2, 2026 — Hans generated a list, swapped a meal in the plan, reopened Groceries, list was STALE. A fresh generate rebuilds the list, but an existing list does not auto-refresh when the plan mutates.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — design resolved and foundation landed; the reconcile consumer (read-side delta computation) is **Block 4**, which closes this entry.
- **The right shape (Hans's framing):** the list should refresh and re-validate **incrementally** (reconcile only the delta), NOT regenerate from scratch. Ties to `bumpPlanRevision` — a list can track the plan `revisionId` it was generated against and reconcile when stale.
- **Why WS7-7:** that's grocery list mutations + Find Similar swap, where the incremental-update plumbing lives. **Arguably bigger than the rest of 5d combined; does not belong in a 5d bug-fix block.**
- **DESIGN RESOLVED + FOUNDATION LANDED (June 11, 2026 — WS7-7-A B1):** **Trigger:** on-read (mirrors PrepWeek's drift-detect), with a user-visible "updating your list to match plan changes" message on stale-detect (Block 5). **Result shape:** the complete consolidated plan-derived set for the meals CURRENTLY in the plan, minus extras, PLUS user-added + recurring items (**always preserved**). **Work shape:** delta-scoped — re-resolve only changed/added/removed meals; carry unchanged meals' resolved rows forward **WITHOUT re-calling AI gap-fill** (efficiency requirement). **Foundation:** an `isUserAdded` flag discriminates user-added Extras (never touched) from plan-derived rows, and a per-row multi-source provenance table means a shared ingredient (garlic from 3 meals) carries forward only if ALL its source meals are unchanged and re-resolves if ANY changed; AI-renamed/merged tail rows get zero sources → "always re-resolve" (conservative). **Check-state-through-edit preservation explicitly descoped → D-WS7-124 (WS9).** **§12.3.2 redline queued** (auto-reconcile-on-read + manual regenerate escape hatch replaces the "regenerate or use existing?" prompt).
- **Owner:** **WS7-7.**

### D-WS7-081 — LLMCallLog has no plan/draft-id linkage (forensic correlation is time-window-only)

- **Tags:** `[OBSERVABILITY]` `[LLM]` `[FORENSICS]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** D-WS7-080 DB probe, June 3, 2026. Resolving whether that repro was real data loss required attributing LLM calls to a specific wizard draft, but the log carries only `userId`, `promptKey`, `success`, `failureReason` — **no plan, draft or request id** — so attribution relied on `userId` + tight time-window clustering: conclusive there, **brittle for noisier traces** (concurrent users, overlapping runs, retries).
- **Proposed fix:** add a nullable correlation column (e.g. `entityId` / `requestId`) populated from the AI-call caller context, so forensic queries can join calls to the plan/draft they served.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN.
- **Owner:** **WS9 (observability / systemic).** Not near-term; surfaced because D-WS7 forensics has needed this twice. Revisit if it recurs a third time before WS9.

### D-WS7-082 — `saveWizardDraft` has the same long-AI-call timeout exposure as activate (+ Android timeout asymmetry context)

- **Tags:** `[WIZARD]` `[MOBILE]` `[TIMEOUT]` `[RELIABILITY]` `[WS9]`
- **Source:** WS7-5b-followup D-WS7-080 mobile fix, June 3, 2026. Two out-of-scope findings:
  1. **`saveWizardDraft` same exposure:** save runs the same finalize-steps fan-out as activate, so it carries the same ~35s-call-with-no-client-timeout exposure. NOT fixed in the activate block because save doesn't activate — it lacks the "perceives failure → re-runs wizard → displaces own active plan" consequence, so the blast radius is lower. A "save silently appeared to fail" report would be the same root cause and the same fix.
  2. **Android-vs-iOS timeout asymmetry (diagnostic context):** **Android OkHttp's ~10s default read timeout makes a client-side abort near-certain on a ~35s call; iOS NSURLSession's 60s default only catches the long tail.** This explains the "intermittent" framing and means **any long-AI-call mobile path is far more failure-prone on Android** — relevant when triaging future long-call reports and setting defaults for new AI-backed mobile calls.
- **Proposed fix:** apply the D-WS7-080 pattern (AbortSignal + client timeout longer than the server budget) to `saveWizardDraft`, and audit any other mobile call fronting a >~10s server AI call.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — logged proactively; no save-failure symptom reported yet.
- **Owner:** **WS9.** Promote if a save-appeared-to-fail report surfaces.

### D-WS7-136 — Global meal/dish edits don't propagate to already-generated grocery lists

So B4 reconcile-on-read never fires and existing lists stay stale. A fresh generate DOES reflect the edit.
- **Two coupled layers to close it:** (a) bump the revision on every plan whose items reference the edited meal (cross-plan); AND (b) in-place change detection for an unchanged meal id — the SAME signature mechanism reserved for D-WS7-134, since meal-id-granularity provenance can't otherwise detect a same-meal content change.

- **Interim mitigation (B5):** visible "list may not reflect recent meal edits — regenerate" hint. Converts silent staleness to visible staleness; cheap, no mechanism needed. Chosen because this affects the highest-priority path (signup → plan → grocery list).

### D-WS7-142 — Just-this-time override model is ingredient + title only; step edits don't persist — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 11, 2026): a step-duration edit must persist on either save choice**

- **Tags:** `[OPEN]` `[MEAL-EDITOR]` `[OVERRIDE]` `[COUPLED:D-WS7-141]`
- **Source:** WS7-7-A B5 follow-on, June 15, 2026 — surfaced in the steps round-trip trace for the D-WS7-141 fix.
- **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 11, 2026 — FALLBACK BUILDING (mobile, BUG-252), TARGET OWED.** Hans, verbatim: *"if a user adds or changes an ingredient they would know if that changes a step. I don't know why a user would have the need to change a recipe step duration once, so I don't know if that's a valid use case. but if they decide things cook better at a higher temperature for shorter or a lower temp for longer, or whatever else makes the meal better the user should be able to save the step duration. and the edit mode is the same regardless of an ingredient or step or duration. on save, the user gets prompted for 'this time, always, cancel.' the 'this time' save use case is aimed at someone subbing an allergen ingredient or other preference one week, or cooking 6 servings instead of 4 because they have guests one day. if it's easier to write to the template meal for step duration edits I am ok with doing that every time, but if we can just have them save in the meal editor and apply always or just this meal that's the target"* — **Fallback (building now):** on "Just this time" with step edits, the ingredient/title override saves as today and the step changes are written to the recipe through the "Apply always" path, with copy saying so. **Target (owed, its own block):** the override carries steps and EVERY reader of a plan item's steps merges them — Cook Mode, prep week, the plan's shown time (D-WS9-235: re-derive from the overridden steps). Surfaced again as BUG-252 on September 11. ✅ **Fallback BUILT `0a1d8d8` (September 11 evening; device-unproven).** ⚠️ **Still lost on either path: a dish ADDED in the editor and saved "Just this time" has no canonical dish to write to, so its steps go nowhere — pre-existing, part of the target.**
- **What it is (VERIFIED, §27):** the override builder emits ingredients + title only, the view-parser ignores steps, and the override read re-merges canonical steps. So **a step edit saved under "Just this time" does NOT persist**; "Apply always" DOES, via the template write. True before and after the D-WS7-141 fix. ⚠️ The ingredient-removal bug is addressed independently; this is a distinct axis.
- **Decision needed:** are per-instance step overrides in scope (extend the override schema, builder and parser to carry steps), or are step edits intentionally apply-always-only?
- **Disposition:** deferred at surfacing — folding it into the B5 follow-on would expand the override schema mid-fix.

### D-WS7-153 — Prep-week per-step checkbox persistence + per-meal prep state + plan-level rollup

- **Tags:** `[PREP-WEEK]` `[COOK-MODE]` `[SCHEMA]` `[PERSISTENCE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8a Block 3 commissioning + build, June 18, 2026 (Hans product direction; Phase 0 audit grounded the design).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN (in build at logging time). Owner: **WS7-8a Block 3** (server); the per-item `isPrepped` response-shape change is consumed by **8b**.
- **The problem:** prep-week steps live in a structure blob **overwritten wholesale** on regenerate, so checkbox/resume state can't live there — and steps had **no stable identity** (only a positional number, which shifts when meals are added or reordered).
- **The stable key (load-bearing Phase 0 finding):** `(phase, ingredientId)` — the engine groups by ingredient and phase-assignment is a pure function of the ingredient, so ingredient→phase is 1:1 and the key is unique-per-step and stable across regenerate. A single **`seasonings_dry#blend`** sentinel covers the collapsed dry-blend step (plan-singular per D-WS7-151).
- **Storage (build-it-right, §5):** side table `PrepStepCompletion { planId, stepKey, checkedAt }`, unique on (planId, stepKey), cascade-delete; row-presence = checked, uncheck = delete. **Chosen over a JSON column** for queryability (per-step checked-at analytics), concurrency-safety (no read-modify-write race), and declarative lifecycle. Plus a manual-override flag on the plan.
- **Per-meal prep state (derived, NOT stored):** a meal is prepped ⟺ every prep step attributed to it has a completion row. **Vacuous-prep ruling (Hans):** a meal with **zero** contributing prep steps rolls up as **prepped** — a no-prep meal is ready to cook, and zero-prep meals are NOT excluded from the denominator (a plan of all-easy meals must reach `prepped`).
- **Plan rollup + manual override:** `prepStatus` (`not_prepped`/`partial`/`prepped`) is **derived** while the manual flag is false — all prepped → `prepped`, some → `partial` ("Prepped (mostly) ✓"), none → `not_prepped`. **Manual override wins + pins:** a PATCH setting `prepStatus` (incl. end-of-session "Done") also sets the manual flag; an explicit un-mark/reset clears it, returning control to the derived rollup. The forward-only transition guard and prep-started event still gate manual transitions. ⚠️ **`partial` re-defined: per-meal mixed, NOT per-step** (PRD redline queued WS7-CLOSE).
- **Endpoints (new):** check / uncheck / read, auth + ownership-as-404, with **no** subscription check — checkbox/resume is free; the prep-week entitlement stays only on the AI-generation route.
- **Orphan-prune on regenerate:** delete completion rows whose step key isn't in the freshly assembled set — prune to the new set, NOT merge-forward blindly.
- **Cook-Mode surfacing (seam):** the cooking-sequence route is plan-agnostic (a meal lives in multiple plans) — ⚠️ threading a plan id in would be the wrong seam. Per-meal prepped state is surfaced on the **plan-scoped reads** Cook Mode launches from instead.
- **8b consumes (flag for 8a-CLOSE handoff):** (a) per-item `isPrepped` defaults the "did you prep this?" prompt; (b) the **mise-en-place recap** is built 8b-side from existing prep-step text filtered by meal attribution — NO new AI, NO new server field; (c) ⚠️ cook-step quantity/qualifier text ("2 cups diced") must NOT be stripped — it's the recovery path when a user marked prepped but missed a step; (d) prep-prompt copy is 8b UI copy.

### D-WS7-154 — Pre-existing: prep-week result validator throws on sub-4-phase input instead of returning `success:false`

- **Tags:** `[PREP-WEEK]` `[VALIDATION]` `[PRE-EXISTING]` `[TEST-RED]`
- **Source:** WS7-8a Block 3 Sub-block A, June 18, 2026 (CC surfaced during the B3 test run).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Owner: **TBD** (out of B3 scope). Candidate for a WS7-CLOSE validation sweep.
- **What it is:** the refinement loops the first four phases with no bound guard, so a result with fewer than 4 phases throws a TypeError instead of returning a clean `success:false`; the negative test is therefore red. ⚠️ **Pre-existing, VERIFIED — not introduced by B3:** CC stashed its B3 changes and re-ran; the test crashes identically on the pre-B3 HEAD.
- **Why deferred:** harmless in production — the assembly path only ever produces exactly 4 phases (empty phases still emitted), so sub-4-phase input never occurs at runtime. Purely validator robustness + the red negative test.
- **Fix when picked up:** add a length/bound guard before the phase loop. Re-greens the negative test.

### D-WS7-155 — `prepStatus` PATCH bumps the plan revision → extra prep-week regenerate (benign under stable keys)

- **Tags:** `[PREP-WEEK]` `[CACHE]` `[OBSERVATION]` `[PRE-EXISTING-BEHAVIOR]`
- **Source:** WS7-8a Block 3 build, June 18, 2026 (CC surfaced at audit; not a B3-introduced defect).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN. Owner: **TBD** — logged for tracking, not action; revisit only if regenerate cost becomes a concern.
- **What it is:** `prepStatus` counts as a changed field on the plan PATCH (pre-existing), so any write to it bumps the plan revision and stales the prep-week structure cache. B3 makes this fire more often because end-of-session "Done" is a `prepStatus` write.
- **Why benign under B3:** the stable-key design means completions survive a regenerate — orphan-prune keeps every step key still in the assembled set, and keys are position-independent. No data loss; cost is one extra (cheap) regenerate.
- **Why not fixed in B3:** narrowing the changed-field set changes shared plan-mutation semantics — out of B3's blast radius and riskier than the symptom (other consumers rely on revision drift detection). Benign-under-stable-keys means there is no functional bug; a note for future cost-tuning only.

### D-WS7-183 — Mixed blend step (make-ahead spice mix + at-cook dredge in one `isBlend` step) can't be cleanly demoted from prep

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[ASSEMBLY]` `[NARRATION]` `[AT-COOK-RULE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 4 prep-week aggregation fixes, CC Phase 0, July 1, 2026 (confirmed against the live tree; Hans ruled defer).
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner WS9 (promote to WS7 if fresh-data device-testing shows it actually occurring). Low.
- The engine collapses all `seasonings_dry` components on a dish into ONE `isBlend` step and `skipSuggested` is all-or-nothing per step. FIX 3's at-cook rule demotes a dredge/breading blend out of prep when a recipe step applies it <~20 min before cooking — reachable for a **single-dish** dredge. But when a blend collapses a genuine make-ahead spice mix and an at-cook dredge into one step, that step is half-prep / half-cook and can't be demoted as a unit without hiding the legitimate make-ahead prep.
- **Accepted behavior (Hans-ruled): leave the mixed blend in prep** — it may tell the user to dredge during prep. Judged rare: needs a spice-blend dish and a dredge dish sharing the collapse in the same plan-week.
- **Fix (if ever wanted):** an assembly carve-out (don't fold a demotable at-cook dredge into a shared blend step) OR per-component skip granularity. Deliberately NOT built — narration defaults **loud** (keep-in-prep when uncertain), so the mixed case lands on the accepted outcome without a carve-out. If FIX 3's wording can't keep single-dish demotion working without mis-demoting a mixed blend, CC stops and surfaces rather than silently under- or over-fixing.
- **Cross-ref:** the single-dish dredge case (the FIX-3 headline for items 1.3/1.5/1.7) is handled in wording, in scope this block.

### D-WS7-184 — Demoted prep steps: "omit + server-exclude" REVERSES the WS7-8a B3 "flag-don't-drop" ruling

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[SERVER]` `[ROLLUP]` `[REVERSAL]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 1 commissioning, July 2, 2026. Device-testing showed demoted steps rendering muted; Hans ruled omit-entirely, forcing the server-side reversal.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner **WS7-8b Block 2** (server rollup threading, not yet commissioned). The render-omit half + the narration demotion rule are Block 1.
- **What it reverses:** WS7-8a B3 ruled **"flag-don't-drop"** — demoted/skip-suggested steps stay in the required-set, flagged not removed. Now **REVERSED**: the AI-free server `isPrepped` derivation must **EXCLUDE** `skipSuggested` steps from the required-set entirely. **Reason (VERIFIED at CC Phase 0):** render-hiding demoted steps in the VM alone means their keys never get written (the "Done with phase" batch pulls keys from the VM), so any meal with a demoted step can never reach `isPrepped` and the Cook gate nags forever. **Omit-on-render REQUIRES server-exclude to be correct; the two are coupled.** The threading mechanism (persist `skipSuggested` per stepKey, read from cached structure, or reuse Block 1's demotion signal) is scoped in Block 2's Phase 0 hard-STOP.
- **⚠️ Guard:** a mixed blend (D-WS7-183, ruled keep-in-prep) must NOT be excluded from the required-set — it stays required because it stays prep. Block 2 Phase 0 confirms this.
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-013, BUG-015; D-WS7-183; D-WS7-185 (defines what "demoted" means).

### D-WS7-185 — Canonical demotion rule: combines-into-a-mix = KEEP; standalone-into-nothing = DEMOTE

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[NARRATION]` `[ASSEMBLY]` `[CANONICAL-RULE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 1 commissioning, July 2, 2026. Cross-ref BUG-014.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner **WS7-8b Block 1**. Becomes a locked behavioral rule at Block 1 close.
- **The rule (Hans-ruled):** a single-ingredient measure that combines **INTO** a marinade / sauce / dressing / seasoning blend = **KEEP** (stays prep); a **standalone** single measure combining into nothing (oil → pan) = **DEMOTE**. Hans's hard constraint: do not ask the user to pre-measure 2 tbsp oil days ahead of cooking.
- **Mechanism:** reads the new **`dishRole`** structural signal, threaded from the meal-dish link's role label through to the prep contribution (zero query change). `dishRole ∈ {sauce, topping, base}` → KEEP; a lone cooking-fat in a `main`/`side` dish that `relevantSteps` shows poured into a pan → DEMOTE; `relevantSteps` is the fallback when role is ambiguous. `dishRole` is the shared assembly-membership signal (serves this rule AND D-WS7-186's grouping); **NOT** `SAUCE_NAME_HINTS`.
- **⚠️ 183 guard:** `isBlend` steps are explicitly EXCLUDED from demotion — the "do not demote a mixed blend" carve-out stays dominant. Safe by construction (Phase 0 + dry-run verified).
- **Sub-mechanism (audit-surfaced, §3):** the **`blendSpiceDish?` code-owned field** is stamped on a grouped sauce step only when that dish's dry spices truly survive into the collapsed blend (3+ per-dish survivors); the mandatory linkage wording ("combine … with the [Special Sauce] spices from your seasoning blend") emits ONLY when the field is present, so it never points at spices that aren't there.
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-014; D-WS7-186 (shared signal + grouping); D-WS7-183 (mixed-blend guard).

- **Tags:** `[WEEK-PREP]` `[ASSEMBLY]` `[PRD-CANDIDATE]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b Block 1 commissioning, July 2, 2026. Cross-ref BUG-015.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN → owner **TBD** (PRD-candidate). Low, TBD-pending-usage.

Hans: 5b may be better UX "but that's still TBD based on actual usage."

### D-WS7-190 — `wantsLeftovers` deprecate-or-reuse (removed from UI, backend retained)

- **Tags:** `[PREFERENCES]` `[WIZARD]` `[UX]` `[SCHEMA-LATER]`
- **Source:** Hans ruling July 6, 2026 — an early-idea preference that doesn't meaningfully shape generation; pull it from the screen now, decide deprecate-vs-reuse later.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — **UI removal + neutralization DONE** (Cookbook Phase B, July 10, 2026). The field is **inert** and the reuse design is RULED; only the deprecate-vs-reuse call remains. Owner: post-launch / catalog-workstream commissioning. Not blocking.
- **Current state:** field kept in schema but **neutralized** — control removed from onboarding, Preferences and both wizard screens and dropped from their inputs and payloads, **schema default flipped `@default(true)` → `@default(false)`**. Servings math is exactly `householdSize` for every user. The prompt-body servings line was left **untouched** — it already produces the correct result when false, so no reseed was needed.
- **⚠️ Why the default had to flip:** with no UI control, leaving `@default(true)` would have **silently turned leftover-inflation ON for every new user** — the opposite of pulling the feature. Removing a toggle is not the same as neutralizing a field; both were required.
- **⚠️ Behavior note (unresolved, low-stakes):** PRD §5.7 says `servings = householdSize + (1-2 if leftovers)`, i.e. the published NUMBER inflates — but a device test with `wantsLeftovers: true` showed **4 servings for a household of 4**. Either the per-run value (D-WS7-035) defaulted it off at generation, or the servings line wasn't taking effect. **Not chased** — the field is inert, so it's moot for shipping. Flagged rather than asserted (§27).
- **Reuse design RULED (Hans, July 10, 2026) — if ever revived:** published **servings stays = `householdSize`** and **per-serving macros/math are unchanged**; the leftover intent is expressed by **scaling ingredient quantities up by 1-2 servings behind the scenes**. Hans: *"you're making 4 servings, the macros and math per serving doesn't change because it knows behind the scenes the user wants another serving or two left over, and the user just cooks more food than they need for 4."* **This REPLACES the PRD §5.7 contract**; redline queued if/when revived, not applied now. Better because it keeps the servings label honest and per-serving macros stable — inflating the number makes both lie.

### D-WS7-192 — USDA backfill whole-file abort on transient failure has no resume-from-offset

- **Tags:** `[USDA]` `[BACKFILL]` `[RESILIENCE]` `[SCALE-LATER]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b USDA arc Block 2, July 5–6, 2026; refined at BUG-028 close.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — low priority.
- On a *transient* USDA failure (429/5xx/network/timeout) the backfill aborts, keeps the partial CSV, and is re-runnable from the top — but with no resume-from-offset a failure at row 300 of 383 re-processes rows 1–299. BUG-028 removed the *deterministic-400* abort (now a per-row MISS), so one un-searchable name no longer kills the run; the transient abort stands and is the correct conservative choice — **don't record a transient blip as a false MISS.** Fine at 383 rows; only matters if the catalog grows large. **Fix if ever wanted:** resume-from-offset or checkpoint the last-processed ingredient.

### D-WS7-193 — Unit-normalization data-quality (`defaultUnit` + `DishIngredient.unit` free-text)

- **Tags:** `[DATA-QUALITY]` `[UNITS]` `[POST-LAUNCH]` `[PREREQ-FOR-DETERMINISTIC-MACROS]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b USDA arc; Hans ruling July 6, 2026.
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — **post-launch, low-priority. NOT MVP, NOT go-live.** Revisit ~10K users.
- `DishIngredient.unit` is free-text with ~33 distinct values including junk (`to_taste`, `large`, `"6 oz"`, ~24 empty-string units); `defaultUnit` is similarly un-normalized. This blocks any future *deterministic* (non-AI) gram-conversion layer, which needs clean units.
- **Why it's safe to defer (Hans ruling, VERIFIED-mechanism / device-confirmation-pending):** USDA grounding is **gram-bounded** — the AI still does the quantity→grams conversion and the per-100g value scales against *that*. So a per-100g outlier (cooking spray at 792 cal/100g) does **NOT** inflate a meal total unless the AI assigns a crazy gram weight, which is pre-existing behavior grounding didn't change — a can of PAM does not add 870 cal unless the AI thinks you're eating a can of PAM. **⚠️ Device-confirmation pending:** spot-check a spray/spice-heavy meal for a sane (single-digit-ish cal) contribution to move this from verified-mechanism to verified-in-practice (§27).
- **Fix if ever done:** normalize both fields to a canonical unit vocabulary + build the quantity→grams table. Prerequisite for D-WS7-194.

### D-WS7-194 — Deterministic ingredient-level macro computation (scale-phase cost optimization)

- **Tags:** `[USDA]` `[MACROS]` `[COST]` `[SCALE-LATER]` `[OPTIONAL]`
- **Source:** WS7-8b USDA arc, Ruling 1's deferred half, July 5, 2026. Hans verbatim: *"be sure this is a logged future phase at scale cost cutting optional item."*
- **Status:** 🟡 OPEN — **scale-phase, optional. Acceptable as-is until ~10K users** (Hans, July 6: *"$130/month at 1k users is entirely acceptable... probably not worth revisiting until more like 10k users"*).
- Dish macros are AI-estimated (Haiku), now USDA-*grounded* per-ingredient but still summed by the model. A fully *deterministic* computation (USDA per-100g × normalized grams, no AI call for the sum) would save ~$130–150/mo at 1K users — an accepted cost, only material at ~10K scale.
- **Prereq:** unit normalization + a quantity→grams layer (D-WS7-193). Can't go deterministic without clean units.
