### D-WS7-200 — Kiwi Community Cookbook: require the meal's Edit button to have been pressed before a URL-imported recipe can be shared publicly

- **Tags:** `[COOKBOOK]` `[IP-RISK]` `[SHARING]` `[v1-STOPGAP]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 10, 2026 (WS7-8b Block B1 close session).
- **The decision (two parts):** (1) **Naming ratified: "Kiwi Community Cookbook"** — "Community" signals **user-generated** content, setting the expectation that these recipes are not Kiwi-authored and reinforcing the legal posture: a community *sharing space*, not Kiwi *republishing* third-party content. (2) **The gate:** before publishing a **URL-imported** meal, the meal's **Edit button must have been pressed at least once**. **Track only that the button was pressed** — do NOT require or verify that an ingredient or step actually *changed*; a single boolean per meal, set on first press, unlocks sharing. Hans's reasoning: content diffs are expensive to build and police, while the button-press is cheap, adds friction and creates a paper trail — *"a little protection to say I tried to protect IP if the app scales rapidly while someone complains."*
- **⚠️ HONESTY NOTE — this is a FRICTION/PAPER-TRAIL gate, NOT meaningful IP protection. Logged explicitly so no future reader mistakes it for a solved problem.** A user can press Edit, change nothing, and publish a byte-identical copy of a copyrighted recipe. "We required an edit-button press" is **not** a defense that would withstand a serious content-creator complaint. **Both parties acknowledged it as thin at logging time.**
- **Status:** 🟢 **RULED as the v1 stopgap — knowingly accepted as weak.** Hans: ship the thin gate now as partial cover during early scaling, **then design a robust plan while evaluating the feature overall.** A conscious risk-acceptance, not a misunderstanding.
- **🔴 COMPANION OPEN ITEM (the real work, NOT resolved here):** a genuine IP posture still needs designing. Candidates, none decided: a **DMCA-style takedown process** (the industry-standard protection); **attribution / source-URL retention** surfaced on the shared recipe; **ToS** language placing publishing responsibility on the user; possibly **disallowing public sharing of URL-imported meals entirely**; real **change-detection** (diff vs. the imported original) if the button-press proves insufficient. **Owner:** Cookbook workstream — a **definition-track ruling**, no code commissioned here. The v1 gate implements whenever public sharing is built; the companion item wants its own decision session **before** the Cookbook opens to real users at any scale.
- **Cross-ref:** URL Import best-effort posture (WS6 6c-1, D-WS6-041, PRD §10.3.1 / §10.3.4 / §10.9) — this entry covers what happens to imported content *downstream* when a user republishes it.

### D-WS7-202 — WS7-11 (Favorites, Saves, Ratings): the post-cook feedback loop gets its own workstream, built on the WS9 design system

- **Owner:** **WS7-11** (new workstream). **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — RULED (scope + sequencing); definition work pending.** **Date:** July 13, 2026 (WS7-8b close).
- **Origin:** Hans — *"at the end of cooking a meal, there's no 'done' or real end to it. the user has to back out of cook mode."* Cook Mode's step list simply **ends**, so cooking a meal through and abandoning it halfway are, to the app, **the identical gesture**.
- **THE SEQUENCING RULING (Hans):** **pulled OUT of WS7-8b; deferred until AFTER the WS9 restyle** — the completion screen is **net-new** and WS9 restyles every screen, so building it now means **designing it twice**. **WS9 → WS7-11 → sharing-lite.**
- **THE SCOPE (four things that are really one — "what happens after you cook, and what the product learns from it"):** (1) **cook completion screen** (PRD §13.5.7 + §13.10.1); (2) **star rating (1–5)**, **needs a schema field**, mounted on the completion screen *and* **Meal Detail** (Hans: *"meal detail should have the rating option for a user to rate a meal at a later time… 'oh, I cooked this last week and it was great'"*); (3) **favorites**, **needs a surfacing decision**; (4) the **`timesCooked` / `lastCookedAt` write path**, adopting **D-WS7-111**'s dead columns.
- **RULING — Done is the only button.** §13.5.7 and §13.10.1 each specify *"two buttons"* and name **different pairs** ("Back to Plan" | "Done" vs. "Save updates" | "Skip"), so built verbatim the screen has **four buttons and two competing exits**. Hans ruled **one button, "Done," → routes to Meal Detail.** Stars save on tap; time/difficulty edits stage locally and commit on exit. **Touch nothing, tap Done → nothing is written — that *is* "Skip,"** so no Skip button. "Back to Plan" is dropped: Meal Detail already has a nav stack under it, and Cook Mode also launches from the **Library** with no `planId`, so it would be dead half the time. **⚠️ The back arrow must behave identically to Done** — otherwise a user sets 50 minutes, hits back, and it silently evaporates.
- **RULING — `timesCooked` increments on DONE, not on Cook-tap.** Tapping **Cook Now** only means *"I'm going to attempt this"* — the intent abandoned when the kid melts down at step 3. Counting on **launch** inflates the number with meals nobody ate and **corrupts the one thing you'd want it for** (*"show me my staples"*): a meal you started and bailed on is the **opposite** of a staple. **The completion screen is the write point.**
- **THE FAVORITES DISTINCTION (Hans's catch — the load-bearing insight):** three concepts, only two controls today. **Saved** = *"this is in my library"* — the **heart** (PRD §9.5: on a public card it is the **save-to-my-library** control), an **acquisition** gesture, **not a rating**. **Rated** = *"it was good"* — net-new stars, retrospective quality. **Favorite** = *"this is a staple; put it in front of me when I'm planning"* — **forward-looking intent**, neither of the other two.
  **Why stars CANNOT subsume favorites:** a **5-star** meal can be a once-a-year showpiece — great, not a staple; a **3-star** meal the kids will actually eat on a Tuesday is **exactly** a favorite. **Quality and reach-for-it-ness are uncorrelated.** Hans verbatim: *"this is a 4 star meal, but it's easy and my kids love it, save it as a favorite if I want to add to a plan because it's a staple meal."*
  **⚠️ Two chat-Claude errors corrected here, both by Hans (§3/§27 — recorded so they don't recur):** (a) framing heart-vs-stars as *"two rating mechanisms that collide"* and leaning toward **stars subsuming the heart** — **that would have deleted the save button**; the codebase disagreed with the framing. (b) then leaning toward stars subsuming **favorites** — wrong for the reason above (treating a rating as a proxy for intent).
  **⚠️ The PRD contradicts itself on the heart:** one section says *"No separate UserFavorite table needed"*, another refers to *"removes the favorite (UserFavorite record)."* One is stale. **Verify against running code, not the PRD, at WS7-11 Phase 0.**
- **THE OPEN QUESTION (definition work — NOT yet ruled):** **favorites must *do* something or they are decoration** — the value is in the planning loop. Candidates: a **Favorites filter/sort on My Meals**; **wizard bias** (seed/weight generation toward favorites — a **prompt-contract change**, not a UI change); **add-to-plan pickers** with favorites pinned to top. *A favorite toggle that visibly does nothing is worse than no toggle.* **Rule this before commissioning.**
- **PRD redline REQUIRED (§13.10.2 `[SCHEMA]` note is WRONG):** it claims *"No new fields required"* because it only contemplated `estimatedTimeMinutes` and `difficulty`, which already exist on `Meal`. **It forgot the stars** — there is nowhere on `Meal` to store a 1–5 rating. WS7-11 needs a **migration** (rating + favorite + cook-tracking, likely one).
- **⚠️ Fork-on-calibrate (do NOT miss this):** §13.10.2 requires that editing time/difficulty on a **curated/public** meal *"creates a user-owned copy if one doesn't exist"* and that *"the post-cook prompt also creates the user copy."* So **rating/calibrating an unsaved curated meal must FORK it.** The machinery **already exists** (**D-WS7-139** fork-on-acquire, gated on not-already-owned, wired at add-to-plan / use-template / meal-swap) — **reuse it, don't reinvent it.** This is the one part of WS7-11 that can **corrupt shared catalog data** if done wrong: never write a personal rating to a `userId: null` row.
- **Cross-ref:** **D-WS7-203** (thumbs ruling), **D-WS7-204** (D-WS7-111 dead columns), D-WS7-139, BUG-018, PRD §13.5.7 / §13.7 / §13.10. Named by Hans: **"Favorites, Saves, Ratings."**

### D-WS7-203 — Rule the sharing-lite thumbs (like/dislike) against the WS7-11 star rating BEFORE sharing ships
- **Owner:** WS7-11 (rule it) → sharing-lite / Cookbook Phase D (consumes it). **Status:** ⚠️ **SUPERSEDED by D-WS7-211** (stars only; thumbs retired). **Date:** July 13, 2026.
- **The collision is not heart-vs-stars — it is stars-vs-thumbs:** sharing-lite specs *"Dislike: thumbs-down, label 'Not for me.'"*; WS7-11 introduces 1–5 stars. Two quality signals on **different scales**, meeting on the Cookbook browse surface. Free to reconcile before sharing ships; after, it is a data migration on public content. **§27:** the thumbs were specced **before stars existed** — reconcilable, not a locked ruling.
- **chat-Claude's lean (NOT a ruling):** stars subsume the public thumbs. **BUT the dislike may have a second job** — feeding *"Not for me"* into recommendation suppression. **Check what the dislike actually feeds before ruling;** if it drives suppression it isn't redundant and can't simply be deleted.
- **Why WS7-11 sequences BEFORE sharing:** WS7-11 is the private half of the feedback loop (what a rating, a favorite and "I cooked this" mean against your own library); sharing exposes those primitives publicly. Build sharing first and you ship thumbs, then reconcile.
- **Notes:** naming LOCKED ("the Kiwi Cookbook," Hans, July 6, 2026); Phase D slotted **"with or after the WS9 restyle so it's built once in the new visual language."**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS7-211 (supersedes) · D-WS7-202 · D-WS7-200 · roadmap row 7 · PRD §9.5.

### D-WS7-204 — `Dish.timesCooked` / `lastUsedAt` dead columns get an owner: WS7-11's completion screen is their write point
- **Owner:** WS7-11. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — supersedes the WS9 targeting on **D-WS7-111**. **Date:** July 13, 2026.
- **State (DB-verified):** both columns are **dead — 0/337 rows written, ever.** That is why `last_cooked` is a **greyed-out sort**: the UI offers it, the data doesn't exist. What exists instead is `mealUseCount`, a **plan-link count** — **planning a meal and cooking it are not the same event.** PRD §13.7 specs `cook_mode_started` / `cook_mode_completed`; **neither is emitted, so nothing in the product knows a meal was cooked.**

- **Naming reconcile still owed:** `lastUsedAt` vs `lastCookedAt` — the column says *used*, the semantics say *cooked*. Rule at WS7-11 Phase 0.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS7-111 (its WS9 target superseded) · D-WS7-202 · PRD §13.7.

### D-WS7-206 — `saveMutationLimiter` is a module-global IP-keyed bucket: any new test file adding `POST /me/meals` cases will 429
- **Owner:** Test infra / any block touching `POST /me/meals`. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN (mitigated).** **Date:** July 13, 2026 (BUG-018 B1). **CC-flagged.**
- **The sharp edge:** a **module-global bucket keyed by IP + method + path** (no `keyFn`), **capacity 12**. The canonical save test was already at the ceiling; added POST cases pushed a downstream case into a 429. **Any future test file adding these cases hits the same shared bucket, and the failure surfaces as an unrelated-looking 429 in a different test.** Mitigated by a test-only store reset (`__clearRateLimitStoreForTests()` + `beforeEach`), zero runtime change.

- **Cross-ref:** BUG-018 B1.

### D-WS9-043 — Catalog SPINE: the harness generates against a curated target-dish LIST (top ~600 most-popular US non-breakfast meals), not a preference-profile spread — supersedes D-WS9-041's profile-as-variety-engine

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[STORE]` `[BLOCK-3]` `[HARNESS]` `[CATALOG]`
- **Source:** Block 3 1B pilot dry-run (July 18, 2026) — 12 attempted / 10 produced. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — ruled, unbuilt. **⚠️ ID note:** minted as -042, **renumbered to -043** on reconcile — the parallel definition track consumed -042 in the same window (live §29.2 collision).
- **The finding that forced it:** the dry-run produced **4 distinct dinners presented as 8** — every omnivore profile converged on **chicken thighs** across four cuisines. **The dedup key did not fail;** normalized-title worked, and the model regenerated the same dish under a cosmetically different name that legitimately passed. **"Different titles mean variety" does not hold** — convergence is the model reaching for the most-probable dish per cuisine when nothing tells it what to make. At that rate 600 calls buy ~60 real meals and 540 near-clones, and **no structural checklist catches it** (every duplicate passes protein-completeness, timings, ordering, the BUG-040 gate).
- **The reframe (Hans's — it dissolves rather than patches):** the harness is **not doing discovery**; the catalog should hold **the most-cooked dinners in the US.** With a target dish name as input **convergence is structurally impossible** — each call has a distinct target and **the dish-name list IS the variety mechanism.** Accepted as **brute-force over logic-creating.**
- **⚠️ GRANULARITY RULE (load-bearing — Hans's burger point):** the list is **dishes at variant granularity, not categories.** "Burger" is NOT one entry — **smash, pub/fancy and standard** are different meals with different ingredients, techniques and audiences; same for tacos, mac and cheese, chicken sandwiches, pizza. **Granularity decides whether 600 entries yields 600 real meals or ~300 plus ~300 collisions.**
- **Popularity-ranked, not taste-curated:** Saag Paneer isn't a bad meal, just not what most US households cook on a Tuesday; ranking handles that automatically. **Geography is a phase axis:** a future market seeds **its own list** — the harness is list-driven, so a new market is a new list, not new code.
- **THE RULING — LIST SOURCING = OPTION 3 (hybrid) WITH HANS'S EDITORIAL PASS.** AI-generate the ranked list in a one-time chunked pass with the granularity rule in the prompt, **spot-check the top slice against a real public source** (free recall drifts toward what food media *writes about* rather than what is *cooked*, plus tail duplicates like "Spaghetti Bolognese" / "Spaghetti with Meat Sauce"), **then Hans reviews and edits before freeze.** Rejected: pure AI-generate + review (thinner grounding); fully external-data-sourced (sourcing cost, paywall/scrape shape). The list becomes a **checked-in constant. Anti-padding rule: better ~450 genuinely distinct dishes, stated as such, than 600 padded with near-duplicates.**
- **What it supersedes in D-WS9-041:** the preference-profile spread as the **variety engine**, plus the two dry-run variety fixes (exclusion-list of generated titles; profile-axis widening) — **both unnecessary. STANDING:** direct meal-gen (not plan-harvest), the finalize-steps quality stage, dish-owned steps, BUG-040 pre-validation, the protein/entrée check, allergen stamping, cache discipline. **Preference profiles do not disappear** — they still parameterize *how* a dish is generated (servings, difficulty); they stop being the variety mechanism. **Cache impact: none** — the target dish name goes in the **volatile** block.
- **Also carried:** ⚠️ **`promptVersion: null` on every harness call** (keys live in the in-memory registry, not seeded per §7) — a **real telemetry gap at 600**; seed before the scale run. ⚠️ **Allergen false-positive:** a *vegan* bowl stamped `egg` — not blocking, we stamp rather than filter. ⚠️ **Near-duplicate dedup stays a backstop** — loosening it to fuzzy matching was rejected as the primary mechanism (**paying for generations you throw away is the expensive way to get variety**).
- **Pilot economics:** 10 meals / 22 AI calls, **73.2% cache hit, $0.0616/meal**; both prefixes cleared the Sonnet 4.6 2048-token floor as measured.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-041 (the harness shape this amends) · D-WS9-040 (this defect class is what its checklist *cannot* catch) · D-WS9-037 · arc scope §4 Block 3.

### D-WS9-045 — Multi-version catalog so one plan never contains two versions of the same dish (mechanism REVERSED — D-WS9-059; generation model SUPERSEDED — D-WS9-062)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[STORE]` `[CATALOG]` `[SCALE-RUN]` `[RETENTION]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 18, 2026, at the list review. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — the retention ruling stands; both mechanisms superseded.
- **The ruling:** generate a **primary version of the full list**, then **additional unique versions weighted by rank.** Hans's rationale is a **retention motion**: *"I liked the last one, I'm excited to try another Kiwi version"* / *"the last one was OK, maybe this one is better"* — and standouts are what people **share socially** (D-WS7-212).
- **⚠️ READ TIER BOUNDARIES FROM D-WS9-057, NOT HERE.** The original flat-3 (~$51) and first tiered tables are history; operative is 25 / 50 / 133 / 350 dishes at 6 / 5 / 3 / 1 versions with tier 3 widened to **76–208**. **Tiering is not in code, so a stale table is a live foot-gun.**

### D-WS9-049 — Post-Block-3 latency & cost batch: four fixes ruled from a read-only diagnostic; the fraction fix SPLIT OUT to its own block

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[PERF]` `[COST]` `[PREP-COOK]` `[WIZARD]`
- **Source:** Hans's post-Block-3 device test (July 19, 2026) + CC's read-only diagnostic against the live server log. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — ruled and scoped; build not commissioned.
- **The trigger (Hans):** a 3-meal plan with catalog hits *"took about the same amount of time"* as full live generation, and prep-the-week took *"almost a minute"* with only 3 meals.
- **⚠️ THE REFRAME — the store is not a plan-generation latency lever, and chat-Claude's first read was wrong twice.** Generation is **ONE compose call regardless of meal count** (VERIFIED); what scales per-meal is expand and finalize-steps, and expand is already at **68ms / 1,496ms** — D-WS9-038's direct bind working as designed — so **there was no remaining expand latency for the store to remove.** ⚠️ chat-Claude asserted the store shortlist was **absent** from the generate prompt: **FALSE** — the conclusion survives **for a different reason than stated.** ⚠️ chat-Claude also predicted the prompt was interleaved and needed a restructure: **FALSE** — the static rulebook is **contiguous and leading**, so caching is **parameter wiring, not a prompt rewrite.**
- **The four items (ruled; ordered by user-visible value):**
  1. **`prep.narrate_steps` input bloat — the headline.** 67s / $0.148 / **24,569 input tokens** for 3 meals. VERIFIED: the input repeats a dish's **full raw step prose across every prep step touching that dish** (~8× for a chili), and sends `totalQuantity`/`unit`/`forMeals` **while the prompt says verbatim "kept for reference only; IGNORE them." We are paying Sonnet to read fields we told it to ignore.** Fix = input-assembly trim.
  2. **`GET /plans/:id` at 1.6–2.3s** — the whole deterministic prep step-set is re-assembled **on every plan read** just to derive an `isPrepped` boolean, plus an **N+1 meal-detail compose in a per-item loop**; the two overlap, so **each meal graph is read twice per call** — on an endpoint refetched ~40× per prep session.
  3. **Prep-completion invalidation is over-broad** — each toggle invalidates **four key groups** in a `finally`, producing a 4× `/plans` + `/home` + `/plans/:id` cascade **per tap.** *(The batch "Done with phase" path already invalidates once — correct by contrast.)*
  4. **Wizard generate uncached** — wire the cached-prefix seam Block 3 built to the leading prefix.
- **⚠️ Caching is the WRONG fix for prep — this reordered the batch.** The narration output is **persisted server-side**, keyed on plan + revision, so a hit costs **no AI call at all**: the 67s is paid **once per plan revision, not per visit**, and under the 5-minute cache TTL a prompt cache would almost always be **cold. Trim the input; do not cache it.** chat-Claude's "67 seconds on a core loop" framing **overstated severity.**
- **⚠️ SPLIT RULING (Hans): the fraction fix does NOT ride in this batch.** Items 1–4 are mechanical; **BUG-042's fix edits the `finalize_steps` body — the same prompt the catalog harness uses** — so a mistake propagates into every catalog meal written afterward. It gets **its own tightly-gated block** (§10 replace-don't-layer, mandatory Phase 0 verbatim re-read) and **carries a hard deadline items 1–4 do not: it gates the scale run.**
- **Still open (do NOT close on the inference):** the **1,005ms aborted expand** — **NOT StrictMode** (CC grepped, zero matches, correctly refusing to repeat the c11–c13 misattribution); the controller aborts only on a 90s chain timeout or explicit cancel and **neither fits**, so the mechanism is **UNPROVEN.** Whether that abort **wasted AI spend** is **INFERRED** — CC did not read the route's disconnect handling; if wrong, every abort burns a full Sonnet expand. **Q4.1 arithmetic doesn't reconcile:** CC read ~40 PUTs as ~40 taps, but five complete within 70ms, which looks like the batch path CC says invalidates once. **Re-check during the build.**
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-042 · D-WS9-038 · D-WS9-019 · BUG-018 (CC correctly declined to force the deterministic analogy onto narration prose — genuine NL generation — while noting `skipSuggested` and `estimatedMinutes` are mostly computable) · D-WS9-047.

### D-WS9-050 — Macros are ungrounded because the estimator is never HANDED the USDA refs: fix = feed refs to both creation paths. ⚠️ Deterministic computation FALSIFIED by bake-off

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[MACROS]` `[USDA]` `[CATALOG]` `[SCALE-RUN]` `[RULED]`
- **Source:** Hans's device test (shawarma wrap ~1.3–1.5× high) → two read-only CC diagnostics, July 19, 2026. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — RULED; Phase 1 + 2 built.**
- **⚠️ FOUR HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED — do not re-investigate:** **NOT a wrong-food USDA join** (BUG-032's avocado→avocado-OIL pattern did not recur); **NOT a raw/cooked basis error on this meal** (though basis IS a real systematic hazard — D-WS9-051); **NOT the servings anchor** (per-serving macros are invariant under a servings change, by design); **⚠️ and NOT "the model ignores the refs" — chat-Claude's framing, and it was WRONG.** Hans's instinct (*"the AI is almost working better than the USDA refs"*) was **correct**; chat-Claude pushed back and should not have.
- **ROOT CAUSE (VERIFIED):** the estimator prompt is **designed** to consume `nutritionRefPer100g` + `resolvedGrams`, but **the creation paths never hand them over** — the wizard path passes only name/quantity/unit, and the **catalog path never calls the estimator at all.** **"Grounded in USDA" is false not because the model ignores refs, but because it is never given them on the paths that create meals** — and it still achieves ~14% mean error guessing in the dark.
- **⚠️ DETERMINISTIC COMPUTATION FALSIFIED — do NOT revisit without new evidence.** A 12-meal bake-off found deterministic **~2× WORSE: mean error 33% vs 14%**, winning **once in twelve.** Two failure modes the estimator smooths: **(A) dry/raw ref × as-served quantity → 1.4–2.7× overshoot** (chickpeas at *"mature seeds, raw"* 378 kcal/100g used as "1 can" ~139 drained); **(B) unmatched or unconvertible rows silently DROP → 0.1–0.7× undershoot** (one meal computed 800 → 97 kcal). **Better data does not fix it:** backfilling conversions onto dry-basis refs makes catalog macros *more confidently wrong*, and deterministic math cannot judge "a can of chickpeas isn't 1,500 calories" — the model can.
- **⚠️ CC recommended AGAINST the ruled architecture and was RIGHT (§3 ratified):** *"Hans's premise — compute from USDA refs and the number becomes truthful — is contradicted by the evidence for the dominant catalog pattern."* Only **30% of catalog rows** are deterministically resolvable, and the calorie drivers skew **into** the gap.
- **THE RULING (Hans, July 19, 2026):** **(1) feed the refs to the estimator on BOTH creation paths** (Hans ruled both; the estimator is Haiku, so live-path latency is acceptable) — the core fix that makes the product claim true; **(2) harvest USDA `foodPortions` → `conversionRef`** — ⚠️ **deterministic, no AI, data already fetched and discarded** (a record says "1 piece = 57g" where the model guessed ~156g — that *is* the shawarma overshoot); **(3) curate the top-25 unmatched ingredients** — **ordinary foods lost to naming variants** (`unsalted butter` vs `butter`), covering **67%** of catalog usage; **(4) recompute the 44 catalog meals** (skip the private wizard meals — disposable test data). **Plus two guards Hans asked for:** a **sanity range** on estimator output, and **stamping each macro grounded vs unmatched** so catalog quality is measurable rather than assumed.
- **Persistence surface (VERIFIED):** macros live in exactly two lock-step places — dish per-serving fields and their meal rollup — and **both must be updated together** or plan-view drifts from dish numbers.
- **⚠️ Caveat on the evidence:** the hand-check column is CC's culinary estimate (INFERRED) and the deterministic column used **favorable** default grams — a simulation of a *fully-backfilled* path, so **real deterministic-today is worse than shown.**
- **Secondary (do not conflate):** ten Foundation Foods pointers violate **D-WS7-201** (a **rule violation, not a macro error** — Foundation vs SR Legacy are near-identical for simple foods), plus two junk seed rows worth cleaning. Separately, **step text vs ingredient list is STATIC BY DESIGN** — at an anchor of 2 servings with the user at 4, the step's "¾ pound chicken" and the list's "1½ lb" are **both correct, visibly disagreeing.** A UX defect, not math, **unrelated to BUG-042**.
- **✅ PHASE 1 + 2 BUILT — what survives as decisions:**
  - Refs fed on both creation paths through one shared resolver shape, and **unmatched rows are still SENT (ungrounded but present)** — never dropped; the explicit guard against failure mode (B).
  - **⚠️ Catalog sequencing changed on contact with the code: there is no point in the catalog flow where refs exist** (resolution happens at persist time; USDA enrichment fires **async and unawaited** after). Ruling: **`generate_meal` → materialize → grounded recompute**, the recompute harness being the single source of catalog macros — **~$11 across the scale run**, noise against ~$68 for generation.
  - **✅ `Dish.macroGroundedPct Float?` — the semantics are the point: a WRITE-TIME fact, not a derived one.** A derived number **silently rewrites history** when refs improve, destroying the ability to audit which catalog meals were written blind. **Nullable is deliberate** and materialize **intentionally writes null** — null *is* the audit signal "written blind, awaiting recompute." Fork **copies** it; a user PATCH **clears** it.
  - **⚠️ G1 IS WEAKER THAN THIS RULING ASSUMED — the wrong-ref policy partly rested on it.** Chicken→butter flags, but **avocado→avocado-OIL does NOT**, nor does **this ruling's own "steak, 3g protein" example.** CC **declined to tighten** — a tighter threshold false-positives on legitimate keto dishes. **So flag-and-log is a coarse backstop for gross implausibility, NOT a wrong-ref detector;** the sensitive channels are the B1 caveat and grounding itself, with a dedicated audit judge (BUG-032's Opus sweep) the real instrument.
  - **✅ B1 wrong-ref clause (Hans): a wrong reference is a DATA DEFECT to be surfaced, not silently corrected** — a quietly "corrected" number hides the bad pointer, which then poisons grocery, the catalog and every future dish using that ingredient. **Permitted: state adjustment** (canned↔raw). **Forbidden: substitution. Fuzzy-case default: no change beyond a state adjustment, and flag in a caveat.**
  - **⚠️ C5 re-sequences the scale run: only 13 of 44 catalog meals are strongly grounded (≥80%), median 71%. P2 (foodPortions harvest) and P3 (curation) must land BEFORE the recompute is applied** — otherwise the write-time stamp freezes 44 meals at a grounding level we already know is about to improve.
  - **P3 curation was REBUILT after correctly failing** — a naive top-1 FDC search produced **kosher salt→"dill pickles"**; CC flagged it unusable rather than shipping it (§3 ratified) and rebuilt on the BUG-028 AI-judge pipeline. **Reframe that shrank the job: 17 of the top unmatched are ZERO-MACRO** — the macro-relevant set is **~12**.
  - **⚠️ DISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT (CC volunteered — §3 working):** the Phase 1 dry-run **WROTE data** — `ai_estimated` `conversionRef` rows via the grams-fallback, before a skip-write-back guard existed. **Verify those rows before P2's harvest runs** — a harvested USDA portion should win over an AI estimate.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-051 (✅ RESOLVED) · BUG-032 · D-WS7-201 (violated 10× catalog-wide) · BUG-031 / BUG-033 · D-WS9-045 · BUG-042.

### D-WS9-052 — Cooking-medium gap: frying oil is grounded at the quantity USED, not ABSORBED — and the estimator prompt actively FORBIDS the fix. Prompt clause now, structural later (Hans ruled (c))

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[MACROS]` `[USDA]` `[PROMPT]` `[SCALE-RUN-GATE]` `[VERIFY-THEN-ESCALATE]`
- **Source:** Stage 4 recompute dry-run of the 44 catalog meals, July 19, 2026. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — ruled, not built. ⚠️ Stage 4 is ON HOLD behind it.** *(Later probe-verified to fire — D-WS9-053.)*
- **The defect (VERIFIED):** Buttermilk Fried Chicken recomputed **930 → 1650 kcal/serving (+77%)** because **3 cups of frying oil → 654g → 5,781 kcal naive** is **88% of the dish's grounded calories.** The model counted half to two-thirds of the frying medium as consumed; realistic absorption is **~10–15%.**
- **⚠️ THE PROMPT ACTIVELY BLOCKS THE FIX — our own clause doing it.** The estimator says *"Correcting for STATE is the ONLY change you may make to a reference value."* That line (D-WS9-050 B1) exists to stop substitution and is **correct for that purpose** — but it also forbids the one legitimate adjustment here. **Over-restrictive, and this is the case that revealed it.**
- **Incidence (VERIFIED, all 44 scanned, false positives stripped honestly): exactly 1 of 44.** CC removed the false hits rather than inflating the count (water is 0 kcal; the "SALT" matches were un**salt**ed butter; the pizza's flour is dough; stir-fry oil IS consumed). **⚠️ But the mechanism will recur at scale** — fried, breaded and brined dishes. INFERRED for scale.
- **THE RULING (Hans, option (c) — both, sequenced):** **NOW, a prompt clause** permitting an **absorption/consumption adjustment** for cooking media (frying oil, dredging flour, discarded marinades, brines, greasing fat) — ⚠️ a **second exception** to "state is the only change," so **narrowly drawn: it applies where an ingredient demonstrably does not end up in the food, NOT as licence to discount quantities.** **LATER, only if the clause proves unreliable: structural handling** — mark cooking-medium ingredients at the data layer with a fixed absorption factor (~12%); deterministic and auditable, but it requires classifying an ingredient AS a frying medium, which the recipe text may not make explicit.
- **⚠️ VERIFICATION MECHANISM (why (c) is safe):** the recompute dry-run with sanity flags is the test — **if Buttermilk Fried Chicken comes back at ~1,050 instead of 1,650, the clause fired.**
- **⚠️ SEPARATE AND PRE-EXISTING — do NOT conflate:** Hard-Shell Tacos protein 83g and Chicken Noodle Soup carbs 165g are unrelated to grounding, with **no double-counting.** *(⚠️ D-WS9-053 later showed both were single-draw artifacts — that diagnosis is NOT SUPPORTED for these two meals.)*
- **⚠️ A PRIOR CLAIM WITHDRAWN (CC falsified its own Stage 4 call — §3 ratified):** Chicken Noodle Soup was flagged as *"the clearest dry-noodle basis miss." That was wrong.* Egg noodles are measured **by WEIGHT**, so dry-weight × dry-per-100g **is correct** — cooking adds water, not calories; same for rice measured dry. **So the +18–27% on rice meals is legitimate grounding of previously-undercounted dry starch. D-WS9-051 stays CLOSED.** *(§27 caveat: a meal measuring "cooked rice" or "canned beans" against a dry ref remains untested.)*
- **Apply posture (Hans ruled the cleaner sequence): add the clause → re-run → then apply everything.** A partial apply of the clean meals was declined: applying stamps `macroGroundedPct` **at write time**, so they would be stamped now and re-run anyway — **writing the stamp twice to gain a day is a bad trade.** Hold list: **Buttermilk Fried Chicken**; **review before trusting** Chicken Noodle Soup, Hard-Shell Tacos, Grilled Chicken Shawarma.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-050 (B1's "STATE is the ONLY change" is the line this amends) · D-WS9-051 (precedent; stays closed) · D-WS9-053 · D-WS9-045 · BUG-042.

### D-WS9-055 — Bone-in / whole-bird yield: the basis clause ALREADY corrects it (~75% thighs, ~55% whole bird) but SILENTLY — deterministic yield factors deferred, not needed now

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[MACROS]` `[USDA]` `[VERIFIED-NO-ACTION]` `[DEFERRED-FIX]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 20, 2026 — *"not all of the chicken is consumed in the first place (neck, back meat, wings, gizzards)… is the model calculating like an average 'chicken' from the full bird?"* — then CC's 5C audit. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN but LOW priority — no action required before the scale run.**
- **⚠️ THE CONCERN WAS LEGITIMATE AND THE REFS DO MISMATCH:** both affected ingredients point at **boneless** refs while the **recipes weigh the bone-in item.** A 3.5 lb whole chicken resolves to **1,588g** against a 215 kcal/100g boneless ref → **naive 3,413 kcal for the bird alone.**
- **✅ BUT THE EXISTING BASIS CLAUSE ALREADY CORRECTS IT — verified to the frying-oil standard.** Chicken Noodle Soup (2 lb bone-in thighs) fires **explicitly and reproducibly** — all 3 temp-0 runs **bit-identical at 505/serving**, with the verbatim caveat *"Chicken thighs: bone-in weight used; edible meat ~75% of total weight."* The whole chicken fires **implicitly**: naive ~1,868/serv → **~1,045**, matching the real ~55% edible yield. **Unlike the frying oil, bone-in needed no new clause.**
- **⚠️ TWO RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES (why this stays open):** (1) **it is SILENT on 2 of 3 dishes** — **an unstated correction cannot be audited** (no way to tell a yield factor from a lucky low guess); (2) **it wobbles** (1015/1075/1015) and so **contributes to the ±120 tail** in D-WS9-053.
- **Surface today is narrow (VERIFIED): only chicken** — whole chicken and bone-in skin-on thighs are the **only** inedible-mass ingredients in the 44; **no shell-on shrimp, mussels, whole fish or bone-in ham.** ⚠️ **The scale run will introduce all of those.**
- **THE DEFERRED FIX (ratified as deferred):** curated **edible-yield factors** (whole chicken ~0.55, bone-in thighs ~0.75) applied at grounding time — the same deterministic pattern as the density work. **Deferred because** it is a **new mechanism** (a yield multiplier, not a `conversionRef` field), the clause corrects acceptably, and only 3 ingredients are affected. **Revisit if** the ±120 tail proves intolerable, or when the scale run introduces shell-on/whole-fish items. **⚠️ For the Whole Chicken meal the servings fix dominates** — 2→4 halves the per-serving number regardless of bone accounting (D-WS9-056).
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-052 (same "recipe quantity ≠ consumed quantity" class, but that one needed a new clause and this did not) · D-WS9-051 · D-WS9-053 · D-WS9-056 · D-WS9-045.

### D-WS9-056 — servingsDefault is FIXED by profile, not model-chosen — but the model can size an INDIVISIBLE anchor into it. Deterministic protein-per-serving gate = a pre-seed requirement

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[STORE]` `[SCALE-RUN-GATE]` `[DETERMINISTIC-OVER-PROMPT]`
- **Source:** CC's 5B audit, July 20, 2026, prompted by Herb-Roasted Whole Chicken flagging at **1.75 lb raw protein per serving.** **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — ⚠️ the gate is a PRE-SEED requirement (a fourth added to D-WS9-054's three).** The one-row data fix is ratified and ready.
- **✅ THE RISK CHAT-CLAUDE FLAGGED DOES NOT EXIST.** The worry was that `store.generate_meal` picks `servingsDefault` freely, making every macro divided by a guessed number. **It does not** — store meals draw from **4 fixed profiles** (family-4, couple-2) and persist the profile's servings; the model is **given** servings and told *"~6 oz raw protein per serving."* VERIFIED.
- **⚠️ THE REAL RISK IS THE INVERSE, AND SHARPER:** the model sized an **indivisible anchor** — a whole roast chicken — into a **2-serving** profile, producing **1.75 lb raw protein per serving** and violating the instruction **it was given. The prompt line already exists and was ignored.**
- **THE RULING (Hans):** a **deterministic post-generation gate** in the seed harness — if raw protein per serving falls outside **~0.25–0.7 lb**, regenerate or bump servings. ⚠️ **Same reasoning as `dishFamily` and `cookingScheduler`: a rule the user can feel must not depend on the model remembering.** At 1,133 meals *"the prompt says so"* is demonstrably not enough — this meal is the proof.
- **The one-row data fix (ratified, ready): Herb-Roasted Whole Chicken `servingsDefault` 2 → 4**, ⚠️ **updating the 4 child dishes in lock-step**, then recomputing. A whole chicken serves ~4; this halves ~1,530/serv to ~765.
- **Audit results (VERIFIED):** the bulk of the 44 sit at a sensible **0.25–0.55 lb/serving.** Three flags, one real — **Herb-Roasted Whole Chicken**; **borderline Crispy Oven-Baked Chicken Thighs** (0.75 lb/serv raw, ~0.53 edible — **the flag is inflated by bone**, D-WS9-055, review-only); **false positive Homemade Pepperoni Pizza** (0.06 lb/serv), since a pizza is **cheese/carb-anchored, not protein-anchored** — ⚠️ **worth encoding so the gate does not fire on legitimately low-protein dish types.**
- **⚠️ §27:** the audit counts **weight-measured** proteins only; count/odd-unit meals ("8 each" thighs, "2 (6 oz)" salmon) showed protein 0 and were spot-checked as plausible. **The gate must handle count-measured proteins or it will miss them.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-054 (the gate list this ADDS to) · D-WS9-055 · D-WS9-045 / BUG-018 (deterministic-over-prompt precedent) · D-WS9-040.

### D-WS9-058 — A meal has no consolidated ingredients list anywhere in the app: add a display-only "View Ingredients" modal + entry buttons on meal cards

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[RESTYLE]` `[MEAL-DETAIL]` `[PLAN-DETAILS]` `[SHOPPING]` `[GAP]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 20, 2026, backlog pass. **Status:** 🟡 **IN BUILD — grocery block C (September 29, 2026), as BUG-331's fix, pre-go-live (Hans); ships in 1.1.** Build shape on D-WS9-285 / BUG-331: comparable units summed, incomparable stay separate lines; scaled to the displayed servings.
- **⚠️ THE GAP:** there is **no way to view a meal's complete set of ingredients** — the quintessential *"Ingredients"* block at the top of every recipe on earth. Kiwi's ingredients live **per dish**, so a meal with a main, base and side scatters them across three places. ⚠️ **Concrete and in-store:** a user in a grocery aisle has no single list, and **an ingredient used across multiple dishes is easy to miss entirely.**
- **The ruling (Hans's shape, accepted):** a **modal** with the meal's **complete consolidated list, deduplicated across dishes**; **display-only** — ⚠️ **not written to the server unless a reason emerges**; a **"View Ingredients" button** on the meal card in **Plan Details** and in the **meals list views**; tapping it opens **meal detail anchored to the ingredients area with the modal expanded**, not a bare modal over the list — **the user lands where the information lives.**
- **Why display-only:** consolidation is a pure view-layer concern over per-dish persisted data; persisting a second copy creates a synchronization surface (servings scaling, ingredient edits, dish swaps) for zero benefit. ⚠️ **If a reason to persist appears — offline access, or a shopping-list divergence — that is a separate ruling, not a quiet upgrade.**
- **Open at build (not blockers):** the **same ingredient at different quantities across dishes** (summing is almost certainly right for a shopping read); and whether the list reflects **scaled** or authored servings (**D-WS7-214**, same seam).
- 🔴 **September 29, 2026 — BUG-331 (Hans, PRE-GO-LIVE):** the meal-detail "Ingredients" label above "Adjust for servings" is hard to see and its tap does nothing, though it is meant to expand. It may be THIS feature's half-built entry; grocery block C's read answers which, and if so it builds this ruling (consolidated, deduplicated, display-only, at the displayed servings), not a new design.
- **Cross-ref:** BUG-331 · D-WS7-214 · D-WS9-050 (step text doesn't scale — third member of this cluster) · `kiwi_ws9_screen_plan.md`.

### D-WS7-214 — Scaled recipes can outgrow their bakeware: flag scaled meals rather than computing pan sizes — 🟡 LOGIC SHIPPED, advisory-wiring pending → WS9 restyle

- **Tags:** `[WS7]` `[POST-LAUNCH]` `[COOKING]` `[SCALING]` `[TRUST]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 20, 2026, backlog pass. **Status:** 🟡 **LOGIC SHIPPED (July 25, 2026), advisory-wiring pending → WS9 restyle.** The reusable "this meal was scaled" predicate and honest advisory copy landed in the servings unification — an honest *"double-check your pan/dish size"*, **never a computed pan size.** What remains is **wiring a visible advisory banner** onto the meal/cook surfaces. **Not a launch blocker.**
- **The problem:** when a recipe is **scaled**, the **bakeware named in the steps goes out of sync with the volume of food** — doubling a casserole does not let it keep fitting the same 9×13, while the step text keeps naming the authored vessel. ⚠️ **A cooking failure the user discovers mid-recipe, with the food already mixed.**
- **⚠️ THE RULING (Hans, provisional): do NOT compute vessel sizes.** Add an **advisory marker** when a meal has been **scaled in servings.** Hans: *"I'd rather [not do] math and logic to determine if they need a 9x12 at 5 servings — but I'm open to doing that if it's easy."*
- **Why the flag beats the computation:** vessel selection is a **volume-and-depth** problem depending on the dish (a lasagna and a sheet-pan dinner scale on different axes), on what the user owns, and on the fact that **doubling often means two vessels rather than one bigger one. Getting it subtly wrong is worse than saying nothing** — a confidently wrong pan size is a trust failure; an honest advisory is not.
- **The case for revisiting:** detection is free (`servingsDefault ≠ authoredServingsDefault`, both persisted per BUG-003). If a **coarse** mapping proves tractable (≥1.5× on a baked dish → *"use a larger dish or divide between two"*), that beats an asterisk. ⚠️ **Scope it at build; do not assume it is hard without checking.**
- **⚠️ Probably one cluster with D-WS9-050**, which records that **step text does not scale with servings** — a scaled meal shows correct scaled quantities beside step text quoting authored amounts, *"both numbers correct, visibly disagreeing." Same defect class: authored-time detail surviving into a scaled context. Worth ruling together.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-050 · D-WS9-058 · BUG-003.

### D-WS7-215 — Component selection is NON-DESTRUCTIVE and reversible, per-user and per-plan: `Dish.componentSelections` + `MealPlanItem.componentSelections` ✅ SHIPPED (Block 3.7) — **ENTRY RECOVERED July 27, 2026**

- **⚠️ RECOVERED, NOT WRITTEN AT DECISION TIME — the recovery mechanism is the lesson.** The ID was handed to CC as next-available, CC consumed it across **six code sites**, and **no log entry was ever written.** Every pointer update kept reading *"D-WS7-215 next"* — correctly, because heading-grep found no heading. Surfaced only when CC refused a handed-forward D-WS7-215 as already live in code. **Content below is reconstructed verbatim from the artifact's own code comments**, not from chat memory (§26.3).
- **⚠️ THE FAILURE MODE IS THE INVERSE OF THE JULY 23 ONE, AND THE STANDING GUARD CANNOT CATCH IT.** That was *entries exist, pointer stale* — heading-grep catches it. This is *ID consumed in code, entry never written* — **invisible to heading-grep by construction, because there is no heading to find.** **Guard: when a CC prompt hands an ID forward, the block close must confirm the entry EXISTS (`grep -c "^### D-WS7-NNN"`), not merely that the pointer moved.**
- **THE DECISION (verbatim from the schema comment):** per-user component selection is a **NON-DESTRUCTIVE map** `{ [componentKey]: 'scratch' | 'bought' }` on the user's own (forked) `Dish`. **"Forever" is a stored selection, NEVER a rewrite of the step rows** — *"a user who buys coleslaw mix in December can still shred cabbage in July by flipping it back."* Absent key = the component's default (scratch). **Per-plan overrides per-user:** `MealPlanItem.componentSelections` is a *"this week only"* map scoped to one plan instance; absent = fall back to the user/dish default. Both NULLABLE + reversible.
- **⚠️ Fork discipline is load-bearing and fails SILENTLY:** the component registry **and** the per-user selection must survive the fork alongside substitutions, *"or a dual-path meal loses the label/order metadata (registry) or the user's saved 'make this easier' choice (selections) on acquire."* Same **DbNull** rule — a null `Json?` column must be passed as `Prisma.DbNull` so it stays SQL NULL rather than a literal JSON null (which Prisma rejects). **Any new `Json?` column needs an explicit fork line or it vanishes on acquire.**
- **Migration additive and catalog-safe:** all columns NULLABLE, so *"every existing row is BASE / unselected"* and the catalog stayed valid untouched.
- **⚠️ MIGRATION-ONLY AT BLOCK 3.7 — "Nothing reads it yet"** appears in both column comments. **No consumer is wired**; the reading surface (a "make this easier" control on meal detail, prep/grocery honoring the selection) is **unbuilt and unscheduled.**
- **Owner:** WS7 (data model). **Paired with D-WS9-066**; this is the persistence/reversibility half.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-066 · D-WS9-064 (same fork-discipline trap) · D-WS9-067 · D-WS9-068 · D-WS9-069.

### D-WS9-059 — Same-dish exclusion is a model JUDGMENT via a prompt instruction, NOT a `dishFamilyKey` mechanism — the key approach is abandoned after three failed attempts (amends D-WS9-045)

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[WS-GEN]` `[CATALOG]` `[PROMPT]` `[AMENDMENT]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 20, 2026. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN** — mechanism ruled; the prompt instruction is an unbuilt gated edit, batched with D-WS9-060. ⚠️ **Supersedes the structural-mechanism half of D-WS9-045**, whose constraint (never two versions of one dish in a plan) **stands** — only the mechanism changes.
- **Why the key failed — three attempts, all dead (§27):** **(1) slug-of-title:** 0 of 12 write-back rows landed on an existing key; four were unmistakably the same catalog dish that slug *differently* because the generated title carries an appliance/method prefix. **(2) thread-an-existing-value:** falsified at Phase 0 — the catalog anchor exists on store **hits** (which fork private and never write back) and is **absent on misses** (the only thing that writes back). **Identity exists exactly where it isn't needed and is absent exactly where it is.** **(3) a normalizer:** reverse-engineering a canonical family from prose, which attempt 1 already proved unreliable.
- **⚠️ THE REAL REASON THE KEY IS THE WRONG OBJECT: same-dish detection is a semantic judgment, not a rule.** A feature rule (*same protein + base + veg*) mis-groups — chicken fajitas and chicken enchiladas satisfy it and are *different* dinners — while missing real duplicates a model catches instantly (Butter Chicken vs. Instant-Pot Butter Chicken; Fajitas vs. Fajita Bowls vs. Burrito Bowls). **No deterministic key separates those; a model reading the titles does.**
- **⚠️ WHY THIS DOESN'T BREAK THE deterministic-over-prompt PRECEDENT.** `dishFamily`-original, `cookingScheduler` and the protein-anchor case were made deterministic because the prompt was insufficient — but those are **numeric** problems (a whole chicken produced 1.75 lb against a "~6 oz" line), where models are weak and arithmetic is exact. **This is semantic similarity, where models are strong and rules are brittle. Opposite problem, opposite answer.** On the record so this reads as a distinction, not a reversal of principle.
- **✅ THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY SUPPORTS THE PROMPT APPROACH (verified, Phase 0):** plan composition is **single-shot** — the model returns the whole plan in one call, so it **already sees all its own picks**, and the shelf shortlist too. -045's premise that *"the model needs to see what's in the plan"* is satisfied by the existing structure: no restructure, no schema change, just a `generate`-body instruction to judge same-dish and not stack variants — **covering the shelf-duplicate edge for free.**
- **⚠️ MUTUAL EXCLUSION WAS NEVER SHIPPED — the whole key effort was premature.** The **only** reader of `dishFamilyKey` is the harness's own re-run dedup; the compose path has **zero** matches. The **12 null write-back keys are inert, not a live defect** (correctly NOT purged / NOT backfilled). **The prompt instruction is the FIRST enforcement, not a fix to a broken mechanism.** `dishFamilyKey` keeps value for the harness's dedup and analytics only.
- **Build home:** the `wizard.candidate.generate` body (the **LIVE plan path — NOT the harness's `finalize_steps`**), a gated §10 replace-don't-layer edit batched with **D-WS9-060**. Verify with a real `count_tokens` if it lands in a cached prefix.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-045 (amended) · D-WS9-060 (batched, same body) · D-WS9-043.

### D-WS9-060 — Ground meal & recipe generation in named standard references (Joy of Cooking + 1–2 modern sources); the model does NOT web-search

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[CATALOG]` `[WS-GEN]` `[PROMPT]` `[QUALITY]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 20, 2026, backlog pass. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — ruled in shape; mechanism-of-reference to be finalized before the next harness run.** A gated `generate`-body edit; batch with D-WS9-059.
- **Hans's intent:** draw on the **standard, well-worn corpus of how popular dishes are actually cooked** — Joy of Cooking as the *"bible… not always amazing, usually not bad, gets the job done"* baseline plus **one or two more recent references.** He is explicit he does **not** intend to reproduce copyrighted recipes — the point is the **commonality** across recipes (shared technique and ratios), not any source's unique expression.
- **⚠️ CRITICAL FINDING — the model does NOT web-search.** Generation is a single Sonnet call with a tool schema and **no web-search tool on that path** (confirm at build). So *"use popular web results"* language retrieves **nothing** — it only nudges the model to *sound like* web recipes. That training knowledge **largely is** Joy of Cooking plus the popular internet corpus, so the instruction isn't useless, but **it steers the model's own knowledge; it fetches nothing.**
- **⚠️ MECHANISM CAUTION for the build:** models are **unreliable at reproducing specific cookbook content** and will confidently attribute invented text to a named book — risking fabricated specifics presented as authoritative, plus a copyright dimension. **Better to describe the CHARACTER Hans is after** — reliable, standard, technique-first, the version that always works, the shared ratios a dish is known by — **rather than instructing retrieval-by-title. The named references become calibration for a style of cooking, not sources to quote.**
- **Open at build:** which 1–2 modern references (Hans to name, weighted by reach); whether there is genuinely no web-search tool and, if there is, whether enabling it is desirable (a much larger change); exact phrasing under the character-not-retrieval framing.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-059 (batched) · D-WS9-061 · D-WS9-043 · D-WS9-040.

### D-WS9-061 — Version variety lives in the ACCOMPANIMENT, not the canonical dish: don't make the harness "think too hard" and wreck well-worn base recipes

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[ARC]` `[CATALOG]` `[WS-GEN]` `[QUALITY]` `[SCALE-RUN]`
- **Source:** Hans, July 20, 2026, backlog pass. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — ruled in principle; confirm at the ~50-meal checkpoint.** ⚠️ **Demoted by D-WS9-062** to a per-row honesty nudge — the expanded pre-named list now carries the variation, and this becomes the editorial judgment applied when authoring it.
- **The problem:** told to make 5–6 versions of a popular dish *different*, the model moves the canonical ratios or substitutes — and **every departure makes a worse meal.** Hans: *"Quiche Lorraine is Quiche Lorraine. Chicken Piccata, largely, at the end of the day is still lemon juice, stock/wine, butter, and capers."*
- **⚠️ THE RULING — variation belongs at the MEAL-COMPOSITION level, not inside the canonical dish.** Seven piccata *meals* differing by **accompaniment** — broccoli, an arugula side salad, orzo, roasted potatoes — are seven genuinely different dinners with the **base recipe intact.** This axis **cannot produce a bad meal**, because the canonical dish never moves. *"Adding broccoli or a side arugula salad is a good way to add variety without messing with standard ingredient ratios in a meal with a well-worn base recipe."*
- **⚠️ IMPLICATION FOR THE TIER TABLE (flagged, not ruled):** depth should probably vary by **how much latitude a dish has**, not rank alone — Quiche Lorraine has one correct form and maybe three sensible accompaniments; a burger or stir-fry has real latitude. The tiers give the top 25 six versions regardless. **The ~50-meal checkpoint is where to see whether forced high version counts on low-latitude dishes degrade. Watch for it there.**
- **Likely phrasing direction:** *hold the canonical dish and its ratios fixed; express versions through accompaniment and presentation, not by altering the base recipe.*
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-057 (the table this pressures) · D-WS9-045 · D-WS9-060 · D-WS9-043 (smash/pub/classic are 3 *entries*; this is versions *within* one entry) · D-WS9-054 · D-WS9-062.

### D-WS9-063 — Decouple the store-fill prompt family from the wizard prompt family before the first post-launch catalog refresh (RULED July 23, 2026)

**Context.** One shared preference-contract preamble is prepended to BOTH the store-fill generate and finalize calls. Authored in the wizard era, it carried wizard-only language — "VARIETY WITHIN THE PROFILE… fits the profile's cuisine" and "If the profile is vegetarian or vegan." For store-fill none of that is real: the gen profile carries only `{key, servings, difficulty}` and cuisine/diet/protein are inferred from the pre-named target row. **The model was reading, in one system prompt, *infer cuisine and diet from the name* AND *fit the profile's cuisine and diet* — the second referring to parameters that do not exist in the call.**

**RULING.** For the seed run the wizard-era language is REMOVED from the shared preamble in place (Block 3.6) — acceptable NOW because the wizard-live path does not exercise the store-fill prefixes. Finalize was verified after the edit, its load-bearing guidance (step timings/phases, quantities-are-source-of-truth) preserved verbatim, prefix 3,162 → 2,947 tok, still clear of the 2,048 floor and still caching.

**DEFERRED.** Before the first post-launch catalog refresh the two prompt families need genuinely separate prefixes. **Editing a shared prefix to suit one caller works until the other caller's needs diverge, and the failure is silent.**
- **Owner:** WS9A / catalog refresh · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-064 · Block 3.6.

### D-WS9-066 — Swappable components: per-component dual-path recipes, non-destructive selection (RULED July 23, 2026 · ✅ SHIPPED)

**The product behavior.** A user reviewing a meal sees the full from-scratch recipe and may decide, **per dish**, to take the shortcut — saved **this week only** or **forever**. *"The recipe updates from the full recipe to the shortcut buy-the-product recipe."* **The cooking changes, not just the shopping list.**

**⚠️ GRANULARITY IS SUB-DISH.** Hans: *"buy the coleslaw mix, but make your own dressing. Or shred the cabbage and use your favorite dressing."* Two independently swappable components = **four valid states for one dish. A per-dish boolean cannot express this.**

**⚠️ "FOREVER" IS NON-DESTRUCTIVE.** A reversible *selection* on the user's forked dish, **never a rewrite of step rows** — someone who buys coleslaw mix in December must be able to shred cabbage in July. Per-plan (`MealPlanItem`) overrides per-user (`Dish`); both nullable, both reversible.

**Schema — shape (B).** `componentKey String?` + `pathKey String?` (`'scratch'`|`'bought'`) on BOTH `RecipeInstructionStep` and `DishIngredient`; `componentRegistry Json?` on `Dish`, **kept SEPARATE from `substitutions`** (whose mutating sanitize pass would otherwise have registry metadata in its blast radius). **Null `componentKey` = base = always present** — which is what keeps existing catalog meals valid untouched. Rejected: (A) a first-class `DishComponent` table (heaviest); (C) bought steps inside the substitutions blob — they would sit outside `RecipeInstructionStep`, forcing every consumer to splice them in and re-derive amount refs, with brittle step-index attribution.

**Why (B) is cheap downstream.** `cookingScheduler` is a pure function of each step's phase type, timing-sensitivity and estimated minutes, and only sees the rows that exist. Bagged coleslaw genuinely having no shredding step makes both the attended-step serialization and the anchor fall out correctly with **no scheduler change** — provided each path carries honest metadata. **This is why display-time name-matching was rejected: changing the step rows is the only lever on the schedule.**

**The plumbing was already there.** Finalize ALREADY received `substitutions` and ignored them — the prompt never mentioned them. **"Make dead data live," not greenfield.**

**MEASURED (25-meal write-free sample, $1.458).** 34/34 substitution-carrying dishes got a bought path; 43 components, 8 dishes with 2+; **zero tag-validation findings.** Four-state check on "Creamy Ranch Slaw": all four coherent, base steps path-agnostic ("the dressing"/"the slaw base"), timing honest at 36/33/27/24 min, salt/pepper correctly confined to the scratch-dressing path since bottled ranch is pre-seasoned.
- **Owner:** WS9 (schema + authoring) → WS9A (toggle UI) · **Status:** ✅ SHIPPED · **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-064 · D-WS9-067 · D-WS9-068 · D-WS9-069 · D-WS7-215 · Block 3.7.

### D-WS9-067 — Grocery list must consume `Dish.substitutions` and per-component selections (RULED July 23, 2026)

The grocery list reads `DishIngredient` and overrides only; **it ignores `substitutions` entirely.** When a user selects the bought path, the list must **drop that component's scratch ingredients** (the `replaces[]` names) and **add the product** with its quantity and unit.

**⚠️ PREREQUISITE — an ingredient-tagging pass that does not yet exist.** `DishIngredient.componentKey/pathKey` were added in Block 3.7 but **left null**: finalize authors steps, not ingredients. Until ingredients carry component tags the grocery list cannot resolve which rows belong to which path. That tagging — a finalize extension or a separate pass — **is this deferral's first task.**

**Aggregation hazard:** the list aggregates across meals, so if one meal takes scratch and another bought for the same component, **the merge must not double-count or cancel out.**
- **Owner:** WS9A · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-064 · D-WS9-066 · D-WS9-068.

### D-WS9-068 — Prep-week narration and the prep-combine engine must resolve the effective step set (RULED July 23, 2026)

Two prep surfaces read from the from-scratch world and would be wrong for a user on a bought path: prep-week aggregation reads raw step text and would narrate *"shred the cabbage and grate the carrot"* to someone who bought the bag; the prep-combine engine is ingredient-driven and hits it from the other side, combining prep work for ingredients the user is not buying. Both need the same resolution the meal-detail and sequencer paths get. **Prep is where the dual-path feature is most visible to a user planning a week, so an unresolved prep surface would undercut the feature's whole point.**
- **Owner:** WS9A · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN · **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-066 · D-WS9-067.

### D-WS9-069 — Mixed component states must be verified on every catalog generation, not assumed (RULED July 23, 2026 · ✅ first verification PASSED)

A dish with two swappable components has four valid states, and **the mixed ones are where correctness breaks.** Hans: *"we don't want a user who wants to cut cabbage and use slaw dressing to be told to open the shredded slaw bag and start mixing the dressing."*

**Accuracy trumps cost and latency here.** The finalize prompt *asserts* every combination is cookable; **assertion is not verification.** Coverage counts can look perfect while mixed states are incoherent — **the two measure different things.**

**⚠️ THE SPECIFIC DEFECT TO LOOK FOR IS A BASE STEP THAT ASSUMES A PATH.** Base steps run in ALL four states, so one reading "toss the *shredded* cabbage with the *whisked* dressing" breaks both mixed states while leaving both pure paths looking fine. **Neither a scratch-only nor a bought-only read would catch it.**

**RULING.** The four-state reconstruction is a **standing exit criterion** for any catalog generation or regeneration — sample K≥3 two-component dishes across rank bands, print all four effective step sets in cook order, and confirm each is coherent, path-agnostic in its base steps, internally non-contradictory and honestly timed. **It costs no API calls.** **First verification PASSED** (Block 3.7, "Creamy Ranch Slaw" — see D-WS9-066).
- **Owner:** WS9 (standing criterion) · **Status:** 🟡 OPEN as a recurring gate · **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-066 · Block 3.7 · Block 3.8 exit criteria.

### D-WS9-071 — Fractional countable ingredients (1.5 eggs, 0.5 tortillas): DEFERRED post-go-live as a display-rounding rule, not a data change
- **Owner:** post-go-live polish. **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — deliberately deferred** (definition track, July 23, 2026). Split off from D-WS9-070.
- **The question (Hans):** *"I don't think I ever thought of or covered 1.5 eggs. is that the only unsplittable ingredient?"* **Answer: no, but the set is small and tolerable** — the pattern is **countable discrete units** (eggs, garlic cloves, whole citrus, tortillas, buns, corn cobs, chicken breasts, cans), **counted rather than measured. ⚠️ It bites when scaling DOWN, not up:** 1.5 eggs reads odd but a person handles it; **0.4 eggs or 0.5 tortillas start looking broken.**
- **RULED — defer, and do NOT gate servings on divisibility.** Hans: *"I don't want to gate recipe servings because they need to use a full egg. and I guess it could be up to the user if they want to try using part of an egg."*
- **The cheap mitigation when it matters — display-only, no data change:** round countables to **fractions (halves), never decimals**, and never display 0.4 of anything. **Because it is a rendering rule, deferring costs nothing structurally.**
- **⚠️ Check before ruling this later: D-WS9-056** already ruled that *the model can size an INDIVISIBLE ingredient*, so the **authoring side already has awareness of this concept.** A display rule ruled in isolation risks contradicting authoring behavior that already exists. **Read D-WS9-056 first.**
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-070 (parent) · D-WS9-056 · D-WS7-131 (fraction round-trip loss).

### D-WS9-072 — Draft recovery is a VISIBLE link, not invisible resurfacing: "See Previous Options" + drafts cleared only by an explicit regenerate act — SUPERSEDES D-WS9-035

- **Owner:** WS9 / Plan-Gen Arc **Block 4.** **Status:** ✅ **SHIPPED July 28, 2026 (Block 4b-3, pushed). Supersedes D-WS9-035**, which deferred "same-session supersede scope" to Block 4.
- **⚠️ THE RULE, in Hans's words (the July 27 refinement, and what shipped):** *"user generates plans, sees results. Next time the user goes to generate plans, let them see the prior plan options that were generated. If they click Generate Plans again, clear the prior results and write the new ones."* **Generation clears. Nothing else does** — saving, activating, previewing, backing out and navigating away clear nothing. ⚠️ **"Build My Plan" and "Get New Results" are NOT two separate clearing controls — they are the SAME ACT on two screens.**
- **⚠️ CHAT-CLAUDE PROPOSED SPLITTING "DISMISS" FROM "DISCARD" — HANS OVERRULED IT, AND HE WAS RIGHT.** The proposal was that the dismissed-set gate the *interstitial* but not the *link*; **that distinction does not exist in the build** — the interstitial's only non-resume option **is** "Get New Results," which *is* the regenerate act. Hans: *"we assume the user is thinking 'I know what those are, and I don't want them, so give me new ones' — they don't need or want to see them again."*
- **⚠️ THIS RETROACTIVELY EXPLAINS WHY THE NO-SESSION-ID RULING WORKS.** If generation always clears prior drafts and writes the new batch, **"all unconsumed drafts" IS the last run, by construction** — nothing to disambiguate. **Do not reintroduce session-id plumbing.** **⚠️ The D-WS9-035 deferral was DISSOLVED, not answered** — it asked whether supersede should narrow to same-session drafts, needing a session id threaded through generation and consume; **Hans reframed: drafts are scoped by an EXPLICIT USER ACT, not by session identity.**
- **SCOPE IS GLOBAL, NOT ROUTE-SCOPED (July 27).** All three generate paths show the same last run: **"I think just showing them what was generated the last run is good for now though." NO HOME-PAGE CTA:** *"my lean is not to do this because it's just more there to decide on and less easy click and get stuff."*
- **What the feature is for (Hans):** *"the user goes to the wizard, sees a plan they like, backs out accidentally, and then if they go back to the wizard it's gone."* **A recovery feature — and recovery problems want a visible way back, not invisible state that resurfaces later.** The gap it fixes: swiping back from plan-options left the drafts **existing but unreachable.**
- **RULED — the UX:** a visible **"See Previous Options"** link surfaces the pending batch; **drafts persist until an explicit regenerate act**; **drafts SURVIVE saving a plan.** **Why they survive saving — the deciding reason:** against *saving clears drafts* and *cleared only by "Use This Week"*, **this is the only option where the user can never lose something they wanted.** Its cost is **stale drafts behind a link — a mild tidiness problem**; the others' cost is an **unrecoverable "I picked wrong," the exact complaint that created this feature.** Hans: *"I think it's a better UX."* The two-save-button variant was also rejected as **too much subtlety for a link most users will never tap.**
- **✅ WHAT SHIPPED:** a `WizardLastBatch` table (`userId @unique`, `payload Json`, `source`; FK cascade) upserted **on success only** at the end of all three generate routes and deliberately **not** on Tell Kiwi's `unclear` short-circuit; a last-batch endpoint + the link, with a rehydrate mode on the results screen (mount-time generate/auto-expand effects early-return on rehydrate). The supersede call moved from all four consume sites to the three generate routes, idempotent branches getting a **scoped self-archive** rather than a blanket supersede (BUG-047's fix).
- **⚠️ Consequent behavior change, intended, not a regression:** expand A → expand B → activate A now leaves **B lingering** as a resumable draft until the next generation. Hans: *"it's ok if they see prior results and the prior results included the one they used."* **Marking the already-used option is WS9 3c polish; do not add a second clearing act to achieve it.**
- **⚠️ DRAFTS ARE NOW WRITTEN FOR THE WHOLE BATCH AT `build-plans` TIME — FORCED by the rule**, because the user must see the last run **even if they never opened a card. ✅ Cost is low — measured, correcting an earlier chat-Claude estimate** that ~20% of slots would still need live AI generation (arithmetic on an *assumed* meals-per-candidate — never measured): the device run was **100% catalog-bound. Not guaranteed** — a thin shelf against unusual preferences still needs live fills. Hash-reuse verified: a rehydrated candidate carries its titles verbatim, so the content hash matches and expand reuses the existing draft with **zero AI calls.**
- **⚠️ MOUNT-GATE MECHANISM (explains a confusing behavior Hans hit).** The resume interstitial fires on **screen mount**, so swiping back from a plan detail returns to an **already-mounted** screen and the gate doesn't re-run, while backing out to home and re-entering **remounts** and it does. **This is why the interstitial appeared inconsistently** — and it is the structural argument for the visible link: *a mount-time interruption can only ever catch the user at one moment.* Dismissals also persist to device storage and filter that draft out permanently on every future mount.
- **Two follow-ons:** **BUG-051** (generation doesn't invalidate the cached last-batch query, so the link serves a stale batch until a remount → WS9 3c) and **D-WS9-084** (a stale batch judged against changed preferences is explicitly **not** a defect).
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-035 (superseded) · D-WS9-032 · D-WS9-070 · BUG-030 / BUG-023 · BUG-047 · BUG-051 · D-WS9-083 · D-WS9-084.

### D-WS9-073 — Catalog exhaustion + repeat behavior: deterministic lineage via `sourceStoreMealId`, AI-judged soft nudge (NOT deterministic scoring, NOT hard exclusion) — ✅ SHIPPED July 27, 2026 — ⚠️ **EFFICACY REMAINS AN OPEN MEASUREMENT QUESTION**

- **Owner:** WS9 / Plan-Gen Arc **Block 4.** **Status:** ✅ **RULED** (July 23, 2026) **and SHIPPED** (Block 4b-2, July 27). **Implements the mechanism for D-WS9-039**, whose *direction* remains governing and unchanged.
- **⚠️ TWO OF THE THREE QUEUED SUB-QUESTIONS WERE ALREADY ANSWERED — no new work:** *"what happens when a household has seen most of the catalog?"* → per **D-WS9-037** the read path degrades on **actual coverage, not a flag**, so **exhaustion is not a cliff.** *"Where's the line between 'you loved this' and 'we're out of ideas'?"* → **D-WS9-039 already ruled it:** no aggressive never-repeat logic, bias toward **letting loved meals recur**, recurrence **preference-aware.**
- **What was ACTUALLY open:** the repeat mechanism was **id-based and lineage-blind** — the fork gives the user's copy a **new id**, so `excludeMealIds` cannot connect it to the store original and **the store can re-offer a meal the user already had, arbitrarily.** Such a repeat is **unlikely** per week — but **rare-and-arbitrary is the annoying kind:** unpredictable, and it reads as careless when it lands.
- **⚠️ Hans's reframe — the target is a PATTERN, not a repeat.** *"baked chicken 2 weeks in a row is fine, but I don't want a user to be like 'man, kiwi really loves suggesting those dang fajitas'… but I also recognize it's easier to cook something you've cooked before."* **A window cannot express this** — it only knows recent/not-recent, and cannot distinguish "twice" from "every week."
- **RULED — the split: DETERMINISTIC DATA, AI JUDGMENT.** **Deterministic: `sourceStoreMealId` on the user's forked copy**, pointing back at the catalog original — **a data fact, not a judgment, and without it there is nothing to pass in either direction.** **AI-judged (do NOT build deterministic scoring):** recently-served store ids go into the generation prompt with a soft nudge. **Rejected: hard exclusion** — it creates a cliff (banned, then abruptly fully available), *precisely* what produces the fajita clustering at the boundary, and it forbids the best-burger recurrence outright. **Rejected: deterministic weighted scoring** — it pushes **all versions of a family down together**, whereas the catalog's intentional multiplication of popular meals lets the model **vary WITHIN a family. Unit of recency: PLAN COUNT, not calendar time** (~3 plans) — a time window punishes heavy users and does nothing for someone planning every three weeks.
- **⚠️ The known cost of choosing AI judgment, accepted with eyes open:** a prompt instruction is **unverifiable** — not unit-testable, learnable only from weeks of real use, and **the arc's standing lesson is that prompt-level claims have failed when measured.** **Treat "does the nudge actually work" as an OPEN MEASUREMENT QUESTION, not a shipped feature.**
- **Prompt intent + STARTING DRAFT (⚠️ NOT frozen text):**

  > Meals recently served to this user are listed below. Prefer meals the user hasn't seen. A recently-served meal — or another version of it — may be chosen when the user's preferences point that way, but no meal or dish family should dominate the user's rotation.

  **Why this wording:** Hans's draft (*"avoid over-representing these. similar variations are ok if the user's preferences say so"*) had the right structure, but **"similar variations are ok" reads as permission and risks being taken as encouragement** — the failure mode where the model over-indexes on the most specific clause and returns *six* fajita variants. The revision makes **"prefer unseen" the explicit default**, renders the variant clause **permitted rather than invited**, and anchors "similar" to **`dishFamily`. ⚠️ Do NOT freeze this wording.**
- **Scope boundary: store meals only.** Live-generated meals have no store id and are unaffected.
- **✅ SHIPPED:** a recent-rotation builder walks the user's last **3** plans (a named constant, to be tuned) and resolves each served meal via the lineage hop `fork.sourceStoreMealId → original.dishFamilyKey → {dishFamily, familyRank}`, falling back to **title-only** for live-generated meals. **Best-effort: a failure yields an empty rotation and never sinks generation.** Threaded onto **build-plans** and **directed** only; **Surprise Me deliberately untouched.**
- ✅ **FIRST EFFICACY MEASUREMENT, September 12, 2026 (BUG-255): THE NUDGE FIRED AND LOST — a shelf meal was re-offered five minutes after the plan containing it was saved into the rotation.** **Cause measured and ruled: at a 30-minute cap the eligible shelf is SIX dinners, and all six appear in this user's generations. Prefer-unseen over six candidates has nowhere to go.** **The rule is unchanged; the fix is the catalog supplement. Revisit efficacy once the shelf is deep.** ⚠️ **AND OTHERWISE IT REMAINS UNVERIFIED — it must not be quietly treated as closed.** At ship time the account carried **24 lineage-bearing forks with `timesRecentlyServed` mostly 1** — almost nothing for "prefer-unseen / no domination" to push against. The device test confirmed the **mechanism**, **not the behavior. Revisit with real usage before assuming this works.**
- **⚠️ FUTURE GAP — the plan-walk misses cooked-but-never-planned meals.** The replaced helper carried a **cooked branch** (`cook_meal` activity events) the rotation walk does not; that branch is **inert today**, so nothing was lost. **But when the Cook Mode completion writer lands (WS7-11 / D-WS7-204), a meal cooked without being on a plan will be invisible to the rotation walk.** The fix is likely a union, not a replacement.
- **⚠️ TWO RULINGS APPLIED AT BUILD TIME (Hans).** (1) **REPLACE, not layer** (§10, the line-824 lesson): the pre-existing `# Recent history` instruction was *replaced*, accepting cache-prefix invalidation and a version bump as the cost of one coherent mechanism. (2) **Build-plans and directed only:** Surprise Me was excluded because its crowd-pleaser constraint (*"popular, mainstream… No obscure or experimental dishes"*) points at the catalog **head** — exactly where a returning user's already-seen meals concentrate — a soft-vs-soft collision with no tie-break.
- **⚠️ ONE CLAUSE CUT FROM THE DRAFT, and the reasoning generalizes:** an *"or genuine ingredient reuse across the plan"* permission was removed. The two surviving exceptions (a listed cuisine; an allergy/constraint that narrows the field) are **user preferences**, which is what this entry licensed; **ingredient reuse is a system objective in a different category**, already instructed elsewhere (D-WS7-167), and naming it a third time invites the model to use it as a general-purpose excuse to repeat.
- **⚠️ THE SHELF GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING — do not let future prompt edits erode it.** Both shipped sections state that prefer-unseen means *"reaching for a different shelf meal or a different dish family, never abandoning the shelf."* ⚠️ **Corrected September 10, measured: that is set_preferences' wording; the directed body says *"prefer-unseen means a different shelf meal or family, not abandoning the shelf."* A guard asserts each body's own phrase.** Without it, prefer-unseen reads as licence to invent over catalog meals, **silently undoing Block 4b-1's entire gain.** Verbatim text is in `kiwi_plan_generation_arc_scope.md` §Block 4b-2.
- **Measured lineage ground truth (corrects canon):** **24** forks carry `sourceStoreMealId` across **20 originals** (canon said ~20 forks); 19/20 carry `dishFamilyKey`. ⚠️ **Every fork's own `dishFamilyKey` is null** — forks never copy it — so **the hop to the original is the only path.** ⚠️ **Canon's "write-backs don't carry lineage" is FALSE.**
- 🔴 **THE GAP HANS FOUND September 11, 2026, AND IT IS IN THIS ENTRY'S OWN SHIPPED DESIGN: the rotation walks the user's last 3 PLANS, so a meal OFFERED in a generation that is never saved is never "recently served" and can be offered again indefinitely.** He has seen one flatbread *"a handful of times recently when generating plans."* **Minted as BUG-255, where the ruling (does offering count as seen?) and the measurement that must precede it live.** ⚠️ **Same shape as this entry's own cooked-but-never-planned gap — and the same likely fix, a union rather than a replacement.**
- 🔵 **TWO NEIGHBOURS ADDED September 10, 2026 — DIFFERENT RULES, KEEP THEM APART.** **BUG-249** (no meal repeated across the three plans of ONE generation) is within a response; this entry is across generations. The server block that builds BUG-249 was told to leave this entry's rotation text byte-identical and to guard each body's own shelf-guard phrase. **D-WS9-234** (the Playlist): a declared staple must not be pushed away by this nudge — confirm at the playlist spec.
- **Cross-ref:** D-WS9-039 · D-WS9-037 · D-WS9-045 (`dishFamily` — the anchor for "similar") · D-WS9-061 · D-WS9-036 · D-WS9-070 / D-WS9-072 · D-WS7-204 · WS7-11 · BUG-249 · D-WS9-234.
