### D-WS9-214 — 🔴 The allergen vocabulary cannot see PROCESSED PRODUCTS, pizza is on a gluten-free shelf today, and this is now a mechanism decision

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[SAFETY]` `[CATALOG]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[LAUNCH-BLOCKING]` · **Date:** September 4, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — gaps ship immediately; the MECHANISM question is unruled and put to Hans.**
- **Source:** CC Phase 0 for the server block. ⚠️ **Found by a generalised sweep that re-derived all 1,192 pool meals, NOT by the three checks — and CC said so against itself: the three checks were shaped from the last bug's vocabulary and structurally could not catch this.**

🔴 **THE LIVE DEFECT: `dough` IS NOT IN THE WHEAT VOCABULARY.** *Sausage, Pepper, and Onion Pizza* and *Margherita Pizza Night* are stamped `[dairy]` and **appear on a Gluten-free shelf.** Ingredients read from the graph: `store-bought pizza dough` · `Pizza dough`. **This is the carbonara defect again, one week later, in a different word.**

**The measured gaps, by meals affected:**

| missing token | ingredient | meals |
|---|---|---|
| **egg** | **Mayonnaise / Japanese mayonnaise** | **136** |
| egg / dairy | brioche buns (five spellings) | 43 / 11 |
| wheat | cream of mushroom / chicken soup | 15 |
| wheat | pizza dough (three spellings) | 11 |
| gluten | lager / stout / dark Mexican beer | 6 |
| sesame · fish · tree_nut · wheat | hummus · dashi · basil pesto · stuffing mix, pierogi, empanada discs | 2 · 2 · 1 · 3 |

- ⚠️ **`worcestershire → soy` (159 meals) is EXCLUDED as `UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESIS`** — brand-dependent, Lea & Perrins US lists no soy. **Do not add it on the same footing as the others.** Same caution killed `Vegetable broth` (11 meals).
- 🔴 **SCALE: the confident gaps are ~230 meal-instances, and MAYONNAISE ALONE (136) IS LARGER THAN EVERY SAFETY-RELEVANT ADDITION LANE A MADE (~30).**

**⚠️ THE PATTERN, AND IT IS ONE CLASS RATHER THAN TWELVE BUGS: the vocabulary matches LITERAL INGREDIENT WORDS. It handles `parmigiano → dairy` and every pasta shape. It cannot handle a COMPOUND OR PROCESSED PRODUCT whose name contains no allergen word** — mayonnaise, pizza dough, brioche, beer, condensed cream soups, hummus, pesto.

🔴 **THIS IS THE THIRD ROUND OF THE SAME GAME, AND CC ALREADY TOLD US IT CANNOT BE FINISHED.** Round 1 added literal words. Round 2 added disqualifiers (`coconut milk`). Round 3 is this. **CC's own conclusion last round, unprompted: *"I do not believe these lists are complete, and I don't think they can be made complete… the find rate has not declined."*** ⚠️ **And it named the exit at the time: *"deriving allergens at generation time, where the model knows the food, rather than pattern-matching the name afterwards."*** **That is Hans's own D-WS9-189 framing — *"we're going to keep playing whack-a-mole with these cases"* — arriving in a second domain.**

**THE OPEN DECISION (Hans's):**
- **(a) Keep patching the list.** Ship the ~230 meals now, accept a fourth round.
- **(b) Model-derived at creation, retire the list.** One cheap call per meal — the model knows mayonnaise carries egg. ⚠️ **Cost unmeasured; size it before choosing.**
- **(c) HYBRID — chat-Claude's recommendation: deterministic floor ∪ model ceiling.** Keep the word list (fast, free, auditable, no call on the hot path); add model derivation at creation for what it cannot see; **union the two, which is safe in the over-stamping direction**. ⚠️ **`allergenSources` (D-WS9-211 follow-on) records WHICH MECHANISM produced each token, so the union stays auditable rather than becoming a black box.**
- ⚠️ **WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, THE ~230-MEAL GAP LIST SHIPS FIRST AND IMMEDIATELY** — pizza on a coeliac's shelf does not wait for an architecture decision.

**✅ RULED BY HANS, September 4, 2026 — OPTION (c), THE HYBRID.** Verbatim: *"C sounds good. I was almost going to say B, but I like using the server and backing up to AI if needed."*

- **The shape:** the deterministic word list is the **floor** — fast, free, auditable, nothing on the hot path. **Model derivation at creation time is the ceiling**, for the processed products the list structurally cannot see. **Union the two.** ⚠️ **The union is safe in the over-stamping direction, which is the direction this project has already ruled acceptable (D-WS9-211's Worcestershire call) — but NOT where the cost concentrates on the protected group (D-WS9-211's coconut-milk lesson). Both constraints apply to the model layer too.**
- ⚠️ **`allergenSources` MUST RECORD WHICH MECHANISM PRODUCED EACH TOKEN.** Without that the union is a black box and no future gap-scan is possible. **This is the reason provenance stopped being a nice-to-have.**
- **Hans's framing of why (c) over (b), and it is a design principle worth keeping:** *"I like using the server and backing up to AI if needed."* **Deterministic first, model as fallback — not model-first.** The list is the thing you can reason about, test, and mutate deliberately; the model is what covers what you failed to anticipate.
- ✅ **Hans's stated goal for this: *"get this put to bed and move on with a complete solution."*** ⚠️ **So a fourth round of list-patching is a FAILURE of this ruling, not a continuation of it. If the hybrid ships and a new gap class still appears, that is a finding about the model layer, not a cue to extend the word list again.**
- **Sequencing:** the ~230-meal deterministic gap list ships **immediately and first**; the model ceiling is a separate block and **its per-meal cost must be measured before it is committed to** (§27.6 — do not project it).

**⚠️ EGG AND DAIRY ARE SEPARATE ALLERGENS AND THE SYSTEM ALREADY TREATS THEM SO — Hans asked, and his assumption is correct.** They are different proteins with different mechanisms (egg: ovalbumin/ovomucoid; milk: casein/whey), and lactose intolerance is a third thing entirely — an enzyme deficiency, not an allergy. **`egg` and `dairy` are two of the nine tokens with two separate chips, and nothing in this arc has ever merged them. Do not "simplify" them together.**

- **What prompted the question was a reporting artifact, not a defect:** `brioche` appears in the gap table under **both** tokens because brioche genuinely contains **egg AND butter** — one ingredient, two independent allergens. **Mayonnaise, by contrast, is egg only** — which is exactly what Hans reasoned unprompted on the device (*"coleslaw… that's eggs and oil and not cheese/milk"*), and he was right on both halves.
- ⚠️ **A LATENT PRODUCT QUESTION, RECORDED NOT RULED:** one `Dairy-free` chip serves both milk-allergic and lactose-intolerant users, who have materially different tolerances — hard aged cheese and butter are often fine for the latter and never for the former. **The single chip is SAFE (it over-excludes) but restrictive.** Same granularity theme as the substitution question. **Do not split it without a ruling.**

✅ **BUILT (blocked at the migration gate, not at the code). SEVEN BEYOND-BRIEF ITEMS FLAGGED FOR VETO — ALL ACCEPTED, each verified against the live catalog first.**

- **Bare `dough` instead of three "pizza dough" spellings** — all 28 catalog names containing `dough` are wheat, and `\bdough\b` does not match inside `sourdough`, which keeps its own entry. Also covers refrigerated pie dough and frozen phyllo.
- **Bare `mayo` alongside `mayonnaise`** — the catalog carries *"Greek yogurt or mayo"*, which now correctly derives **both** dairy and egg from one name.
- **`cream of celery soup`** — the third canonical variety, absent from the catalog, added so this does not need a fourth pass.
- **Five re-scan terms — `roti`, `paratha`, `teriyaki`, `hoisin`, `gravy mix`** — closing **four more meals a coeliac could reach right now**: *Thai Red Curry with Roti*, *Teriyaki Tofu Bowl*, *Mississippi Pot Roast* (au jus gravy mix), *Tofu Pad Thai*. ⚠️ **Three of the four are not new claims: `teriyaki` and `hoisin` ARE soy sauce, sold under names that never say soy, and `soy sauce → wheat` already shipped. `roti`/`paratha` sit at the confidence of `naan`.** Only `gravy mix` is new, it rides the cream-of-soup precedent, and it is **the phrase, not bare `gravy`** — which is often cornstarch.
- 🔴 **`rematerializeMeal` — the EDIT path — now stamps, and this is the sharpest of the seven.** CC's reasoning, kept: *"An edit is what invalidates a stamp — a user adding cheese leaves a stale dairy-free stamp, and a wrong stamp is worse than a missing one (missing fails closed; wrong serves the meal)."*
- **`materializeMeal` derives from the graph rather than honouring `payload.allergens`, including for the batch harness.** The two agree, so it is a no-op there, and it collapses two sources of truth into one.

✅ **AND THE LANE REFUSED ITS OWN RE-SCAN FINDINGS ON CONSISTENCY GROUNDS, WHICH IS THE DISCIPLINE WORKING.** `curry paste → shellfish` (15 meals, Thai pastes commonly contain kapi) and `kimchi → fish` (4 meals, jeotgal) were found and **left out — same confidence class as the rejected `worcestershire → soy`.** Its words: *"Rejecting one and shipping the other would be the inconsistency."* **These 19 meals are ceiling work — a per-brand question is exactly what the model pass is for.** `pesto → dairy` likewise left out and recorded as an open residual.

⚠️ **`stampAllergens` GREW A `force` OPTION, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THE TIMESTAMP MEAN WHAT WE WANTED.** Without it `allergensStampedAt` means *"when the stamp last CHANGED"* — so a row re-verified unchanged under a new vocabulary keeps its old date and a *"re-stamp everything older than X"* sweep **never converges.** The batch pass forces; hot paths do not, preserving the no-write-on-correct-stamp property.

🔴 **THE BACKFILL `UPDATE` MUST SHIP IN THE SAME MIGRATION AS THE COLUMNS.** The filter clause changes in the same commit — **add the columns without the UPDATE and every row reads NULL, so the new clause excludes the ENTIRE POOL from every allergic user.** With it, behaviour is byte-identical to today's the instant the migration completes.

⚠️ **A GREEN BREAK CAUGHT A FALSE BELIEF THAT WAS WRITTEN IN BOTH A COMMENT AND A TEST.** CC had recorded that `\bale\b` matches `guanciale` and `kale`. **It does not — the preceding letter is a word character, so no boundary exists.** Those were `includes()` hits from the Phase 0 probe, carried forward into word-mode code. **Adding `ale` changed nothing, so the test passed for a reason unrelated to what it claimed.** ✅ **Rewritten to pin the real danger one layer down — under `mode: "raw"`, which the `fish` token already uses, a beer word list would swallow all four names.** ⚠️ **Second time in this arc a break-it pass has caught a false belief embedded in a source comment. A comment is not evidence.**

✅ **APPLIED AND COMMITTED — `6a82218`, 1,578 rows written, idempotency proven by an immediate re-run reporting 0 changes on every token and 0/0 on all eleven chips.** Suite 1838/1838, typecheck clean. **This commit completes a contract whose client half shipped in `2bbf3cb`** — until it landed the client's omitted allergen field still hit the old `.default([])`, so the client fix was inert rather than wrong.

🔴 **THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS A SAFETY RESULT NOT A REACH RESULT: 136 meals left the Egg-free shelf, 130 of them because they contain `Mayonnaise`. An egg-allergic user has been served every one of them.** Buffalo wings, Nashville hot chicken, every coleslaw plate. **The 9% reach loss on that chip is the price and it is correct.**

**Measured reach, all eleven chips, computed and self-checked (`before + gained − lost = after`):**

| chip | before → after | newly reachable | newly excluded | top causes of loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Egg-free** | **902 → 824** | 58 | **136** | Mayonnaise 130 · brioche buns 39 |
| Gluten-free | 359 → 385 | 63 | 37 | pizza dough 8 · cream soups 13 · lager 4 · hoisin 3 |
| Wheat-free | 365 → 397 | 64 | 32 | pizza dough 10 · cream soups 13 · hoisin 3 |
| Dairy-free | 251 → 304 | 64 | 11 | brioche (all spellings) |
| Fish-free | 864 → 926 | 64 | 2 | dashi powder, dashi stock |
| Sesame-free | 966 → 1028 | 64 | 2 | hummus |
| Nut-free · Tree-nut-free | 1086 → 1149 · 1107 → 1170 | 64 | 1 | basil pesto |
| Shellfish-free · Soy-free · Peanut-free | 998 → 1062 · 950 → 1014 · 1107 → 1171 | 64 | 0 | — |

⚠️ **The cause counts are TOP CAUSES, not a partition — a meal can lose a shelf for two reasons at once (mayo AND brioche), so they sum above the meal count. Do not add them up.**

⚠️ **THE `+64` ON NINE CHIPS IS REAL AND EXPLAINED, NOT A COPY-PASTE:** the newly-reachable set is dominated by the **64 previously-unstamped pool rows**, which were excluded from *every* chip simultaneously by fail-closed. **Seven of those 64 gain a token under the new vocabulary (`{egg: 6, gluten: 1}`), which is exactly why Egg-free reads 58 and Gluten-free 63 while the other nine read 64.** ✅ **CC's earlier claim that only ONE gained a token was wrong; the two statements could not both be true and the data settled it.**

**⚠️ THE OFF-BY-ONE HAD A REAL CAUSE AND IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ARITHMETIC: THE REACH TABLE WAS JOINED ON MEAL TITLE.** **The catalog contains duplicate titles across `sourceType` — the same dish minted by the batch harness and again by a live write-back** (e.g. *Al Pastor Tacos with Black Bean and Avocado Salad*). A title-keyed set collapses distinct rows, so `gained`/`lost` under-counted while `before`/`after`, counted by id, stayed correct. **That is why exactly three rows were wrong and two were right.** The table is now keyed by id and emitted by the script.

- 🔴 **UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESIS, AND IT IS WORTH ONE PROBE: THIS MAY BE PART OF BUG-166's MECHANISM.** BUG-166 is the largest duplicate-meal bucket (20 groups) and has sat **UNCHARACTERISED**. **If the same dish is live in the retrieval pool twice under two `sourceType`s, a user can be served it twice in one week and the catalog's effective variety is smaller than its row count suggests.** ⚠️ **Do not treat this as characterising BUG-166 — it is a side-effect of a join bug, not a measurement of that bug. Probe it: count pool rows sharing a normalised title, broken out by `sourceType`.**

✅ **AND THE COMPUTE-DON'T-RETYPE RULE WAS IMPLEMENTED RATHER THAN ACKNOWLEDGED.** The reach table, the dark-pool breakdown and the itemised loss are now **emitted by `ws9-d214-allergen-backfill.ts`**, with the prohibition written into the code as a comment. ⚠️ **This was the THIRD hand-assembled table in one block to disagree with its own computed data (126/127, 142/145, this). In all three the data was right and the prose was wrong. The rule now lives where it executes, not where it is merely documented.**

**Residuals, all deliberate, none silent, all noted in `allergens.ts`:** `curry paste → shellfish` and `kimchi → fish` (19 meals, brand-dependent — same confidence class as the rejected `worcestershire → soy`) and `pesto → dairy`. **All three are ceiling work for the model layer.**

### D-WS9-217 — 🔵 The SUBSUMES reader is purchase de-duplication, NEVER substitution — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 5, 2026)**

- ✅ **THE SUBSUMES READER SHIPPED on dev September 28 (grocery B2, `565d138`)**, opt-in on a plan's demanded generics, inside the synonym union-find so the salt veto and the cluster refusal apply to it unchanged (break 2 turned six tests red). Rules on D-WS9-282.

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` · **Date:** September 5, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9, definition track · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — direction settled; the per-edge classification it implies is OPEN and is chat-Claude's to produce** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-189** · BUG-175 · BUG-096 · D-WS9-174.

**The question put to Hans:** *"Is `subsumes` allowed to change what you cook with, or only to prevent a duplicate purchase?"* — with a worked case: a plan where one dish calls for `cheddar` and another for `sharp cheddar`. Folding buys one block instead of two, **and makes the first dish with a cheese it did not ask for.**

**Hans's ruling, verbatim:** *"I like the only collapse when generic demand has no independent purchase."*

**What it settles.** `subsumes` exists to stop the list ordering **two packages of one thing**. It does **not** license quietly re-specifying an ingredient a dish asked for. ⚠️ **Where folding would change what the user cooks with, the two rows stand.** The list being one line longer is the acceptable outcome; the dish silently changing is not.

- **Direction is mechanically forced and is NOT the ruled part:** buying `kosher salt` satisfies a `salt` demand; buying `salt` does not satisfy a `kosher salt` demand. **The surviving row is always the SPECIFIC one.** A reader that folds the other way is a defect, not a policy variant.
- ⚠️ **SCOPE BOUNDARY: this does not authorize `subsumes` to REMOVE a row the user would otherwise see.** It merges two buy lines into one; it never deletes a demand.

🔴 **THE CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MAKES WORK RATHER THAN CLOSING IT: THE 556 `subsumes` ROWS ARE NOT UNIFORMLY SAFE, SO A BLANKET READER CANNOT IMPLEMENT THIS RULING.** The same label covers both halves of the split:

| safe to fold — the swap is culinarily neutral | changes the dish — must NOT fold |
|---|---|
| `lettuce → romaine lettuce` · `egg → large eggs` · `sugar → granulated sugar` | `cheddar → sharp cheddar` (a taste change the recipe did not ask for) |

⚠️ **So the deliverable this ruling creates is a SECOND CLASSIFICATION over the 556, not a reader over all of them.** Until that split exists, **the subsumes reader has nothing safe to read.** ⚠️ **Do not implement a confidence threshold as a proxy for it — confidence measures how sure the judge was that the relation is TRUE, not whether acting on it changes a dish. Those are different questions and conflating them is how a wrong fold ships looking reviewed.**

- ⚠️ **CHAT-CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL, MARKED AS SUCH SO IT IS NOT LATER READ AS HANS'S:** the split is a per-edge judgment, so it is the same shape as A1's authoring pass and should reuse it rather than invent a mechanism (`ws9-d189-a1-relations.ts` → `-finalise.ts` → `-apply.ts`, the BUG-096 contract parameterised). **The rubric asks one question — *"if a dish asked for the generic and the shopper bought only the specific, would the dish be meaningfully different?"*** ⚠️ **That is a rubric question, and A1's own pilot proved a neutral rubric gets shopper-policy cases wrong** (the peppercorn ruling: culinarily true, commercially wrong). **Write the policy into the rubric explicitly; do not expect the model to infer it.**
- ⚠️ **AND USE THE METHOD THAT ACTUALLY WORKED ON A1's REVIEW: rule a CLASS, apply it in bulk.** A1's 101 human rows were stamped programmatically from Hans's class-level rulings, not hand-edited — the largest sheet ever completed by hand on this project is 23 rows. **A per-edge sheet of 556 will not be completed and should not be produced.**

**⚠️ AMENDED SEPTEMBER 5, 2026 — THE FIRST CONCRETE APPLICATION, AND IT IS A PERMANENT REFUSAL: `coarse kosher salt ↔ kosher salt` NEVER FOLDS.** Surfaced by A2 Phase 0 as the only cross-product salt edge in the table (medium confidence, unreviewed, firing on live lists `c08a9f4e` and `98dc58d0`).

**Hans, verbatim:** *"unfolded, we can leave that as coarse and regular as separate items. if the user wants to sub regular for coarse it's up to them."*

- ⛔ **DO NOT REVISIT. Do not re-propose it in a later block, do not promote it on a confidence upgrade, and do not fold it as a side effect of a widened cluster rule.** ⚠️ **If a future cluster rule would sweep it up, THAT RULE IS WRONG.** It also sits beside a locked ruling — BUG-168, on Hans's *"iodized salt is NOT kosher is NOT flaky sea salt."*
- ⚠️ **THIS IS THE THIRD CASE ON THIS PROJECT DECIDED BY ONE PRINCIPLE, AND NAMING IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SALT: THE SUBSTITUTION IS THE USER'S CALL, NOT KIWI'S.** The same reasoning retired the allergen possible-contaminant stamps (**D-WS9-216**, *"the user still has to place an order for the variety of sausage they want"*) and set this entry's own direction. **Two rows on the list is the correct outcome — the shopper can buy one box and use it for both, and that is theirs to decide.**
- **Guard it in code, not prose:** a test that FAILS if the two ever land in one fold. **A permanent ruling that lives only in a document is one refactor away from being lost.**
- 🔴 **AND THE GUARD HAD TO BE A CLUSTER-LEVEL VETO, NOT AN EDGE-LEVEL ONE — A TEST CAUGHT THE DIFFERENCE ON THE FIRST TRY.** Blocking the direct `coarse kosher salt ↔ kosher salt` edge is **defeated by a transitive path through individually-admissible edges.** That is exactly the *"widened cluster rule"* failure this ruling warned about, arriving immediately and from inside the implementation rather than from a later block. ⚠️ **THE RULE THAT GENERALISES TO EVERY FUTURE NEVER-FOLD PAIR: a cluster containing a forbidden pair is refused WHOLE.** Nothing in the data says which edge in the chain is the wrong one, **so folding the remainder would be guessing** — and a guess that produces a plausible-looking merged row is the failure mode nothing catches downstream.

**Downstream, unchanged by this entry but gated on it:** **BUG-175's 16 permanently-inert `IngredientAlias` rows are all generic→specific — they ARE `subsumes`.** The alias table was being asked to express a row→row subsumption with a string→row mechanism, which is why canonical-beats-alias made them unreachable. ⚠️ **The fix is to DELETE those 16 rows once a subsumes reader exists — not to repair them.** Do not attempt the deletion before the reader.

### D-WS9-218 — 🔴 The COMPONENT yield has no stored BASIS UNIT, and `defaultUnit` cannot stand in — 57 of 95 edges are arithmetically undefined

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[SCHEMA]` · **Date:** September 5, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟠 **CONTESTED — THE PREMISE IS CHALLENGED WITH CODE EVIDENCE. DO NOT BUILD THE COLUMN.** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-189** · **D-WS9-222** · D-WS9-182 · BUG-133 · BUG-200.
- 🔴 **CHALLENGED September 6, 2026 (A3-prep), AND THE POLARITY MAY BE INVERTED.** A second CC session reports that **the basis unit IS stored**: `buildRelationIndex` sets `basisUnit = normalizeUnit(row.fromDefaultUnit)`, and on **39 of 39 admitted slots it resolves to a buyable count or pack unit** — `head`, `bunch`, `each`, `dozen`. ⚠️ **Its reading of this entry's own headline number: the 57 in *"57 of 95 undefined"* is the count of edges that DO have a countable basis. The other 38 do not — and they are blocked by a PARENT THAT IS NOT A COUNTABLE PURCHASE** (`jasmine rice` in cups, `water` in cups, `parmigiano-reggiano` in ounces), **which no column fixes. Measured unblock from a `fromUnit` column: ZERO of 38.**
- ⚠️ **TWO CC SESSIONS DISAGREE ABOUT THIS ENTRY AND THE LATER ONE CITES CODE WHILE THE EARLIER ONE ASSERTED.** That is why this reads CONTESTED rather than CLOSED: an audit report is a claim even when it cites line numbers, and one Phase 0 in this arc produced three cited claims that Phase 1 refuted. **Re-confirm `basisUnit`'s derivation at the start of whatever block next touches the pool — one read settles it.**
- ✅ **WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT: DO NOT ADD THE COLUMN, AND DO NOT TREAT THIS AS A BLOCKER GATING THE COMPONENT READER.** The `[BLOCKER]` tag is removed. **The real live arithmetic gap is 2 slots of 26, not 57 of 95:** `broccoli → florets` (yield in `cup`, one live demand in `pound`; both rows carry a `gramsPerCup`, so the density exists and is simply not threaded into the pool's `toYieldUnit`) and `fresh basil → leaves` (`conversionRef` is null, so nothing converts leaves to cups). **Both are small and neither is a schema change.**
- **Found by:** CC, A2 Phase 0, **against its own brief.** ⚠️ **The brief asserted the component pass was buildable as specified. It is not, and the reason is a schema fact rather than a design preference.**

**The defect.** `IngredientRelation.yieldQuantity` / `yieldUnit` mean *"how much of `to` one unit of `from` yields."* ⚠️ **Nothing stores what one unit of `from` IS.** The schema's worked examples (lemon, garlic head) are all implicitly `each`, so the ambiguity never surfaced during authoring.

**`Ingredient.defaultUnit` is NOT the missing value, demonstrated rather than argued** — 57 of 95 parents carry a non-`each` default and the arithmetic comes out absurd:

| edge | reading under `defaultUnit` |
|---|---|
| `large eggs [dozen] → egg whites [1 each]` | **one dozen yields one white — a 12× error** |
| `parmesan [cup] → parmesan rind [1 each]` | one cup of parmesan yields one rind |
| `whole nutmeg [teaspoon] → freshly grated nutmeg [2 tsp]` | 1 tsp whole yields 2 tsp grated |
| `canned tuna in olive oil [can] → olive oil [2 tbsp]` | ✅ correct — the coincidence that hides the class |

- ✅ **RULED FOR A2 (chat-Claude's call, delegated): the component pass ships ONLY for edges whose parent resolves to a countable `each`/`head`/`bunch` basis the conversion table can express — 🔴 **53 of 95**, and the dry run PRINTS every edge it declined and why.** ⚠️ **CORRECTED SEPTEMBER 5: this entry and the go-ahead prompt both said "38", which is the `each` count ALONE — the real admitted set is `each` 38 + `head` 4 + `bunch` 11 = 53, across 23 parents. Chat-Claude relayed a figure without asking which category it counted; CC caught it at build time.** ⚠️ **The declined set is 42, not 57 — 42 declined + 53 admitted = 95.** That keeps lemon, lime, garlic and egg, which are the motivating cases, and **refuses the ambiguous 57 rather than guessing.** ⚠️ **A declined edge must be visibly declined, not silently skipped.**
- 🔴 **UNRULED AND DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED HERE: whether to mint a `fromUnit` column.** It is a schema change, it was fenced out of A2, and **it is the only thing that unblocks the other 57.** ⚠️ **Do not add it as a side effect of another block.**

⚠️ **THE AUTHORING PASS COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART.** The judge was asked *"is A derived from B, and how much"* — a question that is complete without a basis unit. **The gap only appears when something tries to READ the data.** **A1's review verified the relations were TRUE; it could not verify they were USABLE, and no rubric would have.**

### D-WS9-219 — 🔴 STRING→ROW vs ROW→ROW: the boundary that has now stalled four separate things, and neither table can cross it

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` `[ARCHITECTURE]` · **Date:** September 5, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — named, not solved** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-189** · **D-WS9-193** · BUG-175 · BUG-177 · BUG-150 · BUG-164 · BUG-187.

**Two tables, two shapes, and D-WS9-193 rules they never consult each other:**

- **`IngredientAlias`** — **STRING → ROW.** Maps a free-text name onto a catalog row. `aliasKey @unique`, 141 rows.
- **`IngredientRelation`** — **ROW → ROW.** Relates two catalog rows. 1,870 rows.

🔴 **A FREE-TEXT NAME WITH NO CATALOG ROW IS REACHABLE BY NEITHER, AND THAT GAP HAS NOW BLOCKED FOUR SEPARATE PIECES OF WORK THAT NOBODY CONNECTED:**

1. **A2's synonym reader** — 6 of `MERGE_GROUP_VARIANT_TO_BASE`'s 11 entries (`evoo`, `cracked pepper`, `virgin olive oil`, `light olive oil`, `ground pepper`, `fresh ground black pepper`) **have no variant catalog row at all.** No relation edge can ever exist for them. **This is why the hand map cannot be replaced.**
2. **BUG-177** — **there is no catalog row `milk`.** `whole milk` exists; `milk` does not. A row→row relation needs two rows.
3. **BUG-150 / BUG-164 / BUG-187** — the synthetic recurring bucket mints a row with **`ingredientId: null`**. A null FK cannot be an endpoint of a relation.
4. **BUG-175** — 16 alias rows are permanently inert because their `aliasKey` is another row's `canonicalName`, and canonical beats alias unconditionally. **They are trying to express a row→row subsumption through a string→row mechanism.**

⚠️ **THE COMMON SHAPE, AND IT IS WHY THESE KEPT LOOKING LIKE FIVE UNRELATED BUGS: THE SYSTEM HAS TWO NAME-RESOLUTION MECHANISMS AND A POPULATION THAT FALLS BETWEEN THEM.** Free text the user typed, and legacy strings baked into hand maps, are resolved by **neither**.

- ⚠️ **THE CONSEQUENCE FOR TRIAGE, WHICH IS THE ACTIONABLE PART TODAY: any bug whose fix requires relating a NAME to a ROW must not be assigned to the relation program.** It will ride a block and come out the other side still broken. **BUG-150, BUG-164, BUG-177 and BUG-187 are 🟠 ORPHAN with respect to D-WS9-189, not 🔵 ASSIGNED.**
- **The unruled question this poses:** whether the recurring free-text path should resolve through `lookupIngredientByName` before bucketing, which would move these four inside the alias mechanism's reach. ⚠️ **That is a change to a path D-WS9-188 already owns — do not open it from inside a relation block.**
- ⚠️ **Chat-Claude's proposal, marked as such: nothing here argues for merging the two tables.** D-WS9-193's separation is sound and the shapes are genuinely different. **What is missing is a resolution step BEFORE either table is consulted, not a third table.**

### D-WS9-221 — 🔵 The purchase pack must NAME A SIZE, and it is the smallest normal size that retires the demand — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 6, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 6, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — one EXISTENCE question gates the build** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-209** · **BUG-124** · **BUG-171** · **D-WS7-197** · D-WS9-220 · BUG-207 · BUG-211 · BUG-096.

- **Hans, verbatim:** *"pack is derived from sum of demand, for sure. and the purchase pack would by the smallest normal size to retire the demand. the paremesan cheese 8oz example showing a shopping item of 'parmesan cheese' without a unit or size doesn't line up in my mind. I'd rather say I need 8 oz cheese, buy 8 oz cheese. or I need cheese, buy 8oz. not I need 8 oz buy cheese"*

- **The rule in his own three shapes:** ✅ *I need 8 oz cheese → buy 8 oz cheese* · ✅ *I need cheese → buy 8 oz* · ❌ *I need 8 oz → buy cheese*. 🔴 **THE BUY LINE MUST ALWAYS CARRY A CONCRETE SIZE.** A pack rendering as a bare name, or as `1 container` with no size, is the defect. **The size may come from the demand or from the pack — but it must land somewhere the shopper can act on.**

- ⚠️ **AMENDED September 6, 2026 — THE PACK LINE MUST STATE THE COUNT, NOT JUST THE SIZE. Hans's reason generalises well past the copy.** Shown the live merged row `9 oz parmesan · 1 wedge (6 oz)` — a 9 oz need against a 6 oz wedge — he ruled, verbatim: *"the pack line needs 2 wedges. or if a user reads too fast or isn't thinking. OR if they send it to Instacart once that's built, it orders too little."*
- 🔴 **SO THE PACK LINE IS AN ORDER QUANTITY, NOT DISPLAY COPY.** Understating the count is **not cosmetic — it is an under-order**: silently, by a reader skimming, today; and **mechanically, by the retailer hand-off once it exists** (§9 keeps backend shapes Instacart-friendly regardless of when that ships). **A pack line must render the number of packs required to retire the SUMMED demand — `2 wedges (6 oz each)`, never `1 wedge (6 oz)` against a 9 oz need.** ⚠️ **This is the third distinct failure mode in one family: BUG-124 over-orders from a too-big stored pack, BUG-211 under-orders from a missing `subUnit`, and this under-orders from a pack count that is never stated. All three are the same question — how many do I put in the basket — answered by three different mechanisms.**

- **Two clauses, and they are SEPARATE pieces of work:** **(1)** the pack derives from the **SUMMED** demand, never from whichever row happened to survive a merge — that is BUG-209's fix; **(2)** the pack is the **smallest normal retail size that retires that summed demand.**

- ✅ **THIS DOES NOT CONFLICT WITH BUG-171, AND THE APPARENT CONFLICT IS RECORDED HERE SO NOBODY RE-OPENS IT.** BUG-171 ruled (Hans, August 27, 2026) that a **pantry staple** shows the NEED and **no pack at all** — *"users might buy in bulk or only a little at a time, so it's a good call for pantry staples."* **That is a carve-out for staples, not a competing rule.** The discriminator already exists as `isUniversalStaple`: **staples state a need; everything else states a sized buy.**

- ⚠️ **THIS IS BUG-124 RE-RULED FROM THE PRODUCT SIDE, AND ITS EVIDENCE STANDS.** BUG-124 (August 21, 2026) already named the mechanism — *"the purchase-pack field holds computed needs, not buyable packages."* Measured: **13 rows order more than 2× the need — Parmesan 6×, shaved Parmesan 5×, Kalamata olives 4×, olive oil spray 4× — and every one is `packs = 1`, the smallest order the code can emit, with a row pack byte-identical to its stored catalog pack. Cause is the STORED PACK in 13 of 13; not one row over-scaled.** 🔴 **So the fix is NOT in the ordering arithmetic. It is in the pack data.**

- ⚠️ **THE TWO MEASUREMENTS OF "does it under-buy" DISAGREE BECAUSE THEY COUNT DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. DO NOT AVERAGE THEM.** BUG-124's device repro shows `roma tomatoes` ordering **4** against a need of **9** — a real under-buy. The later sweep reports **zero** under-ordering across the **793 computable rows of 2,067**. Both are true; **the computable set excludes the shape that under-buys.**

- 🔴 **THE EXISTENCE QUESTION THAT GATES ANY BUILD, AND IT MUST BE ANSWERED IN CODE BEFORE A SPEC IS WRITTEN (§8.1 — only code establishes existence).** *"Smallest normal size"* presumes a **SET** of normal retail sizes per ingredient. **D-WS7-197's purchase-size / unit-conversion table shipped July 12, 2026** and is the single source for volume↔weight and count↔weight — **but whether it, or anything, stores a SET of purchasable sizes rather than ONE pack per `Ingredient` row is UNVERIFIED.** ⚠️ **If only one pack is stored, this ruling is unbuildable as written and needs a data source first — do not commission a build that assumes otherwise.**

- ⚠️ **THIRD INSTANCE IN ONE WEEK OF A SINGLE SHAPE: THE CODE IS FINE AND THE DATA IS NOT.** **D-WS9-218** — the component yield's basis unit is stored nowhere, leaving 57 of 95 edges arithmetically undefined. **The A1 edge yields** — the review verified the relations were TRUE and nothing verified the NUMBERS. **And now the stored purchase packs.** 🔴 **Expect the next grocery blocker to be data as well, and scope every Phase 0 to ask what is stored before asking what the code does.**

### D-WS9-222 — 🔵 A retail-size catalog per ingredient — the data D-WS9-221 clause 2 needs and that does not exist

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[SCHEMA]` `[BLOCKER]` · **Date:** September 6, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — measured and named, not solved** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **D-WS9-221 (this is its clause-2 blocker)** · **BUG-124** · **D-WS7-197** · BUG-209 · D-WS9-218 · BUG-096.

- **The gap, measured 2026-09-06 by CC, A2b Phase 0:** *"the smallest normal size to retire the demand"* presumes a **SET** of purchasable sizes per ingredient. **There is exactly ONE pack per ingredient, and no set anywhere.**
  - `Ingredient` columns: `purchaseUnit` / `purchaseQuantity` / `purchaseDisplay` — **one each**. **486 of 1,569 ingredients carry one.**
  - `Ingredient.conversionRef` JSON / `IngredientConversion`: the same three optional scalars — **one each**. 236 rows non-null, **53 of those carry a pack.**
  - 🔴 **Rows holding an ARRAY of packs or sizes: ZERO of 1,569.**
  - `ingredientPurchaseDefaults.ts` is gone — **D-WS7-197 absorbed and deleted it** (shipped July 12, 2026). `INGREDIENT_CONVERSIONS` is the code-table fallback and it is **also one pack per key.**

- ⚠️ **WHAT A2b DID INSTEAD, SO NOBODY MISTAKES IT FOR CLAUSE 2:** `pickPackBasis` ranks only **the packs a merge group already holds** — better-stated size → tighter buy → smaller pack → more informative display → lexicographic. **It chooses among what exists. It cannot propose a size that is not in the data.** Worked example from the live diff: `5 oz parmesan (1 wedge, 6 oz)` + `4 oz parmesan cheese (1 block, 8 oz)` → `9 oz parmesan (1 wedge, 6 oz)`, because **2 wedges = 12 oz beats 2 blocks = 16 oz.** ⚠️ **Still 12 oz bought against a 9 oz need — the tighter of two bad options, because no 10 oz option exists in the data.**

- ⚠️ **BUG-124 ALREADY MEASURED THE CONSEQUENCE AND ITS EVIDENCE IS THE SIZING ARGUMENT FOR THIS WORK:** 13 rows order **more than 2× the need** — Parmesan **6×**, shaved Parmesan 5×, Kalamata olives 4×, olive oil spray 4× — **every one at `packs = 1`, the smallest order the code can emit, with the row pack byte-identical to its stored catalog pack. Cause is the stored pack in 13 of 13; not one row over-scaled.**

- 🔴 **THE HAZARD ANY BUILD HERE MUST DESIGN AROUND, BECAUSE IT IS A CLOSED LOOP.** `fillPurchaseSizesWithWriteBack` fires a Haiku gap-fill for **every row where any of the three pack fields is null**, then **writes the result back to `Ingredient.purchaseUnit` / `purchaseQuantity` / `purchaseDisplay`** — and the consolidator **seeds every row's pack from those same columns.** ⚠️ **So a null pack is not "no pack": it is an AI-invented pack persisted into the shared catalog under the representative's ingredient id, for every future list.** **A2b's guard is `NEVER nulls a pack the group already had`, with a deliberate break behind it. Any clause-2 build must keep a guarantee of that shape.**

- ⚠️ **AND 333 OF 354 UNIVERSAL-STAPLE ROWS CARRY A STORED PACK THAT THE RENDER SUPPRESSES (BUG-171).** Not shopper-visible, but the data underneath is still wrong — and it is why BUG-209 measured five times larger than it rendered. **Any pack-data work must state whether it is fixing what is STORED or what is SHOWN.**

- **Open, and unruled:** where a set of retail sizes would come from — curated, USDA-derived, retailer feed, or an AI pass with human review. ⚠️ **This is the THIRD data-shaped blocker in one week (D-WS9-218's missing basis unit; the A1 edge yields; this). Scope every grocery Phase 0 to ask what is STORED before asking what the code does.**

### D-WS9-223 — 🔵 The SUBSUMES discriminator: does the distinction change the dish? — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 6, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 6, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — the AXIS is ruled; the per-item partition is NOT** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **D-WS9-217 (this is its missing discriminator)** · **D-WS9-221** · D-WS9-189 · BUG-123 · BUG-096.

- **The ruling.** Chat-Claude proposed the axis and Hans confirmed it: *"that sounds right to me."* 🔴 **THE TEST IS WHETHER THE DISTINCTION CHANGES THE DISH — not whether the name is a variety, a grade, or a preparation.** A distinction that changes how the food cooks or eats stays **unfolded**; one that is the same food with a different trim, grade or label **folds**.

- **What it resolves, and it is the reason the axis was sought:** Hans had already ruled this same-looking question in BOTH directions, and nothing named the difference. **Salt — do NOT fold:** *"unfolded, we can leave that as coarse and regular as separate items. if the user wants to sub regular for coarse it's up to them."* **Romaine — DO fold:** *"Romaine lettuce hearts are just romaine in my opinion. If you put 'romaine' or 'romaine hearts' on my list I'd probably look at quality and prices and buy what looks right."* ✅ **Coarse salt seasons differently; romaine hearts are romaine with less trim. The axis explains both without overturning either.**

- ⚠️ **THE AXIS IS RULED. THE 18-ITEM PARTITION IS CHAT-CLAUDE'S APPLICATION OF IT AND IS NOT A RULING.** Chat-Claude offered *"folds parsley, apples, butter and carrots; keeps beans, broth, cherry tomatoes and ground beef"* as illustration. 🔴 **`butter → unsalted butter` is already doubtful on the axis's own terms — salted vs unsalted DOES change a dish, and the fold DIRECTION matters besides (buying unsalted for both works; buying salted for both does not).** **Test every item against the axis and report before applying. Do not treat the illustration as the answer.**

- **Scope, measured September 6 and the reason this is tractable at all:** of **556 `subsumes` rows, only 26 have both endpoints on the same live list.** 530 cannot fold anything that exists. 6 already fold under the shipped synonym reader and hand map; 2 are answered by the salt ruling. **18 open questions, led by `flat-leaf parsley → parsley` (10 lists), `Honeycrisp apples → apples` (7), `lime juice ↔ fresh lime juice` (4), `unsalted butter → butter` (4), `low-sodium chicken broth → chicken broth` (3).**

- 🔴 **AND THE RULE THIS REPLACES FAILED ON MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS WHY THE AXIS IS PHRASED IN FOOD TERMS AND NOT IN FIELDS.** D-WS9-217's *"only collapse when generic demand has no independent purchase"* is a sound principle with **no field to run on**: the only column that could express it is `purchaseDisplay`, **null on 69% of the catalog (1,083 of 1,569)** — and null means *nobody gap-filled that row*, not *no independent purchase*. Operationalised and tested against an independent food axis it produced a **55.9% disagreement rate on 254 scorable rows**, and would have folded `black beans → dried black beans` and `chickpeas → dried chickpeas` **123 times**. ⚠️ **Do not rebuild a subsumes rule on `purchaseDisplay`. It was tested and it failed.**

- ⚠️ **`lime juice ↔ fresh lime juice` is the one where the axis needs a fact before it needs a judgment: is `lime juice` the bottle or the squeezed fruit?** The same question sits behind 27 live lime, 8 lemon and 14 orange rows and was flagged for Hans once before without resolution.

### D-WS9-224 — 🔵 The subsumes fold needs a DIRECTION, not just a ruling — six ruled folds are held on it

- ✅ **BUILT on dev September 28 (grocery B2, `565d138`)** as D-WS9-282's H3 rider: `6 bell peppers, at least 2 green` on the one corpus plan that demanded a plain bell pepper; the qualifier is whole counts in the line's unit; the retailer receives the varieties as separate items.

- ✅ **CONFIRMED September 28, 2026 (D-WS9-282, Hans, verbatim: *"ONLY if there's a meal that says 'bell peppers' would we do '5 bell peppers, at least 2 red and at least 2 yellow'"*):** this rendering applies ONLY when a recipe demanded the plain generic and the generic has no everyday default; named varieties otherwise stay separate lines; shares are whole counts, never a measure.

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 6, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026) — the mechanism is the QUALIFIER; still UNBUILT** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **D-WS9-223** · **D-WS9-217** · D-WS9-189 · BUG-210 · BUG-096.
- ✅ **HANS'S RULING, VERBATIM (September 7, 2026):** *"we ruled a while back that if a set of meals needs '1 bell pepper' and '1 red bell pepper' the grocery list says '2 bell peppers (at least one red)'"* — and, on the generic staying generic: *"if it's generic in the recipe it should stay generic on the grocery list and the user can choose."*
- 🔴 **THIS IS THE DIRECTION MECHANISM THE ENTRY WAS WAITING FOR, AND IT DISSOLVES THE PROBLEM RATHER THAN CHOOSING A SIDE.** The entry's fear was that *"the reader keys on the shortest name and would strip a requirement."* **A qualifier strips nothing: the line takes the GENERIC name — which is what the shopper browses by — and carries the SPECIFIC as a parenthetical requirement.** One line, both demands satisfied, nothing silently re-specified.
- ⚠️ **IT ALSO RECONCILES WITH D-WS9-217 RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING IT.** That entry says *"the surviving row is always the SPECIFIC one"* and calls the direction mechanically forced. **Read at the level of the PURCHASE it is still true — you leave the store holding a red pepper.** What Hans's ruling changes is the LABEL, not the buy: the generic name survives on the line, the specific survives in the qualifier. **A future reader must not take D-WS9-217's sentence as licence to rename the line to the specific.**
- 🔴 **AND A CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE RULING — THE `(at least one red)` DISPLAY DOES NOT EXIST.** Hans remembers it as *"tested and worked."* Searched September 7 before relaying (§27.6 item 10): **zero hits for the qualifier in `kiwi_bug_log.md`, in this log, or in `groceryMerge.ts` / `groceryListAI.ts` / `lib/format/grocery.ts`.** ⚠️ **This is the BUG-171 class exactly — a ruling remembered as shipped.** **The ruling stands and is Hans's to make; the build is owed. Do not commission it as "restore the qualifier."**
- **Scope when it is built:** the qualifier is a RENDER concern, not a new relation label — the fold already knows both names. **The five `keep separate` rulings Hans made the same day are the boundary: `lettuce ⊇ iceberg / romaine / hearts`, `butter ⊇ unsalted`, `brown sugar ⊇ dark`, `diced tomatoes ⊇ fire-roasted`, `chili powder ⊇ ancho`, `salsa ⊇ verde` — where the specific is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT rather than a narrower one, no qualifier and no fold.** ⚠️ **And one case runs the other way: `crusty bread ⊇ sourdough` folds to the GENERIC with no qualifier — Hans: *"could be sourdough, but could be french so it stays generic."*** That is a third shape (fold-to-generic, requirement genuinely dropped because the recipe does not care) and the build must support all three.

- **The gap.** D-WS9-223's axis classifies the 18 live subsumes edges cleanly. **It cannot ship six of them, because the synonym reader keys a cluster on its SHORTEST member** — so `apple ↔ honeycrisp apple` would print **`apple`** and **strip a requirement one recipe actually has.** 🔴 **A fold that discards the specific name is a substitution, and D-WS9-217 ruled the reader does purchase de-duplication, NEVER substitution.**
- **Held on this, all ruled FOLD, all needing the SPECIFIC name to survive:** `apple → honeycrisp apple` · `prosciutto → prosciutto di parma` · `crushed tomatoes → crushed san marzano` · `ground beef → 80/20 ground beef` (**two spellings, one edge**) · `plain greek yogurt → plain whole-milk greek yogurt`.
- **What is needed:** a mechanism where **the demands merge but the more specific name survives** — the inverse of the shortest-name representative rule, applied only where a subsumes edge says the specific carries a requirement the generic does not.
- ✅ **SHIPPED WITHOUT IT: 10 of 12 ruled folds**, where direction does not matter because the two names impose the same requirement — the three citrus-juice pairs, `avocado / ripe avocado`, `carrots / large carrot`, `black beans / canned black beans`.
- ⚠️ **SCOPE, MEASURED SEPTEMBER 6 — THIS IS SMALL AND SHOULD NOT BE OVERSCOPED:** of **556 subsumes rows, only 26 have both endpoints on a live list**; the other **530 fold nothing on any list that exists today.** Six held edges is the entire backlog.

- 🔴 **AND THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THIS ENTRY — A CORRECT FOOD CLASSIFICATION IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A SAFE FOLD.** `fresh parsley ↔ fresh flat-leaf parsley` is one food and the ruling stands. **Applying it widened a merge group onto a `1 bunch` row whose unit has no dimension, `mergeGroup` refused the whole group, and a parsley pair that previously merged into one `0.625 cup` row shipped as `0.5 cup` + `2 tablespoon`. Three rows became four.** Reverted. ⚠️ **THE RULE: FOLDING IS SAFE ONLY WHEN THE MERGED GROUP'S UNITS STILL RECONCILE AFTERWARDS. It was found only by measuring all 53 lists AFTER applying the change — no classification review would have caught it.**

### D-WS9-225 — 🔵 Pack yield is DATA, not a garlic-only constant: the subUnit ladder exists for 1 of 1,569 rows, and 31 count-sold foods are uncomputable for the same reason garlic cloves was

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — measured, unbuilt; the CSV block (D-WS9-226) supplies the data, this is the mechanism** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-215** · **BUG-188 / BUG-213** · D-WS9-220 · D-WS9-218 (🟠 contested — this is NOT the `fromUnit` column) · D-WS9-222 · D-WS9-189.
- **Measured (read-only audit, September 7):** `INGREDIENT_CONVERSIONS` carries exactly ONE `subUnit` entry (garlic: head → 10 cloves), so **1 of 1,569 catalog rows resolves a measured need to a count-pack through a ladder.** Meanwhile **31 rows sell by a count unit against a measured default unit** — green cabbage (head/cup), red cabbage, fresh basil leaves (bunch/cup), fresh chives (bunch/tbsp), broccolini, fresh pineapple, lemon zest… — and every one is uncomputable in the same way `garlic cloves` was in BUG-215. **This is BUG-188's bunch-sold-herb problem generalised past herbs**, and BUG-188's own analysis already named the discriminator: yield per pack.
- **The ruling this asks for (chat-Claude's proposal, licence to refuse):** *yield per pack* becomes a per-ingredient DATA field read by the same ladder code that serves garlic today — `packYield {unit, perPack}` — populated from `pack_yields.csv` (Hans's evening pass) and required at intake for any ingredient whose pack unit and default unit differ in dimension. **The garlic constant becomes the first row of that table, not a special case.** ⚠️ **Not D-WS9-218's column**: that proposed a basis unit on the *relation*; this puts the yield on the *ingredient*, where the pack lives, and the component pool keeps reading relations as it does now.
- ⚠️ **Do not build the ladder generalisation before BUG-215's survivor fix** — a ladder that lives on the ingredient is only as good as the fold's choice of ingredient.
- ✅ **HANS'S FIGURES, RULED September 7, 2026, and they are the data this entry was asking for.** A supermarket herb bunch is **~1 oz** — that one number resolves 17 of the low-confidence rows. A bunch yields **2 cups of leaves uncut, 1 cup chopped**, and *"1 cup cilantro"* with no cut named means **leaves and stems as bought, which the user cuts per the recipe.** Celery **8 stalks/bunch** · pineapple **4 cups of chunks** (⚠️ **NOT USDA's 905 g, which is the whole fruit including skin and core — the shipped gate would have taken it**) · watermelon: a recipe's *pound* means **flesh, ~6 lb of a ~10 lb melon** · American cheese **¾ oz supermarket single, not the 1 oz deli slice** · chicken halves: the 4 lb pack is **one bird, two halves, ~2 lb each**.
- 🔴 **AND ONE ANSWER THAT IS NOT A FIGURE AT ALL, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING.** Asked for a grams-per-bunch for `fennel fronds`, Hans ruled the row out of existence: *"I don't think there's a need to put fronds on a list. tops are part of the bulb and come with it."* **A part that arrives free with its parent must never generate its own purchase line — and the mechanism for that already exists and is not a pack figure: a `component` relation with `coHarvestable = true`, exactly as lemon zest rides along with the lemon.** ⚠️ **So a `pack_dimension_straddle` is TWO different defects wearing one label: a missing yield figure, or a missing co-harvest relation. Ask which before pricing anything.** **Sweep the 31 straddlers for the second kind before authoring figures for them** — herb stems, zests, tops, trimmings and fronds are all candidates.

### D-WS9-226 — 🔵 Ingredient INTAKE: a new row must arrive computable or flagged — never with an AI pack sized to one plan's need and written back catalog-wide

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` `[SCHEMA]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — Phase 0 DONE and the product decision RULED (b) September 7; ready to commission after the grocery P1 block** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-124** (the writer) · **D-WS9-225** · D-WS9-222 · D-WS9-224 · BUG-188 · D-WS9-214 (precedent, see refutation) · D-WS9-181.
- **Hans's question, verbatim (September 6):** *"if we get a new ingredient from a wizard or import meal, will it get picked up and processed appropriately by the current rules?"* **Measured answer: NO.** One runtime creation point (`ingredientResolve`), reached from manual meal/dish save + PATCH, recipe import, the wizard and store-fill (Tell Kiwi does not reach it); **nothing at runtime writes `ingredient_relations`, nothing outside the seed writes `ingredient_aliases`** — two search shapes each, gitignore-blind, raw SQL checked. A new row gets: name · keyword-inferred category · the first mention's unit · a pack only if one of 58 static names hits · fire-and-forget USDA nutrition · **no `conversionRef`, no relations, no aliases, ever.** Catalog today: 1,078 null packs (68.7%), 236 `conversionRef` (15%), 1 `subUnit`.
- 🔴 **THE PRECEDENT REFUTED:** the handoff proposed copying D-WS9-214's *"deterministic baseline + AI pass at creation, unioned."* **There is no ingredient-level allergen path** — `Ingredient` has no allergen column; allergens are stamped on `Meal` by a pure function over names. The SHAPE (deterministic first, AI second, unioned, flagged) still applies; the CODE cannot be copied.
- **The design (chat-Claude's calls, delegated; Hans may object):** (1) **`Ingredient.createdAt` / `updatedAt`** — absent today, so intake cannot be measured at all; cheapest first fix. (2) **`Ingredient.packSource`** enum `static | csv | ai_gapfill | user` + **`packReviewedAt`** — `reviewedByHuman` exists only on `IngredientRelation`; the BUG-096 review lives in a CSV, not the catalog. (3) **The gap-fill stops receiving the asking plan's need** — it asks for the smallest common retail pack of the food, not a pack for `requestedQuantity`; the result persists with `packSource = ai_gapfill` so it is visible, reviewable and exportable, never mistaken for a fact. (4) **An idempotent CSV load script** for `pack_sizes.csv`, `pack_yields.csv`, `subsumes_direction.csv`, `unit_conversions.csv`, keyed on the stable ids in column 1, writing `packSource = csv`. (5) **A standing export of `packSource = ai_gapfill` rows** so the next evening pass is a list, not a hunt.
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026): (b).** When a brand-new ingredient has no reviewed pack, the shopper sees the retail-shaped AI proposal, persisted as `packSource = ai_gapfill` **with the asking plan's need removed from the prompt** (option (a), the need-only staple-style line, was the alternative). **AND — Hans's addition, verbatim: *"it should try and also in the future send me an email to review if needed."*** So the standing export of `ai_gapfill` rows (design item 5) is not a file Hans goes looking for: **when unreviewed `ai_gapfill` rows exist, he gets an email listing them** — mechanism to be chosen in the build (a scheduled task that reads the export, or the api-server sending via Resend once row 3a lands); either way the trigger is *rows exist*, not a calendar.
- ⚠️ **Sequencing:** BUG-214 + BUG-215 + BUG-216 first (the P1 block); then this block, whose CSV load can be built before the CSVs are filled and run when they are. **Every write in this block runs on a Neon branch first** (D-WS9-181's mechanism, per the September 7 acceleration review).
- 🔴 **MEASURED September 7, 2026 — THE RECURRING-ITEM POPULATION IS THE WORST-SERVED IN THE CATALOG, AND A `pack_class` FILTER WOULD HAVE MISSED ALL OF IT.** Of the 9 recurring rows on one live list: **2 packs came from the static default table; 7 are Haiku gap-fills; and 4 of those 7 carry a NULL `ingredientId`, so there is nowhere to write the answer back and they are re-asked on EVERY generation, forever** (`coffee`, `pet treats`, `paper towels`, `toilet paper`). ⚠️ **Meanwhile `pack_class` scores the recurring set 0 null and 0 need-shaped — it looks clean, because the classification is keyed on CATALOG ROWS and four of these lines have no catalog row at all.**
- ✅ **SO THE CSV PASS GROUPS RECURRING ITEMS BY PACK PROVENANCE, NOT BY `pack_class`** — static / catalog / `ai_gapfill` / no-row-at-all. **That is also the argument for `packSource` being a column rather than a derived guess:** the thing that identifies a bad pack is where it came from, and today that is only recoverable by re-deriving three separate lookups per row.
- 🔴 **AND THE INTAKE PROBLEM IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — IT FIRED DURING THE VERIFICATION ITSELF.** Hans built one meal through the mode-A parser and it minted **`onion` and `diced onion` as separate catalog rows with separate fold keys**, putting **four onion rows** on one list (`White onion`, `Yellow onion`, `onion`, `diced onion`). ⚠️ **`diced onion` is a PREP MODIFIER that became a catalog row.** The same meal left three ground-beef rows. **This is the intake path manufacturing exactly the duplicate-name population D-WS9-189 has spent the arc folding away — one meal, six new rows of it.** ⚠️ **Any intake fix that does not normalise prep modifiers out of the ingredient name will keep feeding the fold work it should never have been given.**
- ⚠️ **Two catalog-drift instances found in passing, both BUG-124's shape:** `limes` resolves to catalog `lime` whose pack reads `"2 limes"` but the row renders `"1 lime"`; and catalog `bananas` holds `"1 banana"` while the curated static default for it says `"1 bunch"` — **a catalog row that has drifted away from the table it was seeded from.**

✅ **`unit_conversions.csv` REVIEW CLOSED — HANS RULED ALL FOUR OPEN ROWS, September 8, 2026.** ⚠️ **The review surface was **51 rows**, not the 55 canon had been carrying — "51 low + 4 refusals" double-counted, because all four refusals ARE low-confidence rows.** Chat-Claude read all 51; 47 cleared, including the two highest-reach (chipotle in adobo ×19 live rows at 12 g, bay leaves ×10 at 0.2 g).
- ✅ **`whole chicken halves` = 907 g each — the lane's assumption was RIGHT.** Hans: *"2 halves per 4 lbs of chicken halves. If I need 4 halves, I need 8 lbs."* **The row is confirmed, not corrected** — worth recording because the lane explicitly flagged it as a coin-flip that would have been a clean 2× error the other way.
- ✅ **`hoagie rolls` = 57 g → **106 g** (Hans: *"106, medium"*).** 🔴 **THE LANE'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, NOT JUST ITS NUMBER: it wrote *"USDA carries no record for hoagie rolls"* and reached for SR Legacy's "Rolls, hard (includes kaiser), 3½″ dia" = 57 g. USDA FNDDS food code 51157000 "Roll, submarine, hoagie, white" DOES exist and carries three per-roll weights — 73 g small (5½″), 106 g medium (8″), 153 g large (11½″).** ⚠️ **VERIFIED VIA A USDA MIRROR (nutritionvalue.org), NOT A DIRECT FDC READ — the loading block confirms the food code before writing the value.** 🔵 **THE TRANSFERABLE PART: a "no USDA record" negative from ONE database view is a §27.3 single-grep negative. SR Legacy and FNDDS are different corpora; the ladder pass searched one and concluded the food was absent.**
- ✅ **`fennel fronds` — KEEP 7 tbsp per bunch, and fix the REAL problem with a component edge, not a number (Hans).** His constraint, verbatim: *"I don't want to have a fennel bulb for shaved fennel and a fennel bulb for the fronds on the same grocery list."* 🔵 **That is exactly what the D-WS9-189 A3 component pool already does for garlic (2 heads → 17 cloves, LIVE): fronds are a COMPONENT of the bulb, so a frond need is satisfied from the bulb already on the list and no second bulb appears.** ⚠️ **MEASURED September 8: `fennel fronds` has ZERO relations and ZERO aliases, so nothing connects it to a bulb today, and no row in the 260-row CSV references fennel at all.** 🔴 **UNVERIFIED AND IT GATES THE FIX: whether a `fennel bulb` catalog row EXISTS is not answerable from this CSV (it is a 260-row subset of ~1,569). One catalog query settles it — if there is no bulb row, the edge has nothing to attach to.** ✅ **7 tbsp/bunch stays as the fallback for a recipe that needs fronds with no bulb on the list. Blast radius is 1 live row, so this is cheap either way.**
- ✅ **THE FOUR REFUSALS ARE PERMANENTLY BLANK, NOT A GAP TO FILL — Hans ruled the rows out of mass consolidation entirely.** Verbatim: *"applewood chips are wood, toothpicks/skewers are also wood (and skewers could be metal)… we don't need to consolidate those rows."* 🔴 **WRITE THAT DOWN EXPLICITLY, BECAUSE AN EMPTY CELL LOOKS LIKE UNFINISHED WORK: a future pass must not try to invent grams for these four. The blanks ARE the answer.**
- ✅ **AND HANS NAMED THE PRODUCT REASON THEY SHOULD STAY VISIBLE AS THEIR OWN LINES:** *"I saw a recipe that told me to buy skewers, which was great to see - they're like an uncommon not staple thing that people often have, but should confirm before they sign up to make kebabs."* 🔵 **So the requirement is the opposite of consolidation: surface them as countable, checkable rows. Their packs already support it — `1 box (100 count)`, `1 package (8-12 count)` — which is why the gram conversion was never needed.**
- ⚠️ **NO NEW SECTION IS REQUIRED. PRD §12.4's `Household` section already exists for "cleaners, paper goods, pet supplies, etc." and is where these belong.** 🔴 **They are NOT there today — see BUG-232, which this review turned from a one-row cosmetic into a measured class.**

### D-WS9-227 — 🔵 A shopper can change how MUCH, never WHAT — the grocery row exposes quantity and a cosmetic label, and nothing else

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[UX]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — measured and named; the product decision is Hans's and is NOT yet made** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-226** (the case that surfaced it) · **BUG-124** · D-WS9-222 · D-WS9-226 · BUG-225.
- **Hans, verbatim (device pass, September 7):** *"grocery list items are not editable easily (it either checks it as measured or edits the quantity needed and units). it doesn't allow a user to change what's being purchased."*
- ✅ **HIS READING IS CORRECT, AND THE CONSTRAINT IS IN THE SCHEMA AND THE ROUTE CONTRACT, NOT JUST THE UI.** Measured from code, September 7: the item PATCH accepts **eight** fields — `isChecked`, `quantity`, `unit`, `stapleOptedIn`, `storeSection`, `displayName`, `userResolvedTo`, `acknowledgeAmbiguity` — **the client sends five of them**, and every mutation funnels through `AppContext` (no screen calls the API layer directly).
- **What a shopper CAN do:** tick and untick · edit quantity and unit · opt a staple in for the week · resolve or acknowledge an ambiguity · add an extra row · remove a row · undo the removal · mark the shop complete.
- 🔴 **WHAT NOBODY CAN DO, AND THE THREE REASONS ARE DIFFERENT:** ① **the ingredient identity** — `ingredientId` is settable on ADD and absent from the update schema, so once a row exists the ingredient it points at is fixed and **no route repoints it**; ② **the pack** — `purchaseUnit` / `purchaseQuantity` / `purchaseDisplay` are in **no input schema anywhere**, and the schema comment states the rule: **the pack is DERIVED and reconcile regenerates it, the need is AUTHORED** — so it is deliberately non-user-authored and an edit would be overwritten; ③ **swapping one product for another** — the nearest affordance is the Clarify sheet, and it writes `userResolvedTo`, **a display string**. ⚠️ **You can relabel what the row SAYS. You cannot re-point what it IS** — `ingredientId`, the pack and the conversion basis all stay put.
- ⚠️ **TWO FIELDS THE SERVER ACCEPTS AND NO CLIENT EVER SENDS: `displayName` (read path only, zero write sites) and `storeSection` (sent on ADD, never on UPDATE — so a generated row cannot be moved between aisles).** **That is latent surface, not a feature: either wire it deliberately or drop it from the schema.**
- 🔴 **THE QUESTION FOR HANS, AND IT IS A PRODUCT CALL, NOT A BUG:** when the list says something a shopper knows is wrong — `1 quart` of milk, a pack that is not what they buy — **what should they be able to do about it in the moment?** The options are genuinely different in cost and in blast radius: **(a)** nothing, and the fix is always the catalog (today's behaviour; requires D-WS9-226's review loop to be trustworthy); **(b)** a per-list override that changes this row only and never touches the catalog; **(c)** a correction that writes back to the catalog for that user; **(d)** a correction that proposes a catalog change for review — the same shape as `ai_gapfill`, but sourced from a human who is standing in the aisle.
- ⚠️ **DO NOT BUILD ANY OF THEM YET.** (c) and (d) both re-open BUG-124's exact hazard — a value derived from one person's situation persisted as a product fact — and (b) collides with the reconcile pass that regenerates the pack. **The ruling must come before the build, and D-WS9-226's intake work should land first so the catalog side is trustworthy.**

### D-WS9-228 — 🔵 A recurring staple's default names the GRADE the recipes assume — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[GROCERY]` `[CATALOG]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — the axis is settled; the per-food application is NOT** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-225** (the eggs instance) · **BUG-226** (the milk instance, still open) · D-WS9-226 · D-WS9-221 · D-WS9-223.
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"I always buy (at least almost always) and mostly only see Grade A Large eggs and some Grade A Extra Large eggs. Maybe I'm incorrect, but I feel like Large Eggs is what people buy... I think that means the recurring eggs should default to 1 dozen large eggs. am I thinking that through correctly? is there sales data to support the idea that large eggs is what everyone gets?"*
- ✅ **THE RULING: when a food is sold in GRADED SIZES and the recipe corpus assumes one grade, the recurring staple's default names THAT GRADE, in the pack size it is normally sold in.** Eggs: **`1 dozen Large`.**
- 🔴 **THE JUSTIFICATION IS RECIPE CONVENTION, NOT MARKET SHARE — AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS.** Chat-Claude searched for the sales-share statistic Hans asked for and **did not find one**: USDA's shell-egg reports carry prices and movement by size band but publish no retail share, and the consumer sources are explainer articles. ⚠️ **NO SHARE FIGURE IS RECORDED ANYWHERE IN CANON AND NONE MAY BE CITED LATER AS IF IT WERE MEASURED.** ✅ **The ruling does not need one.** The American recipe convention is that an unqualified *"2 eggs"* means **2 large eggs** — so Large is the size the app's own recipe math already assumes, and a shopper who buys Large is never wrong against a Kiwi recipe. **That argument is stronger than a share figure would have been, because it ties the default to something the product controls rather than to consumer behaviour it does not.**
- ⚠️ **THE TEST FOR APPLYING IT ELSEWHERE — and it is deliberately narrow.** A food qualifies only if **(i)** it is sold in named grades or sizes AND **(ii)** the recipe corpus has a default grade it assumes silently. **Eggs pass. Most foods do NOT** — an onion is not graded, and *"1 lb of chicken"* names a weight, not a grade. ⚠️ **Do not turn this into a licence to pick a "standard" size for every ungraded food; that is D-WS9-221's job (smallest normal size that retires the demand) and it answers a different question.**
- 🔴 **IT IS AN ALIAS-PRECEDENCE CHANGE, NOT A FOLD, AND THE `distinct` EDGE STANDS.** Measured September 7: `egg` (`179e8716`) and `Large eggs` (`ff985025`) are separate catalog rows joined by a deliberate high-confidence **`distinct`** edge, and the recurring preference string `egg` lands on the generic row because **a canonical name always beats an alias**. ⚠️ **This ruling changes only WHICH ROW THE RECURRING STRING RESOLVES TO. It does NOT authorise deleting the `distinct` edge, folding the two rows, or a subsumes pass on graded foods** — D-WS9-223's discriminator (*does the distinction change the dish?*) is untouched by it.
- ⚠️ **AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE BUG-225.** Even with the recurring row resolved to Large, two adjacent lines can still both open *"1 dozen"* for unrelated reasons. **The unrelatable-pack render is still the defect of record.**
- ✅ **COMMISSIONED September 29, 2026 — grocery B3 (D-WS9-284 rule 4):** a recurring-only grade map (`egg` / `eggs` → `large eggs`) applied after the non-creating lookup; the `distinct` edge and both catalog rows untouched. B3 Part A measured why the canonical-first precedence defeated it: a row named `egg` exists (39 recipes), and the `egg → large eggs` alias is shadowed by it.
- ⚠️ **UNBUILT. NOT COMMISSIONED.** The ruling is recorded so the CSV pass and the intake work (D-WS9-226) can apply it to the recurring group; **no block has been written for it, and the alias-precedence code has not been read.** Whoever commissions it reads `ingredientResolve`'s precedence first and reports before editing.

### D-WS9-229 — 🔵 The grocery-generate limiter's BUDGET is reasoned, not priced — and it will hit Hans's own device passes before it ever hits an attacker — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9A]` `[COST]` `[UX]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9A · **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 7 — all three questions answered; the BUDGET ships as committed, the ESCAPE HATCH and the MESSAGE are UNBUILT** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-222** (the limiter) · BUG-223 · D-WS9-181 · D-WS9-226.
- **What shipped, at CC's own declaration that it is a reasoned number and not a priced one:** `POST /api/plans/:id/generate-grocery-list` gets **capacity 4, refill 4 per 300 s, keyed on `userId`.** Placed against the existing ladder: `mutationLimiter` 60/min (cheap writes) · assist/recalc/prepWeek 12/min (mid-tier AI) · `wizardLimiter` 8/min (the tightest existing AI tier). **Half the wizard's burst, refilling 5× slower, because canon calls this the most expensive request the server serves.**
- 🔴 **CC COULD NOT PRICE A SINGLE GENERATE AND SAID SO.** Pricing needs a live AI call or an `LLMCallLog` read; **both were barred in the block.** ⚠️ **So the number is calibrated by RELATIVE POSITION IN A LADDER, not by dollars — and the ladder itself has never been priced either.** **Do not describe this budget as cost-based.**
- 🔴 **THE NEAR-TERM CONSEQUENCE IS NOT AN ATTACKER, IT IS HANS. A device pass that regenerates repeatedly gets 429 after four, then one per 75 seconds** — and a 429 on his screen mid-test reads as a defect, not as a limiter working. ⚠️ **This is the §27 pattern exactly: if the product owner misreads it, a beta user will.** **Nobody should run a grocery device pass without knowing this.**
- **The decision, and it is three questions, not one:**
  1. **Is 4 burst / 4-per-5-min the right BETA budget** for a friends-and-family group, or is it tuned for a public URL that does not exist yet?
  2. **Should there be a dev/test escape** — an env-gated non-firing bucket, the same DI seam the suites already use — so device passes and local work are not throttled? ⚠️ **An escape hatch that can be set in production is worse than no limiter; if this is built, it must be impossible to enable on a deployed instance.**
  3. **What is the USER-FACING behaviour at the limit?** Today it is a bare 429 from a route the app calls during a generating overlay. **A limiter with no message is a hang.**
- ⚠️ **THE REAL FIX IS THE ONE THIS ONE STANDS IN FOR, AND BUG-222 SAYS SO: there is no per-user AI SPEND CEILING anywhere in the server**, and `GET /api/wizard/limits` reports a cap it does not enforce. **A rate limiter bounds requests per minute; it does not bound money.** ✅ **Ship the limiter now — it is strictly better than nothing — but do not let it close the spend question.**
- ✅ **ONE PART NEEDS NO RULING AND SHOULD NOT BE REOPENED: the key is `userId`, not `ip`, deliberately.** Under BUG-223 an IP key collapses behind Cloud Run's front end, **which on this route would let one user's regenerate exhaust everyone's.** A per-user key is immune whatever `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` becomes.
- ✅ **HANS'S RULING, September 7, 2026 — ALL THREE, YES.**
  1. ✅ **The budget stands: 4 burst, 4 per 300 s, per user, for beta.** No change to `fa1859c`.
  2. ✅ **BUILD THE DEV ESCAPE HATCH**, env-gated, using the DI seam the suites already use. 🔴 **AND THE CONSTRAINT IS PART OF THE RULING, NOT A CAVEAT: it must be IMPOSSIBLE to enable on a deployed instance.** An escape hatch a production env var can flip is worse than no limiter at all.
  3. ✅ **AND THE MESSAGE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, BECAUSE HANS REFRAMED THE WHOLE THING.**
- 🔴 **THE DURABLE INSIGHT: A RATE-LIMIT MESSAGE SHOULD DIAGNOSE THE PRODUCT, NOT SCOLD THE USER.** Hans's copy, verbatim: *"Kiwi seems to be missing the mark, please refine your preferences or use the 'Tell Kiwi' option with more details about what you'd like to eat."* And his statement of intent, verbatim: *"Basically 'hey, if you're messing around and using tokens for fun, please stop. and if this really isn't getting you what you want, try something else'."*
- ✅ **WHY THAT IS BETTER THAN A LIMIT NOTICE, AND THE REASONING GENERALISES TO EVERY LIMIT IN THE APP: someone regenerating five times in ten minutes is telling you the plan is wrong, not that they love clicking.** A message that says *"slow down"* answers the server's problem; **a message that says *"this isn't working for you — here is the path that will"* answers the USER'S problem and reduces the load as a side effect.** ⚠️ **The `Tell Kiwi` pointer is the load-bearing half — it names the cheaper, better route instead of leaving a dead end.**
- 🔴 **CHAT-CLAUDE SAID "WITHOUT THE MESSAGE THE LIMITER IS A SILENT HANG." THAT IS REFUTED BY THE DEVICE, September 7, 2026.** Hans drained the bucket (~5 presses) and the app showed **"something went wrong, please try again in a moment."** ⚠️ **The client has a generic error path and it caught the 429.** ✅ **So item 3 is a COPY improvement on a working error state, not a rescue from a spinner — a smaller and less urgent job than this entry claimed.** ⚠️ **§27's rule again: a UI claim asserted from a route contract, without opening the client's error path.**
- 🔵 **AND HANS'S SECOND PASS AT THE COPY, WRITTEN AFTER SEEING IT FIRE, DIFFERS FROM HIS FIRST — WHICH IS INFORMATION, NOT INDECISION.** Verbatim: *"Kiwi is having trouble with your grocery list and needs a rest. Please wait a few minutes and try again."* **The first version diagnoses the USER'S SITUATION (the plan is missing the mark — try Tell Kiwi); the second states the SYSTEM'S STATE and the recovery (wait, then retry).**
- ✅ **THEY ARE NOT COMPETING DRAFTS — THEY ANSWER THE TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS A PERSON HAS AT THAT MOMENT, IN ORDER: "is it broken and what do I do now?" then "why does it keep happening?"** ⚠️ **A message that only diagnoses gives no recovery; a message that only says wait leaves them regenerating again in five minutes.** 🔵 **WORKING SHAPE, PENDING HANS'S CONFIRM: the recovery first, the diagnosis second** — *"Kiwi needs a short rest — please try again in a few minutes. If the plans aren't hitting the mark, refining your preferences or using Tell Kiwi will get you there faster than regenerating."*
- ⚠️ **Do not ship the limiter to a beta user without item 3** — the current copy is truthful but says nothing about the cause or the cure.
- ⚠️ **UNBUILT: items 2 and 3 are ruled and NOT commissioned.** ✅ **Item 1 is already in `fa1859c`.** **The limiter itself is live in the tree, so item 3 is now the highest-priority piece of this entry — a device pass can produce the silent-hang state today.**
- ⚠️ **STILL OPEN AND NOT ANSWERED BY THIS RULING: the per-user AI SPEND CEILING (BUG-222's product half).** A rate limiter bounds requests per minute; **it does not bound money.**
