### D-WS9-230 — 🔵 NO BACKFILLS. Fixes are FORWARD-ONLY, and Hans's existing data is disposable — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026)**

- **Tags:** `[WS9]` `[WS9A]` `[SCOPE]` `[PROCESS]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** every block from here · **Status:** ✅ **RULED — binding on commissioning** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-186** (which first split forward fixes from historical backfills) · D-WS9-203 · D-WS9-184 · D-WS7-219 · BUG-231 · BUG-232 · BUG-096.
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"on any fixes, there is NO NEED to backfill or fix data. I can test on new plans for everything. and it's all my data and no one else is in there, so bad data is fine for me to ignore."*
- ✅ **THE RULING: a fix ships when NEW data comes out right. Existing plans, lists, meals and imports are NOT repaired, NOT migrated and NOT audited for residue.** **Verification is "generate a fresh plan and look", never "re-run the corpus."**
- 🔴 **THIS IS A LARGE, PERMANENT SCOPE REDUCTION AND IT SHOULD BE APPLIED AGGRESSIVELY.** This project has repeatedly built a fix and then built a second thing to repair what the bug already wrote — review sheets, dry-run/apply merge scripts, residue-rate gates, 53-list re-measurements. ⚠️ **A large share of that was serving a corpus of ONE developer's throwaway test plans.** ✅ **Pre-launch, with no other users, the corpus has no value worth an engineering hour.**
- 🔴 **THE CARVE-OUT, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL — DO NOT READ THIS RULING AS "NEVER WRITE DATA AGAIN."** Two different things are called "data" here:
  - **USER-SCOPED data — plans, grocery lists, meals, imported recipes. THIS is what the ruling releases.** It belongs to Hans, no one else has any, and he throws it away by making a new plan.
  - 🔴 **THE SHARED INGREDIENT CATALOG (1,569 rows), its relations, aliases and packs, is NOT user-scoped and is NOT covered.** **Every future user inherits it on day one.** ⚠️ **D-WS9-226's CSV load, the pack-size work and the relationship program are PRODUCT DATA and remain in scope exactly as ruled.** **A chat that cancels the CSV load citing this entry has misread it.**
- ⚠️ **THE TEST, when it is unclear which side something falls on: WOULD A NEW USER SIGNING UP TOMORROW INHERIT THIS ROW?** If yes it is catalog and it gets fixed. If no it is Hans's scratch and it gets ignored.
- ✅ **IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCES, already applied:** **BUG-231** (`onion` / `diced onion`) needs the INTAKE fix only — **the four onion rows on Hans's current lists are not to be cleaned up.** **BUG-232** (`Celery Seed` in Produce) is a catalog-side classification and **stays in scope, because a new user inherits it.**
- ⚠️ **IT ALSO CHANGES WHAT A DEVICE SCRIPT ASKS FOR: "generate a NEW plan and check" replaces "open your existing list and confirm the old rows changed."** Several past scripts asked the second question and got confusing answers for exactly this reason.
- 🔵 **AND ONE THING IT DOES NOT LICENSE: it is not permission to ship a fix unverified.** **Forward-only means the ACCEPTANCE TEST runs on new data, not that there is no acceptance test.**

**✅ AMENDMENT — September 14, 2026: THE RULING EXTENDS FROM DATA TO THE SCHEDULE. A BROKEN APP FOR A FEW DAYS IS AN ACCEPTABLE COST OF A FASTER ROUTE.**

- **Hans, verbatim:** *"this is a meal planning app, so I'm not like actively using it. I just test there and have done some weekly meal plans and grocery lists to kick the tires… chats often forget that breaking something temporarily is ok for now because this is development mode until we actually go on an app store… if that impacts our build approach to be more efficient in the delivery of what's on the roadmap it's ok for the app to be unusable for a couple days at a time if necessary."*
- 🔴 **WHAT IS NEW: the original ruling released HIS DATA. This releases THE SEQUENCE.** The entry above already said his plans are disposable; chats kept honouring a second, unwritten constraint — *keep the app working at every commit* — and paid for it in lane splits, feature flags and extra round trips. **That constraint is lifted until the App Store submission.**
- ✅ **WHAT IT LICENSES, named so a chat can act on it without re-asking:** a rewrite may REPLACE a flow rather than run beside it (no dual-path scaffolding, no feature flag, no compatibility shim built only to keep the old path alive) · a lane may land in a knowingly broken intermediate state and be fixed by the next lane · a sequence may be split by WHAT IS EFFICIENT TO BUILD rather than by what keeps the app usable — **the D-WS9-239 1a/1b/1c split was partly the second, and a comparable split in future should be justified by build cost or measurement, not by user-visible inertness** · device testing belongs at the END of a sequence, not between every step · **a schema change may drop or reshape a column carrying only user-scoped rows without a migration path for them.**
- 🔴 **WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH, AND THE LINE IS NOT "USER-VISIBLE" — IT IS REVERSIBLE vs EXPENSIVE-TO-UNDO.** There are no users on either surface, so "don't break the app" was never the real boundary. What still binds: **the SHARED INGREDIENT CATALOG and the 1,872-meal catalog** (the carve-out above — every future user inherits those rows, and a wrong write costs a repair pass, which is the thing this entry exists to prevent) · **anything that cannot be taken back**: the Play Store application id, a published store build, a live sending domain, a deleted column whose content is catalog · **the audit gate (§3) and acceptance (the clause directly above)** — speed comes from sequencing, never from skipping the check that catches the wrong build.
- ⚠️ **SO A MEASUREMENT GATE IS NOT THE THING BEING RELAXED.** D-WS9-239's fresh-20 gate protects the **catalog**, not Hans's comfort: 1c writes tags onto shared meals. **Read a gate's purpose before citing this amendment at it.**
- 🔴 **REFINED BY HANS THE SAME DAY, AND IT IS THE HALF A CHAT WILL GET WRONG IF IT READS ONLY THE LICENCE ABOVE.** Verbatim: *"the big thing, and where I should be inserted into a defined run, is if we're building something that benefits from a build checkpoint or validation partway through to reduce variables if it's broken when I get to testing."* ✅ **THE DISTINCTION, STATED ONCE: a checkpoint that exists to keep the APP USABLE is dropped. A checkpoint that exists to ISOLATE A VARIABLE before Hans tests is KEPT — and named explicitly in the sequence, with what it proves.** ⚠️ **Going faster is not the same as handing him a finished pile he has to bisect.** A stop before an irreversible or expensive step (a catalog write, a spend, a store submission) is the same class and stays for the same reason.
- ✅ **AND ON THE CATALOG, HANS, VERBATIM: *"it's less the $17, and more making sure we're doing the right thing."*** **The carve-out above is not a budget rule and must not be argued down with a cost figure.**
- ✅ **CC MAY NOW RUN `prisma:seed` ITSELF (Hans, September 14).** The reseed was the main thing stopping a lane mid-flight for a round trip through his terminal — 1b cost three. ⚠️ **Disclosed when he ruled it and still true: the seed also upserts the 12 recipe rows and the ingredient rows, so it touches CATALOG — idempotent, deterministic from a file in the repo, and it has run many times, but it is a catalog write and it is the one place this permission brushes the carve-out.** **Migrations are unchanged — `prisma migrate deploy` stays DENIED to CC and Hans runs them (§2).**
- ✅ **AND IT RETIRES A CLASS OF PARAGRAPH FROM CHAT MESSAGES AND CANON ALIKE:** *"note that plans generated between X and Y may read wrong"*. **Hans does not need to be warned about his own scratch data.** State the live-DB fact once if a chat must not misread it, never as a caution to him.

### D-WS9-231 — 🔵 `kiwi://` custom-scheme links do not survive email, and every link the app mints is one — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 7, 2026): https fallback page now, universal links later — and they are the SAME URL**

- **Tags:** `[WS9A]` `[AUTH]` `[MOBILE]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Owner:** the auth+email block · **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 7 — option 2 (https + web fallback), with option 1 as the later upgrade on the same URLs** · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-235** (the client that would consume it) · **BUG-224** · BUG-233 · D-WS7-022.
- **CC, auth+email Phase 0, flagged unprompted:** both mail-bearing flows mint **`kiwi://…`** URLs — `kiwi://reset-password?token=…` and `kiwi://verify-email?token=…` — **and neither has ever been through a real mail client, because neither has ever been sent.**
- 🔴 **A CUSTOM SCHEME IS THE ONE LINK SHAPE EMAIL IS WORST AT.** Many clients decline to linkify a non-`http(s)` scheme, some strip it, and **if the app is not installed the link is simply inert — no store page, no web fallback, nothing.** ⚠️ **The user experience of a failure here is a link that visibly does nothing, on the one email whose entire job is to rescue a locked-out account.**
- ⚠️ **THE EXISTING EVIDENCE PROVES THE WRONG THING AND MUST NOT BE MISREAD: `kiwi://verify-email` works — from a device, where something already resolved the scheme.** **That says the ROUTER is wired. It says nothing about whether Gmail will render the link.**
- **The decision, and there are three real options:**
  1. **`https://` universal / app links** — the app opens if installed, the web page loads if not. 🔴 **Costs a live domain and a hosted `apple-app-site-association` (plus the Android asset-links file), so it is gated on the same DNS session as everything else — and it is the only option that degrades gracefully.**
  2. **`https://` link to a plain web fallback page that then hands off to the app** — cheaper, one page, works everywhere, one extra hop for the user.
  3. **Keep `kiwi://`** — free, and accepts that some recipients get a dead link. ⚠️ **Defensible for a friends-and-family beta where Hans can talk someone through it; indefensible at launch.**
- 🔴 **IT GATES BUG-235's BUILD RATHER THAN FOLLOWING IT.** The deep-link target screen, the token hand-off and the fallback behaviour all differ by option. **Building the client first and choosing after means building it twice.**
- ⚠️ **AND IT COMPOSES WITH THE `PUBLIC_APP_URL` GAP: options 1 and 2 both need an https host the server can build links from, and no such variable exists** (see BUG-228's env contract).
- ✅ **HANS RULED OPTION 2, September 7, 2026** — *"fallback page is fine"* — and asked the right follow-up: **why not build universal links now?**
- 🔴 **THE ANSWER IS THAT UNIVERSAL LINKS ARE NOT A DIFFERENT LINK, THEY ARE THE SAME URL PLUS THREE THINGS THAT DO NOT EXIST YET.** The email carries `https://<host>/reset-password?token=…` in BOTH options. **The upgrade is hosting two association files and shipping a build that claims the domain — the email, the route, the token and the server change NOT AT ALL.** ✅ **So option 2 is not a detour that gets thrown away; it is the foundation, and the migration is additive.**

### D-WS9-232 — 🔵 `stoveType` and the dead-preference-field audit: remove what nothing reads — and check the schema DEFAULT before removing anything

- **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[ONBOARDING]` `[SCHEMA]` `[AUDIT]` · **Date:** September 8, 2026 · **Owner:** the WS9 redesign / onboarding pass · **Status:** 🔵 **OPEN — Hans's intent is stated; the audit has not been run** · **Cross-ref:** PRD §3.5 · **D-WS7-190** (`wantsLeftovers` — the precedent that makes this dangerous) · D-WS9-207.
- **Hans, September 8, 2026:** user preferences carry a **stove type** (electric / gas / induction); he does not believe it does much of anything and wants it out of the layout **to reduce onboarding friction** — *"it's worth confirming there are no extra fields that don't really do anything when we do that."* **The audit is the larger half of the ask.**
- **What canon establishes and what it does not.** PRD §3.5 specs `stoveType` as an enum (gas / induction / electric / unknown) inside the OPTIONAL, expandable Cooking-equipment section of onboarding step 3 — alongside `equipment[]`, `kidCount`, `kidAgeRanges[]`, `pickyEaterCount`, `pickyAvoidances[]`, `spiceTolerance`, `healthGoals[]`, `budgetLevel`, all carried under one `[SCHEMA]` note. ⚠️ **That proves it was SPECCED, not that anything READS it (§8.1: only code establishes existence, and the PRD's characteristic failure is OVER-REPORTING what exists).**
- **The audit is one read-only sweep with TWO columns per field, and the second is the one that matters: is it WRITTEN** (does the screen set it, does `PUT /me/preferences` accept it) **and is it READ** (does any prompt body, filter, sort, or display consume it). **Written-and-never-read is the removal candidate. Read-only-by-a-prompt-body is NOT dead, and removing it silently changes generation.**
- 🔴 **REMOVING THE CONTROL IS NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY PAID FOR THAT LESSON ONCE.** `wantsLeftovers` (D-WS7-190) was pulled from onboarding, the Preferences screen and both wizard screens — **but its schema default was `@default(true)`, so a UI-less field would have silently turned leftover-inflation ON for every new user**, the exact opposite of pulling the feature. It needed its own migration to flip the default. ✅ **THE RULE THIS ENTRY CARRIES: every removal in this sweep checks the SCHEMA DEFAULT and every consumer, not just the screen.**
- ⚠️ **AND THE CONSUMER THAT HIDES FROM A SYMBOL GREP IS THE PROMPT BODY.** Some prompt bodies are `{{…Input}}` with the real instructions in compiled TS (§7's footgun), so a field can be load-bearing inside a prompt string while a grep for its name returns nothing useful. **Sweep `aiPrompts.ts` and the compiled prompt surfaces, not only the TypeScript that names the field** — and per §27.3, no negative from a single grep shape.
- **OPEN, for Hans once the audit reports:** whether "nothing reads it" means **drop the column** or **keep the column and drop only the onboarding control.** 🔵 **Keeping a written-but-unread column is the cheaper reversal if equipment data is ever wanted for recipe filtering — which is what the PRD said it was for** (*"so we don't suggest recipes you can't make"*). **Friction is removed either way; only the schema decision differs.**

### D-WS9-234 — 🔵 The cooking "Playlist" — a FOURTH concept, and it RENAMES what D-WS7-202 has been calling a favorite

- **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[SCHEMA]` `[WS7-11]` `[SPEC]` · **Date:** September 8, 2026 · **Owner:** **WS7-11 — Favorites, Saves, Ratings** (roadmap row 6a) · **Status:** 🔵 **OPEN — Hans has stated the concept; it is not yet ruled into WS7-11's model** · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **D-WS7-202 (the entry this AMENDS)** · D-WS7-203 · D-WS7-204 · D-WS7-111 · D-WS7-139 (fork-on-acquire) · PRD §13.10.4 · BUG-018.
- **Hans, September 8, 2026, in his own frame:** meatballs and a lasagna he loves are **favorites**, and he would rate them **5 stars** — *"other users may not favorite those meals and some people could think the meals are less than 5 stars and that's fine."* A chicken piccata is **a favorite, probably a 4-star meal, and a recurring meal they cook** — *"it's on our 'playlist' of meals we cook regularly because we know them, they taste good, meet our dietary needs/goals, and everyone eats them."* **He wants Favorites, Ratings, then "add to my cooking playlist" as an attribute tag — and the wizard to incorporate it, "or even shuffle ONLY the user's playlist meals when it generates plans and suggestions."**
- 🔴 **THIS IS A RENAME AS MUCH AS AN ADDITION, AND A BLOCK BUILT FROM D-WS7-202 AS WRITTEN WOULD GET IT WRONG.** That entry defines **three** concepts — **Saved** (the heart; acquisition, not a rating) · **Rated** (stars; retrospective quality) · **Favorite** (*"this is a staple; put it in front of me when I'm planning"* — forward-looking intent). **Its verbatim Hans quote from July is the SAME chicken-piccata argument:** *"this is a 4 star meal, but it's easy and my kids love it, save it as a favorite if I want to add to a plan because it's a staple meal."* ⚠️ **JULY'S "FAVORITE" IS SEPTEMBER'S "PLAYLIST."** Hans has now split that one concept in two and moved the name: **Favorite = plain affection ("I love this")** · **Playlist = the staple / planning signal.** **Four concepts, not three — and the word "favorite" now means the lighter one.**
- ✅ **AND IT ANSWERS D-WS7-202's OWN BLOCKING QUESTION, WHICH IS WHY THIS ENTRY UNBLOCKS RATHER THAN COMPLICATES.** That entry forbids commissioning WS7-11 until *"what do favorites actually DO?"* is ruled, because *"a favorite toggle that visibly does nothing is worse than no toggle."* 🔵 **The answer falls out of Hans's model: the PLAYLIST is the one that does something — it feeds the wizard. The FAVORITE can then be the light one (a My Meals filter/sort), because it is no longer carrying the planning job it was never a good fit for.**
- 🔵 **THE WIZARD ASK IS THE NEW SCOPE, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE "BIAS" D-WS7-202 CONTEMPLATED.** That entry's candidate was *"wizard bias — weight generation toward favorites, a prompt-contract change."* **Hans is asking for that OR a stricter mode: shuffle from the playlist ONLY.** ⚠️ **These are different builds. A weight is a prompt-contract change. "Only these meals" is closer to a constrained selection over the user's own library than to a generation prompt** — and it has a failure the bias does not: **a playlist of three meals cannot fill a week.** **Rule which one, and rule what happens when the playlist is too small (top up from the catalog? refuse? shorten the plan?), before commissioning.**
- ⚠️ **KEEP DECLARED SEPARATE FROM OBSERVED — the trap this entry exists to flag.** *"Meals we cook regularly"* is exactly what `timesCooked` / `lastUsedAt` would measure **if anything ever wrote to them** — they are dead columns, DB-probed **0/337** (D-WS7-111, adopted by D-WS7-204). 🔴 **The playlist is a user's DECLARED intent, not a derived frequency. Do not auto-populate it from cook counts, and do not let the cook-tracking work absorb it** — a meal you cook weekly out of obligation is not on the playlist, and a seasonal favourite is.
- ⚠️ **D-WS7-202's HAZARDS CARRY TO THE PLAYLIST FLAG UNCHANGED:** **fork-on-calibrate** — never write a personal playlist flag to a `userId: null` catalog row; **reuse D-WS7-139's fork-on-acquire, do not reinvent it** · the **migration WS7-11 already needs** (rating + favorite + cook-tracking, now + the playlist attribute — still likely one) · and the PRD §13.10.2 `[SCHEMA]` note that was **already redlined once for forgetting the stars** — ⚠️ **it now also omits the playlist. Redline it in the same pass, or it will be wrong a second time in the same way.**
- **Sequencing unchanged:** WS7-11 sits **AFTER** the WS9 restyle (net-new UI, built once in the new design system). ✅ **This entry is DEFINITION-track work and can run now, alongside WS9A execution — it produces rulings, not code.**
- ✅ **HANS, September 10, 2026 — THE PLAYLIST IN HIS WORDS, AND IT IS THE PRODUCT'S STANCE ON REPEAT COOKING:** *"Most importantly, I want to introduce the concept of a meal Playlist. Users can save meals to a playlist (either by importing or selecting a Kiwi Cookbook meal), and marking the meal as a playlist meal. Then, they can create plans from the playlist if they want. or generate a plan and include playlist meals. the idea is a lot of home cooks repeat the same meals because they're easy, they work, and they taste good. I don't want Kiwi to get in the way of that."*
  - **It adds three things this entry did not have:** the two ways IN (import a meal, or pick a Kiwi Cookbook meal — the latter is fork-on-acquire, above); **plans built FROM the playlist** (the "shuffle ONLY" mode); and **generation that INCLUDES playlist meals** (the bias mode). **Both modes are wanted — the either/or above is answered "both"; what remains open is the too-small-playlist behaviour.**
  - 🔴 **"Don't get in the way" has two concrete consequences for machinery that already exists — chat-Claude's reading of this quote plus D-WS9-039, to confirm when the playlist is spec'd:** (1) **the fatigue nudge (D-WS9-073) must not push against a playlist meal** — a declared staple is the opposite of "Kiwi really loves suggesting those dang fajitas"; (2) **BUG-249's no-repeat-across-suggested-plans rule exempts playlist meals the USER chose to include**, exactly as it exempts meals named in TellKiwi — **but playlist meals Kiwi picks on its own are fillers, and still vary across the three plans.** ⚠️ **And a user-chosen playlist meal over the cook-time cap is included with its honest time (BUG-245's ruling), not filtered out by the shelf predicate.**
  - ⚠️ **SEQUENCING HAS MOVED BY HANS'S STATEMENT: the playlist is part of the plan-building redesign he places after "the last few P1 bugs and grocery stuff" (D-WS9-237) — not only WS7-11 after the restyle.** The roadmap update is owed; the mockup session precedes the build.
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, 2026, mockup round 2 — recorded on D-WS9-237 with the rest of the flow): the Playlist is a BOTTOM-NAV TAB where users manage the meals they cook the most, and its per-plan use is a DIAL on the Kitchen Wizard — Playlist meals: None · Some · Mostly · All (default unselected).** **That dial answers the "both modes" question above: All = build the plan from the playlist only; Some / Mostly = the bias mode.** The per-plan include toggle drawn in mockup round 1 is gone — the dial replaced it. ⚠️ **Still open: the too-small-playlist behaviour when the dial says All or Mostly, and the intake sheet (drawn as Hans described it, not ruled).**
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 16, 2026, mockup round 5):** **"Plan a week from these" → the Pick screen filtered to the user's playlist meals only — no Kiwi suggestions, the same "Build my week", one active plan.** **"Add meals" → the existing Create Meal screen's six options, plus the bulk intake (now D-WS9-244).** **Copy: "your go-to favorites", not "the meals you actually cook"** — Hans: *"came off like the rest of the kiwi meals aren't great."* **A user with NO playlist meals cannot set the wizard's Playlist dial; they see instead:** *"No playlist? No problem. If you want your own personal go-to favorites included in your plans, click here to get started"* (his words; the link opens the Playlist tab). Still open: the too-small-playlist behaviour when the dial says All or Mostly.
- ✅ **BUILT — Block 2b, September 16, 2026 (`36482cf` the tab and screen · `c812f3d` the two ways in · `f31b149` "Plan a week from these"), AUDITED PASS; device-unproven.** The fifth tab exists with Hans's copy (*"your go-to favorites"*, the rotation line), membership is DECLARED only (no cook counts, no "last cooked" — BUG-275 stays dead as ruled), "Add meals" is today's Create Meal screen with a `toPlaylist=1` thread through all six ways in plus a Meal Detail toggle, and "Plan a week from these" is the Pick screen with `source: "playlist"` — no Kiwi suggestions, no "Get more options", the same "Build my week". **Still open and now sharper: the too-small-playlist behaviour when the dial says All or Mostly** (the server neutralises a dial to `none` at zero meals, but a 3-meal playlist against a 5-day plan on `all` is unruled — the Pick path just shows 3; the generate path is BUG-281's territory), and **BUG-283** (membership is not determinable client-side).
- 🔵 **NOT DESIGNED — Hans, September 10: *"the multi-select list screen hasn't been designed. Same with the playlist."*** **His intake idea, verbatim, for the spec — not ruled:** *"I was thinking of an easy 'tell kiwi' type of import with like 10 rows and a cached call or version of the call to anthropic. so a user like me could add a line 'grilled chicken breasts, near east rice pilaf, roasted broccoli. and grilled chicken thigh tacos with pico and saucy black beans and chicken picatta with arugula salad etc. etc. etc.' and have it create meals for me in my playlist. but there's a lot there, and we can save it for the spec work before build."* ⚠️ **For the spec, not now:** it is TellKiwi's shape turned toward the library — a named-meal parse (the directed path already extracts `explicitMeals`), a Kiwi Cookbook match before any generation (catalog hit = no AI cost, per the arc's ~18× store-bound saving), live generation only for the misses, and every result marked as a playlist meal.

### D-WS9-235 — `estimatedTimeMinutes` is DERIVED from steps at save time, with the scheduler's parallelism, and ACTIVE time is captured beside it — ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 10, 2026)**

- **Raised:** September 9–10, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 · **Tags:** meal-generation · data-integrity · prompt-contract · **Source:** BUG-245's Phase 0 · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-245** · **BUG-069** · **D-WS9-122** · D-WS9-128 · D-WS9-230 · BUG-246.
- **Hans, September 9, verbatim, which is the direction:** *"the time to cook should be estimated or calculated at the meal level… we have meals, dishes, ingredients, and STEPS in the catalog, so the data should be there."*
- 🔴 **WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT A PROMPT TWEAK.** BUG-245's Phase 0 found the generator being INSTRUCTED to write a false number: `wizard.candidate.expand v5` says *"Author estimatedTimeMinutes from the actual recipe, then keep it under the cap… No exceptions,"* with a worked example licensing the exclusion of unattended time. **Writing 30 for a 58-minute bake is the COMPLIANT answer.** ✅ **A prompt fix closes THAT leak. It does not close the CLASS: any prompt that authors a scalar independently of the steps can drift from them, and BUG-069 → D-WS9-122 → BUG-245 is three instances of exactly that in six weeks.**
- ✅ **THE STRUCTURAL FIX: the meal-level time is COMPUTED from the steps at save time and the generator never writes it.** Then no prompt can lie into it, a time cap must be met by SELECTING meals whose steps fit rather than by writing the cap, and the whole class becomes impossible rather than patched.
- ⚠️ **NOT TRIVIALLY `Σ steps`.** D-WS9-128 measured the step sum overcounting parallel work at a 1.84 median ratio (p90 2.69). **But the data to do better exists: `parallelGroup` is 0 of 25,564 steps, so a dish's own steps are strictly sequential — the honest floor is the LONGEST DISH's serial sum, and the scheduler already knows which cross-dish steps overlap.** **The formula is a design question inside this ruling, not a blocker to it.**
- 🔴 **AND A PRODUCT QUESTION FALLS OUT THAT ONLY HANS CAN ANSWER: WHEN THE CAP CANNOT BE MET, WHAT DOES THE APP DO?** Today it fabricates. **Once the number is honest, a 30-minute cap against a catalog where 40–75% of meals overshoot their own claims will refuse a lot.** Options are not exclusive: tell the user and offer to relax · relax silently to the nearest fit · treat the cap as "aim for" rather than "never exceed." **Unruled.**
- ⚠️ **SEQUENCING WITH BUG-245's PROMPT FIX: complementary, not alternatives.** The prompt fix's SELECTION half — "if the recipe cannot fit the cap, pick a different recipe" — is needed either way. **Its DEFINITION half becomes moot if this is ruled "derive."** Rule this first; it decides the shape of that block.
- 🔵 **BACKFILL:** Hans is open (September 9) and D-WS9-230's carve-out already covers catalog meals. **A derived formula, once ruled, IS the backfill — run it once over the pool, then it runs on every save.**
- ✅ **RULED September 10, 2026 — Hans, verbatim, because each clause changed the block:** *"on the structural piece, yes, but to refine that a bit more: the steps need the parallelism baked in to them. bake one thing for 20 minutes and sautee another for 10 minutes can be done in about 20 minutes. we did a lot of work on this and what counts as parallel or not, so the rules are there. I would also say if this requires a backfill or process to get at the data we should do the cached prompt thing and have it run overnight like when the catalog was created. almost more importantly, is if we're going to all this trouble - and we are - we should get active time and cook time. filtering the wizard on active time and whatnot is NOT MVP and can be deferred to the roadmap."*
  1. 🔴 **THE FORMULA IS THE SCHEDULER'S.** `cookingScheduler.ts` (BUG-018 B2) already decides what overlaps: **unattended = `{preheat, rest, hold}` OR `cook && !isTimingSensitive`.** The derived **TOTAL** is that timeline's end for the meal's dishes; the derived **ACTIVE** is its attended minutes. **Neither `Σ steps` nor a new parallelism model is acceptable — the "formula is a design question" line above is CLOSED by this ruling.** Hans's example is the acceptance test: a 20-minute bake beside a 10-minute sauté derives to about 20, not 30.
  2. ✅ **TWO FIELDS.** `estimatedTimeMinutes` keeps D-WS9-122's meaning (total wall-clock); a new active-time field is captured beside it on every derivation. **Filtering or steering the wizard on active time is NOT MVP → D-WS9-236.** ✅ **Display RULED the same night — Hans: *"capture for sure. displayed would be great if it's not much more work."* Capture is unconditional; display (meal card + meal detail) goes into Phase 1 if the design pass sizes it small, otherwise it queues.**
  3. ✅ **THE DATA PATH IS PRE-AUTHORISED.** If the derivation's inputs are missing or untrustworthy at scale, the remedy is **an overnight cached-prompt tagging pass over the catalog** on the Block 3.8 pattern (`25db784`) — not a forward-only fix. D-WS9-230's carve-out covers it.
- ✅ **THE PRODUCT QUESTION IS RULED TOO — verbatim:** *"if we can't meet their needs, we should be honest about it. the wizard generation falls back to AI, so I would imagine it would figure something out to suggest (right or wrong), so I don't know if we really need an error page or anything."* 🔴 **The cap constrains SELECTION; the number shown is the derived, honest one; there is NO error page, NO refusal state and NO relax-the-cap dialog.** A cap the pool cannot meet surfaces a meal with a true number over the cap, and that is the product telling the truth. ✅ **Hans's own pool-side remedy is scheduled: a catalog supplement targeted at 30-minute meals before launch, during UAT (`kiwi_go_live_todos.md`).**
- 🔴 **COMMISSIONED September 10: a READ-ONLY design pass in the server lane (`kiwi_cc_prompt_LANE_A_time_from_steps.md`) — what the scheduler returns today, the state of the step inputs by `sourceType`, every meal-writing path and what the wizard card shows before steps exist, the prompt's residual shape, and whether the overnight pass is needed. Phase 1 is written from its report; BUG-245 carries the build status.**
- ✅ **THE DESIGN PASS ANSWERED THE SAME NIGHT (server lane; full detail on BUG-245):** the scheduler already returns the total (`scheduleCookingSequence → totalEstimatedMinutes`); ACTIVE needs one export-only change inside the module that owns the predicate; the step inputs are FINE (`isTimingSensitive` true on 16.4%, `estimatedMinutes` on 100%) so **the overnight tagging pass is NOT needed and Hans's pre-authorisation stays banked**; every persistence path has steps at write time and only the candidate CARD does not; `mealMaterialize` defaults a missing number to **30**. 🔴 **And the under-claim is SYSTEMIC, not constraint-driven: 93.8% of 1,555 meals, p50 +20 minutes, capped and uncapped alike — only 19 meals honestly fit a 30-minute cap (163 at 45, 567 at 60).** ⚠️ **"The constraint dominates", relayed into this entry from eight rows, is withdrawn; the ruling stands because it ruled the structure, not the cause.**
- 🔴 **ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN SEQUENCING NOTE: D-WS9-122's definition is moot for the PERSISTED value only. The candidate card still shows the generator's number before steps exist, so the expand prompt still gets the wall-clock definition — for the card's estimate, not for storage.** ✅ **BUILT September 11 (BUG-245's O1, `f6e6571` · `6ed3b02`; device-unproven, reseed pending): for live slots, expand v7 also writes a timed step outline and the draft's number is derived from it; the authored number remains only as the fallback when an outline is missing, and as telemetry. The outline is stripped before `finalize_steps` sees the meal, so the saved steps are still written independently; the draft-vs-saved gap is logged per meal.** ✅ **Device-proven September 11 (drafts honest; every fresh meal outlined). 🔵 The gap measured the same day: saved runs +11–22 over the draft because the OUTLINE is thinner than finalize's steps (2–3 vs 7 steps per dish; skipped plating/rests/preheats) — expand v8 brings the outline to finalize's shape; details on BUG-245.** ⚠️ **Two things the measurement surfaced for THIS entry:** (1) **the scheduler leaves unattended windows unfilled** — steps within a dish are serial and nothing is placed into another dish's `rest` (al pastor's 10-minute marinade sat empty with 11 minutes of sides' prep queued; serial ÷ scheduled is 1.26–1.33 across the catalog). **That is the ruled scheduler behaving as ruled — whether the marinade window SHOULD take another dish's prep is Hans's, not a defect; recorded, not commissioned.** (2) ✅ **A FOURTH WRITE-PATH GAP, CONFIRMED AND CLOSED `6ad0554` (September 11 evening; a dish step edit DEVICE-PASSED that night — the edit saved and the meal containing the dish updated its time, while an ingredient edit correctly did not propagate).** ⚠️ **The round's data check cannot prove the phase half: the re-stamp runs in the same transaction as the step rewrite, so stored always equals derived-from-current-steps and `move zero` is structurally incapable of failing for an edited meal (§27.4's shape). A direct read of an edited dish's `phaseType` values is owed — one query, in the next read-only lane. ✅ **PROVEN September 12: the edited dish reads `{prep, cook, assemble}` and its siblings `{prep, preheat, cook, rest, assemble}` — no dish fell to all-`cook`. `6ad0554` is closed.**** The gap itself: both builders send steps without `phaseType`, and every step re-created by a builder save had fallen to the column default `cook` (50 of 50 on nine re-created dishes; catalog 35.9%) — so a re-stamp after such a save derived from all-`cook` steps. Now an omitted phase or timing flag inherits the existing step at the same index. ✅ **`activeTimeMinutes` is on the wire `4222db4`** (beside `minutes`, null never absent) and shown on the plan review row and meal detail (`ddc1773`).
- ✅ **PHASE 1 COMMISSIONED September 10 (server lane): `Meal.activeTimeMinutes Int?`; `estimatedTimeMinutes` keeps its name and becomes the derived total; dish scalars derive; `src/lib/mealTiming.ts`; hooks at both `mealMaterialize` sites after step creation, the `?? 30` default retired; `mealCreate`/`mealFork` re-derive; prompt v6 (selection-not-the-number, honest-number rule, wall-clock definition for the card); deterministic hash-verified backfill over 1,458 meals, Hans applies. The MOBILE half — show active time on card + detail if small, and label the card's pre-finalize estimate — follows once the server lands.**

### D-WS9-236 — Filtering or steering the wizard on ACTIVE (hands-on) time — 🔵 NOT MVP, roadmap

- **Raised:** September 10, 2026 · **Owner:** roadmap (post-MVP) · **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[ROADMAP]` `[WS9]` · **Source:** Hans's D-WS9-235 ruling · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-235** · BUG-245 · D-WS9-122 · D-WS7-166 (the cook-time cap) · PRD §17.5.1.
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"filtering the wizard on active time and whatnot is NOT MVP and can be deferred to the roadmap."*
- ✅ **WHAT IS IN MVP: the active-time NUMBER is derived and stored on every meal (D-WS9-235 item 2), so this feature starts with its data already populated.** **What is deferred: any wizard control, preference field, prompt instruction or catalog filter keyed on active time** — e.g. *"under 20 minutes of hands-on time"* as a cap distinct from D-WS7-166's total-time cap, or steering weeknights toward low-active meals.
- ⚠️ **When it is picked up, it is a PREFERENCE-CONTRACT change (a second cap beside `maxCookTimeMinutes`) plus a selection-filter change, and it inherits D-WS9-235's rule that a cap constrains SELECTION and never the number.** The obvious product shape is the D-WS7-166 control with a second row; do not design it now.
- ✅ **Display IS ruled (September 10, Hans): capture unconditionally; show it on meal cards / meal detail if it is not much more work — sized in D-WS9-235's Phase 1. This entry defers only FILTERING/steering.**
- 🔵 **THE DATA, MEASURED September 11 (server lane, read-only; public, non-archived dinners with a derived time, n = 1,189) — recorded for when this is picked up, NOT a reopening of the ruling:** total ≤ 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 60 → **6** / 15 / 51 / 115 / 197 / 435 · active ≤ 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 → 1 / 14 / 74 / **177**. **A 30-minute cap on total time is a six-dinner shelf; the same cap on hands-on time would be 177.** Until this is picked up, thin short-cap shelves are met by live composition under BUG-245's selection rule and by Hans's planned 30-minute catalog supplement.
- 🔵 **HANS, September 11 (midday), after seeing honest draft times of 43 and 55 on a 30-minute plan — product input, verbatim, NOT yet a ruling that moves this out of the roadmap:** *"I'm ok with how it's working right now. the times are honest. and if we display the prep time, and especially if we give a prep time max with a flexible total time that's perfect."* **That is this entry's feature described from the user's side — a hands-on ceiling with a loose total.** The display half is already BUG-245's mobile half. **Whether the hands-on CAP is pulled into MVP was put to Hans (September 11).**
- ✅ **HANS ANSWERED, September 11 afternoon — verbatim, and it REFINES this entry rather than reopening it:** *"for hands-on, I feel like that's almost more important than total time. a 45 minute meal where I'm active the whole time is a pain on a busy night (think of a risotto with constant stirring and steps), but a 45 minute meal where I put things on a sheetpan and multi-task or watch my kids while it bakes is fine if I need an easy night of cooking. I'm thinking the labels may need an adjustment more than we need to engineer options. a true 30 minute ceiling sounds appealing, but if a meal is 8 minutes of prep and 37 minutes total to cook, I don't think a home chef would complain. the edge to consider with prep/active being low is a slow cooker meal - if the chef needs dinner on the table and it's 8 minutes of prep, but 4 hours of cooking, that's not a great weeknight option"* **What that settles:** (1) **no new cap option now** — *labels, not options*: every place a time shows carries BOTH numbers, total and hands-on, plainly labelled (BUG-245's mobile half, building September 11: `38 min · 10 min hands-on`); (2) **the MVP cap stays on total time**, and an honest few-minute miss is fine (BUG-245); (3) **the roadmap item is reframed:** not "a second cap on active time" but **a weeknight-suitability read that needs BOTH bounds — low hands-on AND a bounded total** (a slow-cooker dinner fails on total; a risotto fails on hands-on). Design it as one control, not two rows, when it is picked up. **Still post-MVP.**

### D-WS9-238 — When the eligible shelf is thin, does the shelf guard relax and let Kiwi invent? — ✅ RULED by Hans, September 14, 2026: CATALOG FIRST, AI FALLBACK

- **Raised:** September 12, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 / plan-gen · **Tags:** `[PLAN-GEN]` `[PROMPT]` `[COST]` `[PRODUCT]` · **Status:** 🔵 **OPEN — a decision, not a defect** · **Source:** Hans, challenging chat-Claude's BUG-255 (b) ruling · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-255** (where the measurement and the withdrawal live) · **D-WS9-073** (the shelf guard's own entry) · D-WS9-037 (coverage degrades on actual coverage, not a flag) · D-WS7-166 (the cap as a shelf predicate) · `kiwi_plan_generation_arc_scope.md` §3 · `kiwi_go_live_todos.md` (the supplement row this decision may retire).
- **Hans, verbatim:** *"if it can't find a catalog option for a slot it should make up a recipe and meal or meals as needed. I caught this because you created a list of 70 meals in under 30 minutes no problem."*
- ✅ **RULED by Hans, September 14, 2026, verbatim:** *"worth measuring to be sure it's not crazy, but if a meal doesn't exist it should be generated from the wizard. the process should try to pull from the catalog (which is built to reduce the every time cost of creating many meals), and then fall back to AI to create meals if none match the user's criteria."*
- 🔴 **WHAT THIS SETTLES, AND IT REFRAMES THE GUARD RATHER THAN TUNING IT: the catalog is a COST OPTIMISATION, not the boundary of what Kiwi can offer.** The shelf guard’s job is therefore **not** "protect a thin shelf by repeating meals" — it is **"decide when to stop searching the catalog and start generating."** A slot with no catalog match is a GENERATION, not a repeat. **D-WS9-073’s guard was written for a 1,214-meal catalog and read as a scarcity rule; under this ruling scarcity is not a reason to repeat, it is a trigger to invent.**
- ⚠️ **THE ONE MEASUREMENT HANS ATTACHED ("worth measuring to be sure it’s not crazy") — owed before the build, not before the ruling: the PER-GENERATION COST of an invention-heavy plan.** If most slots miss the catalog, a week’s plan becomes N generations instead of N lookups, on the most latency-sensitive path in the product and against the spend guard’s per-user cap. **Measure: cost and wall-clock for a plan where 0 / half / all slots miss, and the per-user-cap headroom that leaves.** ✅ **The ruling does not depend on the answer — the answer sizes the guard’s threshold and tells us whether a cap is reachable in normal use.**
- ⚠️ **Chat-Claude’s note, recorded as a read and not a ruling:** the 30-minute shelf is now **12** meals (D-WS9-239’s catalog pass, measured from the DB). **On a 30-minute cap this ruling is what makes the promise deliverable at all** — 12 catalog dinners cannot fill repeated weeks, so generation is the mechanism, not the exception.
- ✅ **THE PREMISE IS CORRECT AND ALREADY BUILT.** Live gap-fill is the arc's design (§3): the shelf is a pool the AI composes from, invention fills what it cannot cover, and the fallback triggers on measured coverage rather than a flag. **Two of four dinners in the September 11 round were live-composed.** The capability is not the constraint.
- 🔴 **THE CONSTRAINT IS ONE SENTENCE OF PROMPT.** D-WS9-073's shelf guard — *"never abandoning the shelf"* — was written to protect Block 4b-1's reach gain against a 1,214-dinner shelf. At a 30-minute cap the eligible shelf is **six**, and the guard keeps pointing the model back at six meals the rotation nudge has already exhausted. **Guard and nudge conflict precisely when the cap is tight.**
- **The three shapes, none built, none ruled:**
  - **(a) THRESHOLD RELAX** — when the eligible shelf is below N (N unmeasured; six is clearly below it, 116 at a 45-minute cap probably is not), the guard softens to *prefer* the shelf rather than *never abandon* it. **Smallest change; one prompt edit per body; the cost moves per generation and is unbounded.**
  - **(b) CATALOG SUPPLEMENT** — author 30-minute dinners into the catalog until the shelf is deep, and change no rule. **One-time cost; the 95-row target list exists; it fixes the 30-minute case only and every future tight constraint re-opens it.**
  - **(c) BOTH** — supplement the common caps, relax below a floor for the long tail.
- 💰 **PRICE THE DECISION BEFORE RULING IT, and do not use the arc's headline numbers as if they were this measurement.** Block 4b-3 measured store-backed **$0.0458** / three plans against live **~$0.27** / one plan (**~18×**), but neither was a thin-shelf 30-minute generation. ⚠️ **Owed: the real per-generation cost and latency of a 30-minute plan built mostly by invention** — a read-only measurement, and (a) should not be chosen without it. Latency matters as much as money: live slots run `expand` + `finalize`, which is where the 20s-per-call cost lives, and the whole latency block exists because generation speed is a product property.
- ⚠️ **Quality is the third axis and it is unmeasured.** Catalog dinners went through the D-WS9-040 quality gate and an editorial pass; an invented 30-minute dinner has had neither, and **BUG-245's whole history is invented meals writing dishonest times.** Invention gets cheaper to trust *after* the expand v9 ceiling and BUG-256's scheduler fix land — so this decision is also **sequenced behind them**, not independent of them.
- 🔵 **OPEN QUESTIONS:** what N is · whether the relax is a prompt clause or a server-side signal passed into the payload (the payload already knows the shelf size) · whether `'most'` behaves differently from `'all'` · whether relaxing re-opens BUG-249 (repeats within one generation) by giving the model more freedom.

- ✅ **THE COST MEASUREMENT OWED BEFORE THIS BUILD — taken from `LLMCallLog` (30 days, successful calls) by the redesign arc's Phase 0, September 16, read-only:** an invented wizard meal ≈ expand (v6–v8: $0.027–0.036, 12–18 s) + finalize_steps (v7: $0.035, ~19 s) ≈ **$0.06–0.075 and ~30–40 s serial** (fan-out is parallel across meals), plus the candidate generate ($0.03–0.05, ~20 s, titles only). The store-fill generator: **$0.048 / meal, ~34 s, 99% cache-read.** So in the redesign flow (D-WS9-237: "Get more options" on a ≤10 shelf = up to 2 AI rounds of 3–5) **one round ≈ $0.20–0.35 and ~40 s wall.** ⚠️ **What this does NOT measure:** a whole invention-heavy PLAN at 0 / half / all slots missing the catalog (the original ask) — the redesign replaces that shape for the meals path, so the per-meal figure is the one the build needs. **The spend guard (D-WS9-241 D) is the per-user backstop.**

### D-WS9-239 — Intra-dish overlap: the step generator records where an overlap starts AND ends (`parallelGroup`), the scheduler honours it, existing meals get a tagging pass — ✅ RULED (a), September 12, 2026

- **Raised:** September 12, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 / plan-gen + scheduler · **Tags:** `[COOK-TIME]` `[PROMPT]` `[SCHEDULER]` `[DATA]` `[PRODUCT]` · **Status:** ✅ **RULED (a) by Hans, September 12, 2026 — IN SCOPE, sequenced as the server block right after WS9A lands and BEFORE the UAT 30-minute catalog supplement; the catalog tagging pass is a separable step whose per-meal cost is measured on 20 meals first. UNBUILT.** · **Source:** CC's read-only intra-dish measurement (BUG-256, second amendment) · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **BUG-256** (the numbers) · **D-WS9-235** (the ruled derivation this extends — steps within a dish are SERIAL today; the scheduler's cross-dish parallelism is what "the scheduler's parallelism" has meant) · **BUG-253** (Ask-Kiwi imports are one-dish meals — the population this helps most) · **D-WS9-238** (the other half of the thin-shelf problem) · **BUG-018** (finish-alignment, kept) · D-WS6-034 (`parallelGroup`'s type drift, the field's own history) · `kiwi_go_live_todos.md` (the 30-minute catalog supplement).
- **What the measurement established (2,344 meal-schedules, September 12):** the recipes ARE written with intra-dish overlap in mind — *"While the potatoes bake, make the marinara"* — and D-WS9-235's serial-within-dish rule charges every such minute to the meal. **Removing the serialisation honestly is worth ~12 minutes mean over the catalog and takes the 30-minute shelf from 6 dinners to 17–20, the 45-minute shelf from 116 to ~250, the 60-minute shelf from 443 to ~680 — the largest lever on the "30-minute meals" promise measured to date, three times the catalog supplement's likely effect and ten times BUG-256's ordering fix.** ⚠️ **But only the START of an overlap is recoverable from text (195 steps, ~1 min mean, one shelf meal); the END — which later step needs the unattended step finished — is recorded nowhere, and without it every automatic rule either drains the potatoes before the boil ends or makes the griddle wait for the onions.** The missing bit is exactly what `parallelGroup` (exists on `RecipeInstructionStep`; set on 0 of 26,409 rows) was for.
- **The shape, none built:** **(1) generator contract** — the step-generation prompt (`finalize_steps` and its siblings) emits, on every step that may run inside an earlier unattended step of its own dish, a `parallelGroup` token naming that unattended step, and the SAME token on the unattended step; every untagged step after the group waits for the unattended step's finish. Prompt-playbook loop; one bump per body. **(2) scheduler** — honour the tag (the TEXT rule for tagged steps, the window-close for untagged ones); finish-alignment and attended-serial unchanged; re-derive on save as today. **(3) tagging pass** over existing catalog dinners — the cached-prompt overnight pattern that D-WS9-235 pre-authorised *"if the step data needs it"* (it does), then a re-derivation of every stored time. **(4) sequencing:** (1)+(2) BEFORE the UAT 30-minute catalog supplement, so the 95 new dinners are generated with the contract and never need the pass; (3) is separable and can follow.
- 💰 **Costs owed before ruling, not guessed:** the per-meal cost of the tagging pass at the cached-prompt rate (measure on 20 meals, then multiply) · whether the generator can be TRUSTED to place the window end (hand-check 20 tagged dishes against the timelines, the way the regex was checked) · the re-derivation's effect on saved plans is NIL by D-WS9-230 (forward-only; catalog meals are shared data and ARE re-derived).
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT reopen:** D-WS9-235's ruling that time is derived from steps with the scheduler's parallelism — this EXTENDS the scheduler's parallelism to inside a dish using data the generator supplies; it is not Σ-steps and not a second model. Active time is unaffected (0 of 2,344 changed). BUG-018's invariant is kept. **BUG-256's ordering fix (ALT-B) is NOT authorised by this entry; it is revisited only inside this build, where the two interact.**
- ✅ **RULED (a), Hans, September 12, 2026.** His framing of the kitchen, verbatim, which the design must honour: *"I think it's related to logic that you can't reliably chop stuff for 10 minutes while you're sautéing an onion. I don't want the kitchen to feel rushed, but things do need to run in parallel. doing the prep/chop stuff first makes cooking so much easier, and you can sautee two things at once if your food is ready to put in the pan, but that's a hard set of rules to create."* **Three of those four are already the rules and stay: (1) attended never overlaps attended — no chopping during a sauté (BUG-018 / D-WS7-164, single cook); (2) attended work MAY run inside an UNATTENDED window (a low caramelise, a bake, a simmer, a rest) — cross-dish today, and THIS entry extends it to inside a dish, only where the recipe's own steps declare the window; (3) prep-first is the recipe author's ordering and is not changed by this.** 🔴 **The fourth — two attended sautés at once when the food is ready — is DECLINED as scope: it is the "hard set of rules" Hans named, it would weaken the single-cook rule that keeps the number honest, and the intra-dish lever alone carries ~12 min mean without it. Do not re-propose it as part of this build.** ⚠️ **"Not rushed" is a design constraint on the build, not a slogan: the scheduler infers NO overlap — it honours only what the generator declares (start AND end), and a step that is not tagged waits, exactly as today. The derived number stays the honest one.** Remaining open, for the build's Phase 0 (not for Hans): the catalog pass's measured cost · the 20-dish hand-check of the generator's window placement · whether the card needs a label beyond D-WS9-236's hands-on time.

Real model-placed tags give **7.55 min mean (Sonnet, all tags) / 4.95 min mean on the dishes whose tags survive a hand-check**; p50 is 0 on the trusted set — most dishes have nothing to overlap. **On the 20-meal sample, zero meals cross the 30-minute line under any tag set; 1–2 cross 45.** The *"30-minute shelf from 6 to 17–20"* projection does not survive: intra-dish overlap is an honesty correction of a few minutes on meals with real windows, not the shelf lever. **The 95-dinner UAT supplement is the shelf lever; this entry's sequencing ahead of it was justified by a number that was the ceiling, not the expectation.**

The recurring shape is a rider that CONSUMES the window's product: *"thread the marinated shrimp"* riding the marinade rest; the ribs' 150-minute bake riding the oven preheat (starts cold, 15 min deleted); the fettuccine riding the water it cooks in (8 min deleted); a 500°F pizza preheat riding a roast in the same oven. **Every error is in the direction "not rushed" forbids — the number gets LOWER than true.** Chat-Claude's premise that bad tags can only make the number more conservative was **refuted**: true for structurally invalid tags, false for semantically wrong ones. **Haiku is out. Sonnet is usable only behind a re-measured error rate.** One structural rule catches 9 of the 19 wrong tags with zero false positives: **a `rest`/`hold` step never rides the `cook` immediately before it** (it is waiting on that cook by definition).
  - **(3) THE SCHEDULER DESIGN HOLDS; THE PERSISTENCE SURFACE IS WIDER THAN THE ENTRY SAID.** `parallelGroup` is not "write-rejected" in general — only the `/me/meals` canonical save returns 400; **every AI step schema strips it silently**, and so do the step-preserving re-save (`readPreservableSteps`), the meal fork (`STEP_COPY_FIELDS`) and every read projection feeding the scheduler — the day tags exist, a Dish Builder edit or a fork would silently drop them and the number would jump back up. `mealTiming.dishTotals` sums serially, so under tags a dish could stamp longer than its meal. **Design additions from the replay (160 tagged schedules, 0 early finishes, 0 attended overlaps, 0 order violations):** a token's group must be CONTIGUOUS (a token re-appearing after its group closed is invalid); the first step carrying a token must be the unattended window; **the meal total can get LONGER under a valid tag (1 of 160 — a list-scheduling anomaly, 79 → 82) — the guard is to schedule with tags honoured and ignored and emit the shorter, deterministic and cheap**; finish-aligned unattended riders change no total and break the intra-dish order pin — start-aligned it is. Tagging-pass economics: **Sonnet ≈ $0.017/meal → ≈ $20 for the catalog, ~2 h; no cache benefit at this prompt size** (the prefix is under the cache floor). The two step-writing instruction copies (wizard finalize body · store harness prefix) have DIVERGED around a byte-identical step-rules core — Phase 1 edits both in lockstep.

### D-WS9-237 — The meal-selection plan flow: the wizard returns MEALS the user multi-selects, and suggested plans stay — ✅ SCREENS RULED by Hans, September 15, 2026 (mockup round 2); build NOT commissioned

- **Raised:** September 10, 2026 · **Owner:** WS9 → the plan-building redesign (sequencing per Hans below; `kiwi_roadmap.md` does not reflect it yet) · **Tags:** `[PRODUCT]` `[PLAN-GEN]` `[ROADMAP]` · **Status:** 🔵 **DIRECTION RECORDED — this entry owns only the flow and its sequencing; every piece below has its own owner entry** · **Source:** Hans, device-pass notes on BUG-249, and his correction the same evening · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-120** (Cookbook scope) · **D-WS9-234** (Playlist) · **D-WS9-200** (the hand-off) · **D-WS9-191** (the chooser redesign) · D-WS7-207 · BUG-249 · D-WS7-166 · roadmap row 7 Phase D · PRD §9.5.
- **Hans, first mention, verbatim:** *"there is an upcoming redesign of the meal plan generation coming where users will select meals for their plan vs. having suggested plans. The suggested plans option will still be available, so that's valuable work to fix."*
- **Hans, the same evening, verbatim — the flow and the sequencing:** *"it's coming up in the roadmap/sequence one we get the last few P1 bugs and grocery stuff put to bed. This is where a user can use the wizard to get a list of meals that they multi-select for a plan. similarly, users will be able to search and filter and sort the Kiwi Cookbook (maybe try that term?) to find meals they can add to a plan."* · on screens: *"We should plan on some HTML or whatever mockups to talk through the screens in detail, but the specs are well defined and available in canon."*
- 🔴 **CORRECTION, and the lesson is §27.3's: this entry's first draft said "IT WAS NOT IN CANON" after three searches — FALSE. The searches used "select meals" / "redesign" vocabulary; canon files this under "Kiwi Cookbook" and "Playlist."** Where the pieces live:
  - **Browse/search/sort/filter the Kiwi Cookbook and add to a plan** → **D-WS9-120** (search bar, attribute sort/filter, a Cookbook chip on Add Meal · Swap for Different · Recipes → Meals) + `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §6 / roadmap row 7 **Phase D** (browse · sort · view · save-creates-copy · add-to-plan).
  - **"Users select meals from a list to build their plan"** → Hans, quoted in **D-WS9-200**: *"when we go to a model where users select meals from a list to build their plan, ultimately the user will choose and they control the selection of combinations that result in more or less waste."*
  - **The Playlist** (save meals, build plans from them, include them in generation) → **D-WS9-234**.
  - **Favorites surfacing in the plan-builder / add-meal-to-plan screens** → **D-WS7-207**.

- ✅ **CONFIRMED BY HANS, September 10: the wizard's multi-select list screen is NOT designed, and neither is the Playlist (D-WS9-234). The mockup session designs both before any build.**
- ✅ **What it settles now: suggested plans are NOT retired, so fixing them (BUG-249, D-WS7-166's shelf predicate) is not throwaway work.** ✅ **And D-WS7-166's shelf — the capped, filtered, fatigue-aware catalog query — is the natural pool for the wizard's meal list and for Cookbook filters, so build it as shared, not wizard-private.**
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, 2026 — mockup round 1 → round 2; the design canvas "Kiwi Meal Selection" holds the boards). Four rulings, one open list:**
  1. **Home has TWO entries: "Use my preferences" → the Kitchen Wizard, and "Tell Kiwi" — its label left of the free-text input, otherwise unchanged.** 🔴 **SURPRISE ME IS RETIRED.** Verbatim: *"surprise me goes away. we shouldn't plan on trying to put 5 meals together in a single plan and be right. it's not realistic or probable."* (The 3c §7.6 zero-typing path goes with it.)
  2. **The entry decision lives ON the Kitchen Wizard screen, not on Home.** At the top: **"Build my plan", terracotta, DISABLED until the user picks a path** — in Hans's words *"Create plan by selecting meals"* or *"Select plan, have kiwi put in the meals"* (labels are open copy). **Path A → the meal-select screen (3). Path B → today's three-plan chooser (D-WS9-191), unchanged.** Under the choice, two dials, each **None · Some · Mostly · All**: **Playlist meals** (default unselected) and **Discovery meals** (default None — today's `discoveryMealsPerWeek` Off / 1 / 2 becomes a share of the plan; the concept is `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §4.2's, outside preferred cuisines and recent history). **Everything below the dials — plan length, household, the Adjust-saved-prefs disclosure, notes — stays exactly as built.** The goal, verbatim: *"simplify the entry decision: tell me what you want, or kiwi will suggest things."*
  3. **The meal-select screen: Kiwi returns ~15 matching meals for the request (cap it — *"we should cap it so it's usable"*), the user selects — FEWER OR MORE than the plan length is allowed — and "Build my week" compiles EXACTLY those into ONE ACTIVE plan.** Verbatim: *"no different combinations, just one plan the user created based off meals kiwi suggested. no draft, no save, just create an active meal plan for the user with the meals in the plan."* 🔴 **So "beside, replacing, or feeding the chooser" is answered NONE OF THE THREE — the picks ARE the plan, and the chooser serves path B only.** **Cookbook search / sort / filter is NOT in this flow** — that is the separate Cookbook screen, post-go-live (D-WS9-120). No source row and no filter row on the meal-select screen.
  4. **Playlist is a BOTTOM-NAV TAB** (fifth tab; D-WS9-234 carries the model). Verbatim: *"users manage the meals they cook the most. Cooking fatigue is a big factor in why people fall off cooking… I want to head off user attrition."*
- 🔵 **OPEN after round 2 — chat-Claude's proposals on the canvas, Hans to rule:** the path-card copy (drawn *"I'll pick the meals"* / *"Kiwi picks the meals"*, with one-line sublines) · whether an unselected Playlist dial ALSO holds the button, or means "Kiwi's call" (drawn: only the path gates it) · **All on one dial forces None on the other** (they share one plan) · the thin shelf — when a 30-minute cap yields 6 meals, widen the cap or let Kiwi invent up to ~15 (D-WS9-238 says catalog first, AI fallback; drawn: no invention, the honest count) · tab order (drawn Home · Plans · Recipes · Playlist · Groceries). ⚠️ **FOR THE BUILD SPEC, NOT A DESIGN QUESTION: "create an active plan directly" bypasses the wizard-draft lifecycle** (D-WS9-072 / BUG-047: generation clears, nothing else does; drafts are `isWizardDraft`) — **path A must say which rows it writes and that it never leaves a draft behind.** The roadmap update placing this arc after the P1s and grocery work is still owed.

  1. 🔴 **THE PRINCIPLE — "good every time, which makes it great."** Verbatim: *"The book 'The Effortless Experience' talks about customer service, but the concept of 'wowing' a customer rarely actually works, and is more prone to pissing people off. we want this to be good every time, which makes it great."* **Kiwi does not guess that a user might like something random.** The target is the goulash case — *"my family tested some plans and made a goulash, which we had never had before, and it stood out as a pretty easy meal we would try again."* Apply this to every suggestion surface, not only the dial below.
  2. **DISCOVERY MEALS ARE RE-DEFINED: meals NEW TO THE USER that still match their preferences — not meals outside their cuisines.** 🔴 **This retires `kiwi_cookbook_spec.md` §4.2's generation rule (*"N meals outside preferred cuisines AND outside recent history"*) and its "wild card" helper copy; redline that section at close.** Playlist meals = meals from the user's playlist. **Both dials default UNSET, and unset on both means today's behaviour — straight preferences** (this supersedes round 2's "Discovery default None").
  3. **The path cards must read as Kiwi curating, not the user hunting.** *"I'll pick the meals"* was rejected: *"makes me think I have to go pick meals that I want. not that Kiwi is going to curate a list based on my preferences."* Drawn in round 3: section *"What should Kiwi suggest?"* → **"Meals to choose from"** / **"Complete plans"** (proposed copy, not ruled).

  5. **The thin shelf: NO per-filter widen links** (*"hard to scale"*). ### D-WS9-243 — The store-bought shortcut has NO DATA SLOT: `Dish.substitutions` runs scratch→bought only, so a component that is bought BY DEFAULT cannot carry its from-scratch alternative — the generator either stores the long path as the default or inverts the path labels

- **Raised:** September 15, 2026, by the substitution lane's first-10 gate (it STOPPED at 4 of 10 ≤ 30 and reported the cause rather than continuing) · **Owner:** the catalog generators (`storeFillPrompts.ts`, the store-fill volatile input) for the fix; WS9B for the grid half · **Tags:** `[CATALOG]` `[AI-PROMPT]` `[SCHEMA-SHAPE]` · **Status:** 🔴 **OPEN — ruling Hans's. It BLOCKS the rerun of the remaining 85 supplement meals (D-WS9-240 item 6) and nothing else.** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-242** (the effort-class grid, whose defaults this distorts) · **D-WS9-240 item 6** (the 95) · **D-WS9-066** (the dual-path model: scratch is the default, bought is the option) · **BUG-270** (stored time = base + DEFAULT path) · **BUG-121** (both paths render; unbuilt, which is why nothing user-visible is broken today).
- 🔴 **THE MECHANISM, measured on 10 regenerated meals.** The wire sentence told the generator to build the default path around the bought product and treat the from-scratch version as *"the optional bought→scratch alternative."* **There is no bought→scratch direction:** `Dish.substitutions` entries go scratch→bought, and BUG-270 stores base + the SCRATCH path as the meal's time. So the model expressed the alternative as a swappable component and the stored default then carried whichever side it had labelled `scratch`, two ways:
  - **The long version lands in `scratch`, so the STORED time is the long one.** KM-004 Turkey Club: *"Roast a 1½ lb turkey breast 50–60 min"* tagged `turkey/scratch`, deli turkey tagged `bought` — **derived 94 on the default, 26 on the bought path.** KM-008 Broiled Salmon: stovetop rice 22 min `scratch`, pouch rice `bought` — 29 / 19. **The 30-minute premise loses on the number that gets stored.**
  - 🔴 **The labels INVERT, which is the worse half because the number looks right.** KM-005 / KM-006 / KM-010: canned tuna and canned soup, boxed mac, and rotisserie chicken tagged `scratch`; *"cook 1½ lb albacore in simmering water"*, *"elbow macaroni"* and *"raw boneless chicken breasts"* tagged `bought`, with `substitutions.product` set to the RAW INGREDIENT. Today's derived time is right; **under D-WS9-242's grid a level-3 user (*"buy it"*) would be handed the raw-chicken path.** ⚠️ **Nothing reads path labels yet (BUG-121 unbuilt), so this is latent, not live — but it is catalog data, and it is exactly what the grid will read the day it ships.**
- 📊 **The 10, derived through the shipped scheduler** (`parallelGroupDerive.ts` + `selectDefaultPathSteps`, `ADJACENCY_MAX_MINUTES = 5`), stored default / bought path: **BLT 23/23 · Smash Burgers 31/27 · Smash Burger Tacos 33/31 · Turkey Club 94/26 · Tuna Melts 29/38 · Hot Dogs + Boxed Mac 32/32 · Sheet-Pan Sausage 42/42 · Broiled Salmon 29/19 · Chicken Caesar Wraps 26/20 · Buffalo Quesadillas 38/52.** **4 of 10 ≤ 30 (23, 29, 29, 26) → the gate's STOP.** Shortcut honoured on the default path by reading: **15 of 23 products; 6 of 10 meals fully.** Misses are all the same shape — bagged slaw against a default that shreds half a cabbage, pouch rice against a 22-minute stovetop rice, bottled Caesar against a whisked dressing.
- 🔴 **THE CAUSE IS CHAT-CLAUDE'S, NAMED SO IT IS NOT REWRITTEN: the wire sentence invented a direction the schema does not have.** `componentRegistry` was existence-checked in that lane's Phase 0; **the `substitutions` direction was not, and the sentence was written against an imagined symmetric model.** §27.6 item 4 / item 9 — an instruction that names something which does not exist. ⚠️ **Do not re-issue any wording that asks for a bought→scratch alternative until this entry is ruled.**
- 🔵 **THE THREE SHAPES, for Hans to pick from:** **(a)** leave the wire as is and let the STORED default become f(effort class) once D-WS9-242's grid ships — defers the problem into the grid build and leaves 95 meals wrong in the meantime · **(b)** add a bought→scratch direction to the schema and the wire — the general fix, a real schema-shape change, and it reopens what BUG-270 means by *"the default path"* · **(c)** **drop the alternative clause entirely and author the shortcut as a PLAIN BASE INGREDIENT with no `substitutions` entry at all.**
- ✅ **CHAT-CLAUDE RECOMMENDS (c), with an explicit licence to refuse — the reasoning, and the evidence it rests on:** **these 95 meals are DEFINED by their shortcut.** A *"BLT with bakery bread and chips from the bag"* is not a from-scratch dish carrying an option; the bought item IS the recipe, and there is no from-scratch intent to preserve. ✅ **It is also the pattern the existing 1,124-meal shelf already uses** — D-WS9-242's own Phase F measured 167 dishes starting from bought tortillas, 527 from bought stock and 12 from store pizza dough, all as **plain ingredients, not as substitutions**. So (c) makes the 95 look like the rest of the catalog rather than inventing a shape for them. **It needs no schema change, no grid dependency, and no second ruling.** ⚠️ **Its honest costs, both accepted: the 95 carry no bought paths and are therefore inert to the effort-class grid (correct — a meal whose ingredients are already bought has nothing to classify); and the store generate prefix needs a SHORTCUT MODE branch, because *"author this product as a plain ingredient"* is the opposite of what the prefix tells every other catalog run.**
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT block:** the effort-class stamp (landed, `b3ae94d`), the prefix parity and vocabulary work (landed), and the redesign arc. **Only the 85 wait.**
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 15, 2026, morning): OPTION (c), REFINED — THE SHORTCUT PRODUCT IS AUTHORED AS A PLAIN BASE INGREDIENT AND NO FROM-SCRATCH ALTERNATIVE IS AUTHORED FOR IT.** Hans, verbatim: *"we don't need a 'why to go from taco kit to making the spice mix.' and no one is going to bake turkey breasts to slice them for a sandwich. and no one is going to bake bread for a BLT."* ⚠️ **AND THE SCOPE FENCE, VERBATIM, BECAUSE IT IS THE KIND OF IDEA THAT COMES BACK: *"there's an argument that the day after thanksgiving could be a good day for turkey clubs, or a quick bread maker loaf would improve a BLT, but we're 100% not chasing that for this piece."* DO NOT REOPEN THE SEASONAL / BREAD-MACHINE VARIANTS IN THIS LANE OR THE NEXT ONE.**

- 🔵 **THE LEFTOVER, RECORDED AND NOT COMMISSIONED — it belongs to D-WS9-242's grid build, not here: the shelf stores ONE time per meal, and once the grid ships the default is PER USER.** A level-2 or level-3 user sees a shelf number derived from the scratch path on every component where the bought path is materially faster — **Phase F measured 180 components saving ≥ 20 minutes**, so this is not hypothetical. **The 95 do not need it** (under this ruling their default IS the fast path), which is why it is recorded rather than solved. **Shapes when it is picked up: store both times, or derive at query time — CC has already shown both are cheap to compute.**
- ✅ **BUILT AND AUDITED PASS — `d359ba3` (LOCAL, September 15). THE RULING HELD ON ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: 0 of 27 `substitutions` entries across the 95 names a shortcut product, checked mechanically AND read by eye.** The prefix gained a distinct `# Shortcut mode` section placed after `# Store-bought substitutions` as its explicit override (the shape chat-Claude proposed and CC adopted), and `b3ae94d`'s bought→scratch paragraph was DELETED, not qualified. Suite 2226 = 2224 + 2 skip; break red, restore sha1-identical (CC disclosed that the prefix's token-count doc comment was edited after the sha1 pair and before the commit — the pair still proves what it tested). Generate prefix 4,931 → 5,150 tokens; finalize unchanged. **$4.22 for 95 meals, $0.0444/meal, 0 API failures.**
- 🟢 **THE FIX IS VISIBLE IN THE ONE NUMBER THAT DIAGNOSED THE DEFECT: the Turkey Club went 94 → 22 derived minutes.** First-10 gate passed at **6 of 10 ≤ 30** (was 4 of 10). **Full distribution of the 95: ≤30 21 · 31–45 51 · >45 23**, against the last honest run's **8 / 38 / 49** — the ≤30 shelf nearly tripled and the >45 tail halved. ⚠️ **These are FRESH generations, so meal-by-meal comparison against the old run is not like-for-like; the distribution is.** ✅ **The public shelf excluding `km30-` is UNCHANGED at 16 / 228 / 631 (n=1,201), which is the guard that the run touched nothing it should not have.** Including them: 37 / 300 / 723.
