### D-WS9-251 — The Neon branch was WIPED by `prisma migrate diff --shadow-database-url <the live DATABASE_URL>` (row 5 Block 1c, September 18, 2026, ~16:16Z); recovery is a point-in-time restore, and the rule that prevents a repeat: a URL with data on it is NEVER a shadow database — 🔴 INCIDENT, rule ✅ RULED (chat-Claude under delegation, September 18, 2026; the restore is HANS's step)

- Tags: `[INCIDENT]` `[DATA]` `[MIGRATION]` `[PROCESS]` `[RULED]`
- Source: the Block 1c lane's own stop report, September 18, 2026, verbatim: *"I wiped the Neon dev database… At about 16:16Z today I ran, to get Prisma to emit the 1c migration SQL non-interactively: `pnpm exec prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --shadow-database-url "<the dev DATABASE_URL>" --script`. Prisma treats a shadow database as disposable: it dropped and recreated the schema of the dev branch… to replay the 66 migrations into it."* Measured at 16:18:54Z: **35 tables, every one empty; `_prisma_migrations` does not exist.** The lane then stopped, committed nothing, ran no git command beyond `status`/`log`, and reported — the right behaviour after the wrong command.
- 🔴 **WHAT WAS LOST (until the restore): everything on the branch** — the catalog (1,308 rows as Block 1b measured it) and the rest of the 1,843 `meals` rows (1,561 with images, 282 without), the 1,646 dishes and their steps, the ingredient tables, `ai_prompts`, every user, every plan, `llm_call_logs` (the image-spend record), `_prisma_migrations` (66 rows). ✅ **Not lost: the 1,561 objects in `gs://kiwi-prod-508416-images` — nothing touched GCS — and every line of code.** ⚠️ **Cloud Run points at the SAME branch, so the production API served empty responses from 16:16Z; Hans's device pass that evening — old account "invalid credentials", the featured-meals rail gone, the wizard reporting no matches, a plan skeleton that never resolved — is entirely this incident and NOT four bugs. Nothing from that pass is minted; items 3–9 are re-run after the restore.**
- ✅ **RECOVERY — Neon point-in-time restore of the branch to `2026-09-18 16:10:00 UTC`.** The last confirmed read of real data was ~16:05Z; `migrate status` at ~16:14Z was read-only; the wipe ran ~16:16Z; no dev server was listening and Hans had not yet opened the app. Neon keeps the pre-restore state as a backup branch and the connection string does not change, so neither Cloud Run's secret nor the lane's `.env` needs an edit. ⚠️ **HANS's step — the lane has only `DATABASE_URL`, no Neon credentials, and would not have done it unasked.** ⚠️ **The restore window is finite — hours on Neon's lower plans — so it went to the top of Hans's list, ahead of everything, at 17:40Z.** Lost by the restore, deliberately: the `+62` test account Hans created after the wipe.
- ✅ **RE-VERIFICATION BEFORE ANY LANE TOUCHES THE RESTORED BRANCH (the 1c lane's first act):** `meals` = 1,843 (1,561 `imageUrl IS NOT NULL` / 282 null) · 253 forks with an image · `_prisma_migrations` = 66 applied · `users` > 0 · `SUM(costEstimateUsd)` over `mode=image` ≈ $11.59 — the Block 1b shape, the last known-good state. Then `migrate deploy` for 1c's migration, which is written and unapplied (`migrate deploy` refused it with P3005 on the wiped branch because `_prisma_migrations` was gone).
- 🔴 **RULED — THE SHADOW-DATABASE RULE, binding on every migration lane from now on (a §3.1 amendment candidate for Hans's next working-agreements batch): a URL that points at data anyone wants to keep is NEVER passed as `--shadow-database-url`, and `migrate dev` — which provisions and resets a shadow database implicitly — is never run against the shared branch.** Migration SQL comes from **`prisma migrate diff --from-url "$DATABASE_URL" --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --script`** (a read-only diff against the live schema) or is hand-written as the last three migration lanes did, and is applied with `migrate deploy`. If a shadow database is ever genuinely needed, it is a throwaway Neon branch created for the purpose and deleted after. ✅ The 1c lane has adopted this for the rest of its block and wrote the hazard to its own memory.
- ⚠️ **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: §5's "no real customer data" licence makes the branch FEEL disposable — but it holds the CATALOG, shared product data under D-WS9-230's carve-out that cost real money and hours to build (the images alone: $11.59 and 4 h 22 m; the catalog itself far more). "No real customer data" was never "no real data."** D-WS9-249 named that licence's expiry at the production release; for the data on this branch the expiry is already here.
- 🔵 **A STANDING CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED NOT RULED: the branch CC develops against and the branch Cloud Run serves are the SAME branch.** A production release cannot ship on that footing — a separate production branch (or project), with the catalog promoted into it and a non-shared `DATABASE_URL` in Secret Manager, is a **packaging-step row**. Recorded here so the packaging checklist inherits it.
- ✅ **RESTORE DONE — Hans, September 18 evening, verbatim: *"my old user was restored, the images are showing."* The branch is back; his pre-wipe account authenticates; meal images render. ⚠️ **The 1c lane's own re-verification of the 1,843 / 1,561 / 282 / 253 shape and `_prisma_migrations` = 66 is still owed and is its first act on resuming — Hans's device look confirms the restore happened, not that the counts are exact.**
- ⚠️ **NOT A SECOND INCIDENT: Hans also reported *"not all images are in."* Cause is the BINARY, not the data — his installed `preview` APK was built from `2ed7cd7`, which predates Block 2 (`51bd00a` · `67471e1`, pushed 17:5xZ). On that build `MealPickCard`, the Swap / Add-Meals / Dish-chooser sheets and `PlanOptionCard` render no image by construction, and his own 282 authored meals have none by D-WS9-230. The next `eas build` picks up all of it but the last two.**
- Owner: ✅ Hans (the restore, DONE) · 🔵 the 1c lane (re-verification, then the block). Status: ✅ **RESTORED** — 🔵 shape re-verification owed · the rule ✅ RULED.
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-248 · D-WS9-246 · D-WS9-230 · D-WS9-249 · §3.1 · §5.

### D-WS9-259 — A guest's plan is JSON on `GuestSession`, never a plan row; the claim is a FIRST PERSIST for the new account in TWO stages — ✅ RULED (Phase 0, September 25, 2026) · ✅ BUILT (row 13 Block 1, September 25; device-proven September 26)

- Tags: `[TEST-KITCHEN]` `[SERVER]` `[AUTH]` `[SCHEMA]` `[BUILT]`
- Source: row 13 Phase 0 (read-only audit) refuting `claude/kiwi_try_before_trial_scope.md` §3.1/§3.4; the corrections are that doc's §9.1.
- ✅ **Why no plan row:** `meal_plan_instances.userId`, `meal_plan_templates.userId`, `user_preferences.userId` and `wizard_last_batches.userId` are NOT NULL (RESTRICT / CASCADE). A guest never owns a plan, never forks a meal, never has a preferences row. **`GuestSession` holds `preferences` · `candidates` · `draft` (the exact `GET /wizard/drafts/:id` shape).** Rejected: a shadow `User` per guest (collides with `authLimiter`, email uniqueness, the per-user `Subscription`); a nullable `userId` on the plan tables (touches a RESTRICT FK and every `where: { userId }`).
- ✅ **The claim is TWO stages, and CC was right to refuse one:** **stage 1 inside the signup transaction** — user → subscription → `UserPreferences` from the guest blob → the guarded single-use update (`WHERE claimedAt IS NULL`; count 0 = someone else won the race → the whole signup rolls back, 409 `guest_session_invalid`); **stage 2 after the commit** — persist → finalize → materialize, because `materializeWizardDraft` needs a COMMITTED draft row and the activate route's 60 s transaction budget does not fit signup's 5 s. **A stage-2 failure leaves a good account with no plan and says so** (`claimedPlanId: null`) — ✅ **and since Block 1b Part A (`e094595`) it RELEASES the claim for retry: `releaseClaimForRetry` clears `claimedAt` / `claimedByUserId` only where this user holds it, and the response's `claimRetryable` reports whether the release actually landed; a sign-in with the same `guestSessionId` then re-claims.**
- ✅ **Sign-IN also accepts `guestSessionId`** and claims the plan WITHOUT copying preferences — a demo blob must never replace a member's allergy list. A stale session at login is logged, never refused.
- ⚠️ **Names that do not exist, so nobody looks again:** `activateWizardDraft` (the use-template body is `lib/planFromTemplate.ts::copyTemplateForUser`) · `AdminActionLog` · `req.user.id` (it is `req.userId`). The PATCH-preferences Zod is `.strict()` and EXCLUDES the wizard's two fields, hence `GuestPreferencesSchema` (wizard names → columns: `difficulty→difficultyDefault`, `weeklyPacing→weeklyPacingDefault`, `planDurationDays→planLengthDefault`).
- ✅ **Measured on the device, September 26:** claim signup 201 in 9.9 s, `claimedPlanId` set, 5-meal plan, `firstPlanCreatedAt` set, 0 AI calls during the claim; a second signup with the used session → 409, no second user; deleting the claimant leaves the session row with `claimedByUserId` NULL (ON DELETE SET NULL).
- ⚠️ **Block 1's comment "so the mobile draft screen renders a guest plan through the code path it already has" described a screen that no longer exists** — Block 2 built `app/test-kitchen/plan` over `GET /guest/draft` instead (D-WS9-263).
- Owner: ✅ Block 1 (`b75bfa7`…`a7f0e81`, local). Status: ✅ BUILT — 🔵 UNDEPLOYED (store-review freeze; migration `20260925170000_row13_b1_guest_sessions` is on PRODUCTION already — D-WS9-266).
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-260 · 261 · 262 · 263 · scope doc §9 · BUG-262.

### D-WS9-263 — A Test Kitchen sign-up COMPLETES onboarding; the first Home shows a "personalize" nudge instead of a second form; the guest wizard hides sauces and both dials and NEVER saves a hidden default — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 26, 2026)

- Tags: `[TEST-KITCHEN]` `[ONBOARDING]` `[UX]` `[SERVER]` `[WEB]` `[RULED]`
- Source: Block 1's device audit, finding 3 — after a claim `onboardingComplete` was FALSE, and the app's root redirect sends such a user to onboarding step 2, **which pre-fills from an in-memory draft, not the saved preferences** — they would have seen defaults and been asked everything again.
- ✅ **Hans:** *"agreed we don't want them to have to go to the same form, unpopulated, after saving."* **Ruled:** when the claim's preferences copy succeeded, stage 1 also sets `onboardingComplete = true` (an unreadable blob keeps onboarding required). The user lands on Home — on the web after a web sign-up, in the app on first sign-in there.
- ✅ **The nudge, copy ruled (option A):** *"Your plan is saved. Welcome to Kiwi! The Test Kitchen only asked the basics. Tell Kiwi how you really cook — your skill, your gear, who's at the table — and every plan after this one fits you better. [Personalize my plans] [Later]"* — primary button opens Preferences (everything named is editable there: skill, equipment, kids, picky eaters, spice, budget). **Shown on the first Home of EACH surface (web, then app) until they personalize;** "Later" is per device (client-local); `User.personalizeNudgeDismissedAt` flips on opening Preferences or saving them; `GET /home` derives `showPersonalizeNudge` for `signupSource = test_kitchen` only.
- ✅ **The guest form (Block 2):** the app's wizard, with **sauces hidden (runs as `balanced`) and "The mix" hidden (both dials off — a guest has no playlist, and a "discovery" meal means one this user has not been served, which for a guest is every meal).** ⚠️ **Rejected: sending `discoveryLevel: all` for guests** — same plan for the guest, and a saved "all" would make every future plan 100 % never-seen dishes. **Rule: the claim copies what the guest ANSWERED; a hidden default is never saved.** Two more Block 2 requirements found reading the wizard as a guest: the collapsed *"Adjust saved prefs for this plan"* disclosure (which holds cuisines / eating styles / **allergies**) must be EXPANDED and retitled for a guest, and the payload builder must send those fields for a guest (today `hydratedSlice` sends them only when stored preferences loaded — a guest's allergies would be silently dropped).
- ✅ **An existing account that tries to sign UP from the Test Kitchen gets the ordinary duplicate-email refusal — correct** (Hans: *"they should have been logged in or using the app to generate a plan"*). Sign-in from the door already claims the plan without touching stored preferences (D-WS9-259) and shows no nudge.
- ✅ **Server half BUILT — Block 1b Part B2 (`07cf499`, September 27, local, undeployed):** `ClaimInTxResult.preferencesCopied` drives `onboardingComplete` in the same transaction (a second `tx.user.update` — the decision depends on the claim's result, so it cannot precede the create); `onboardingRequired` is derived, never a literal; the dismissal is one guarded write-if-null in `lib/personalizeNudge.ts`, called from `PATCH /me/ui-state` and (best-effort) a successful `PATCH /me/preferences`; `GET /home` returns `showPersonalizeNudge` from its existing narrow user read. **Two user-shape builders exist and both carry the new fields** — `toUserShape` (signup · login · `/auth/me`) and a hand-rolled `select` in `PATCH /me/profile`; the fields are REQUIRED on `toUserShape`'s input type so a forgetful `select` fails to typecheck. An app that has not updated ignores the new Home field (mobile's `HomePayloadSchema` is a plain `z.object`, which strips unknown keys). Migration `20260926221500_row13_b1b_signup_source_nudge` written, NOT applied (freeze).
- ✅ **`otherAllergies` in the claim (1b Part C) is plumbing for a field that is DARK in every client** — `OTHER_ALLERGIES_FIELD_ENABLED = false` per D-WS9-206's ship gate, and `WizardInputSchema` does not carry the key. When D-WS9-211's honouring mechanism is built, the wizard schema gains it in the same block. No gap today; no ID.
- ✅ **Client half BUILT — row 13 Block 2 (September 27, branch `next`, commits `ac56ed6` B · `ff3eed2` C · `c795aeb` D · `db076b1` E · `79b9cc6` F · `a641186` B-fix; mobile suite 1,846 / 0 fail, +97; `expo export --platform web` exits 0; `app.json` untouched; audited PASS). What the tree changed about the design: **three NEW guest screens** (`app/test-kitchen/{index,options,plan,recipe}`) rather than reusing `plan-options` / `plan/[id]` / `meal/[id]` — every one of those is member-only on mount (SSE stream, `GET /plans/:id`, member meal reads) and `getWizardDraft` had no screen caller left since D-WS9-191; a guest's draft carries NO cooking steps (finalize runs at save/activate, both doors), so "read the full recipe" is served by `sourceStoreMealId → GET /meals/:id`, now typed; **a guest token on a member route is a 401, never a 403** (measured with no server: `verifyToken(token, "session")` returns null on `purpose: "guest"`), and since an authenticated 401 IS the session-expired cascade, the design is an ALLOWLIST of guest routes, never a 403 handler; the 409 `guest_session_invalid` rolls the whole sign-up back (stage 1 is inside the user-creating transaction), so the client RESENDS once without the session and says the plan expired; `onboardingRequired` was parsed and never read before this block (sign-up routed unconditionally to onboarding — pre-existing, fixed here, no bug entry per §28.1); `sessionGateShouldEvict` would have evicted every guest on mount (fixed, 5 cases added to the EXISTING test file); guest generation is BUFFERED, not the SSE stream (a second principal in `wizardStream.ts` risked the member cascade) — ⚠️ the guest waits ~16–24 s with no progressive cards: the first browser pass judges whether the loading state carries it; `maxCookTimeCoverage` rides only when a cap is chosen (otherwise it is a hidden default); doors are VISIBLE CTAs (a visitor should see the grocery list exists); the guest token lives in `sessionStorage` like the member token; the nudge is `showPersonalizeNudge` bare-optional (a `.default(false)` diverges Zod's input/output types and breaks `apiClient`'s generic — measured TS2719).
- Owner: ✅ Block 1b (server) · ✅ Block 2 (client). Status: ✅ RULED — ✅ BUILT both halves, UNDEPLOYED — 🔵 browser pass owed (Block 3).
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-259 · D-WS9-264 · D-WS9-256 (the first-run family) · D-WS7-035 (per-run overrides never write back) · scope doc §8.2–8.3.

### D-WS9-266 — Split the database into PRODUCTION and DEV now, during the store-review freeze: Cloud Run stays on the branch it already uses (it becomes production), and local development moves to a Neon CHILD branch — ✅ RULED (Hans raised, September 27, 2026; the mechanism chat-Claude's under delegation)

- Tags: `[INFRA]` `[NEON]` `[LAUNCH]` `[SAFETY]` `[RULED]`
- Source: Hans, September 27: *"I think maybe we should do the sandbox/production branching setup soon so dev can keep going safely… I told it to hold off last time so we didn't mess up the submissions. once I have confidence we won't break that stuff I'm happy to do more."* The packaging list already required *"a PRODUCTION Neon branch before public"* (D-WS9-249); the freeze makes it urgent, because today every local device run writes to a database the store reviewers may be using.
- ✅ **THE SHAPE, and why it is freeze-safe:** nothing about Cloud Run changes — no deploy, no secret change. Its current branch simply BECOMES production (it holds the 1,300-meal catalog, the images' rows, the reviewer account). A Neon child branch is copy-on-write and instant, so **dev starts as an exact copy of production** (catalog included) and the local `.env` `DATABASE_URL` is repointed to it. From then on local lanes, device scripts and migrations touch only dev.
- 🔴 **PREREQUISITE — THE OPEN QUESTION FIRST:** the local `.env` endpoint is NOT in the Neon project Hans can see (position block). Step 1 is to print the HOST (never the credential) of both URLs — the local `.env` and Cloud Run's database secret — and compare. **If they differ, local dev may already be isolated but on an unknown and possibly stale database (the row 13 migration went there), and the split is then "make dev a child of the CLOUD RUN branch, repoint `.env`, retire the unknown one."**
- ⚠️ **Consequences to carry:** migrations are applied to dev first and to production at deploy (§3.1 rule 14 — `migrate status` against production's URL comes first) · the image drain runs only on Cloud Run against production, so a dev-created meal gets no image unless the drain is run locally (acceptable) · the GCS bucket stays shared (images are write-once by key — no collision) · the `SystemSetting` flags (the Instacart flag) are per-branch after the split — flip them on the branch you mean · a dev branch can be RESET to production's current state in one click, which is the clean way to refresh it.
- ✅ **BUILT September 27, 2026.** Measured first: the local `.env` and Cloud Run's `DATABASE_URL` secret pointed at the SAME endpoint, `ep-royal-butterfly-am5ajo4w` (branch `production`, `br-delicate-sky-amieeehs`, project "Kiwi" `odd-dew-83625464`) — so the row 13 Block 1 migration applied on September 26 went to PRODUCTION (additive: new tables and a nullable column the deployed code never reads; nothing a reviewer sees changed). ⚠️ **The "endpoint not in Hans's Neon project" line was WRONG** — the project has one Neon project; the September 26 SQL-editor mismatch was the console pointed at the 2-day-old child branch `Branch1 9826` (`ep-calm-water-amqaag9u`), harmless, deletable. Chat-Claude created branch **`dev`** (`br-summer-shadow-amgn5roi`, endpoint **`ep-broad-haze-am9ca2gv`**, parent `production`, current point in time, auto-delete NEVER — the console's default was 1 day) through the browser; the device bridge REFUSES writes to `.env` by design, so Hans swapped the host in `artifacts/api-server/.env` himself (backup of the production `.env` at `%USERPROFILE%\kiwi-env-prod-backup.txt`, outside every repo), then `migrate status` on dev showed the one pending migration (`20260926221500_row13_b1b_signup_source_nudge`) and `migrate deploy` + `migrate status` → up to date. **Production still lacks that migration — it applies with Block 1's deploy after approval (`migrate status` against production FIRST).** ⚠️ `migrate status` exits 1 whenever a migration is pending — the `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC_FIRST_FAIL` line is expected there, not a failure. Ignore Prisma's "update to 8.0" banner: Prisma is pinned to 6 and npm is banned (§6).

### D-WS9-267 — CHECKOUT RAILS: Stripe web checkout EVERYWHERE — web sign-ups pay on the web, and the apps link out to Stripe in the external browser; no Apple in-app purchase, no Google Play Billing — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 27, 2026: *"option: a."*)

- Tags: `[STRIPE]` `[BILLING]` `[1.1]` `[STORE]` `[RULED]`
- Source: `kiwi_business_plan.md` §3's open "IAP vs web checkout rails" question, put to Hans as the one ruling on 1.1's critical path after he pulled row 9 forward (roadmap, September 27).
- ✅ **What was ruled, and the three options it beat:** (a) Stripe web checkout everywhere — RULED · (b) store billing in the apps plus Stripe on the web — rejected: two or three billing systems, 15% on in-app sales, a larger 1.1 with a closer billing review · (c) store billing only — impossible, because the web Test Kitchen cannot use store billing.
- **The US rules as researched September 27, 2026 (chat-Claude is not a lawyer; the rules are in active litigation):** Apple's US storefront has allowed links to an external web checkout since May 2025 with no commission, no entitlement and no requirement to also offer IAP; the Ninth Circuit (December 11, 2025) remanded for the district court to set a permissible commission, and the Supreme Court granted certiorari June 30, 2026 (argument this term). Google Play Billing is no longer mandatory in the US; linking out requires enrollment in the External Content Links program, whose fees (proposed ~10% on subscriptions) apply from late 2026. Sources: tiun.io "iOS external payments in the US: what they actually cost in 2026"; RevenueCat "App-to-web purchase guidelines"; Play Console Help answers 15582165 and 16497028.
- ⚠️ **The risk accepted with it:** a court-set Apple commission on link-outs could arrive later — it would apply to in-app link-outs only, never to Test Kitchen (web) sign-ups. **Re-check both stores' rules at 1.1's scoping and again before submission; a rule change there is not a reason to re-open this ruling without Hans.**
- 🔵 **Consequences for 1.1's scope:** no store-billing SDK (no RevenueCat / StoreKit / Play Billing module) · the in-app upgrade opens Stripe Checkout in the EXTERNAL browser (Apple requires the full browser, not an in-app web view) with a neutral notice before redirect · Google Play: enroll in the External Content Links program before 1.1 ships to Play, and meet its disclosure screen · subscription state flows Stripe webhook → server → app refetch; the return to the app is a universal link (1.1 already carries universal links) · the web sign-up (Test Kitchen and `app.kitchenwizard.ai`) checks out natively with Stripe.
- ✅ **AMENDED September 27, 2026 — THE TRIAL IS NO-CARD (Hans: *"no card - ruled"*).** 14 days, full premium, no payment method collected at sign-up; the card is asked for when the trial ends. It matches every promise already on screen — the sign-up's shipped *"14-day free trial · no credit card needed"* (D-WS9-138) and the Test Kitchen's *"no account, no card"* — and the business plan's own note that no-card trials convert at ~8–25% but start in far greater numbers; a first launch wants sign-ups and retention data before revenue. Rejected: card-upfront (fewer, better-qualified trials; every trial promise on screen would change).
- 🔵 **Still open, ruled at 1.1's scoping, not here:** the post-trial state (read-only vs locked; business plan §3's direction is read-only) · Stripe Tax · whether 1.1 on Android waits for the Play program enrollment.
- Owner: 🔵 row 9 (1.1). Status: ✅ RULED — 🔵 unbuilt.
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-020 (trial-then-paywall) · D-WS9-249 · D-WS9-258 (no price or trial copy in the first binary) · roadmap row 9 and "When marketing starts" · `kiwi_business_plan.md` §3.

### D-WS9-268 — Sign in with Apple and Google, SERVER: one `user_identities` table, tokens verified against the providers' published keys, unverified emails REFUSED, Apple tokens revoked on account deletion — ✅ BUILT (row 9 OAuth Block 1, September 27, 2026, branch `next`; design chat-Claude's under delegation, decided points CC's, all accepted at audit)

- Tags: `[AUTH]` `[OAUTH]` `[1.1]` `[SERVER]` `[SCHEMA]` `[SECURITY]` `[BUILT]`
- Source: PRD §3.3 / §3.7 (locked: "Continue with Apple" / "Continue with Google" on sign-up and sign-in; Meta future); OQ-3.3's default (accept Hide My Email); App Review 5.1.1(v). Commits `ab5fb5d` A · `b8b6f73` B · `f5b8bdd` C · `58c2a0a` D · `c6bd5a3` E · `13e2fc6`; server suite 2,729 / 2,727 / 0 fail / 2 skipped (+90); tsc clean; **no new package** — `googleOidc.ts` (row 5's Cloud Scheduler verifier) already held the JWKS machinery and became `lib/oauth/jwks.ts`, re-exported so the drain is byte-identical; ⚠️ reverting the OAuth lane now takes that file with it.
- ✅ **Shape:** `UserIdentity { userId CASCADE, provider (apple|google), subject, emailAtLink, emailVerified, isPrivateRelay, appleRefreshTokenEnc, appleClientId, timestamps }`, unique `(provider, subject)`; `users.passwordHash` was already nullable. Migration `20260927120000_row9_oauth_user_identities` — additive; **applied to DEV by Hans September 27; production at the 1.1 deploy.**
- ✅ **Routes:** `POST /auth/oauth/apple { identityToken, rawNonce, authorizationCode?, … }` · `POST /auth/oauth/google { idToken, … }` → the signup/login response + `isNewUser`; `201` new / `200` returning; every verification failure is one generic `401` (reason in the log); a provider whose audience list is unset → `503 oauth_unavailable`. Both on `authLimiter`; both added to `KNOWN_PUBLIC` with their reasoning (the credential is the body, checked against Apple's/Google's keys).
- 🔴 **Resolution order:** `(provider, subject)` → that user · else a VERIFIED email matching an existing user → link · else create (names body → token → empty; consents and phone on CREATE only). **Google `email_verified: false` → REFUSE, not create** (an account created on an unverified claim of someone else's address would be linked INTO by the real owner's later verified sign-in — a takeover). **A token with no email and an unknown subject → refuse** (nothing to put in `users.email`; a synthetic address is an account nobody can recover). Identity facts refresh on every sign-in; `userId` is never rewritten. A `P2002` race on the unique index retries once as branch (a).
- 🔴 **The nonce contract, Apple only: `nonce` claim === lower-case hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 raw nonce the client sends.** A client that base64s the digest 401s a valid token. Google: no nonce (optional in its native flows; requiring it refuses correct clients).
- ✅ **Revocation (5.1.1(v)):** the Apple route exchanges the one-time `authorizationCode` at `/auth/token` with a per-call ES256 client-secret JWT (10-minute TTL, never stored; `APPLE_TEAM_ID` / `APPLE_KEY_ID` / `APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY`), stores the refresh token AES-256-GCM-encrypted (key via HKDF-SHA256 from `APPLE_REFRESH_TOKEN_ENC_KEY`; versioned `v1.` blob; explicitly not a KMS — `v2.` is where Cloud KMS would go); `DELETE /me` calls `/auth/revoke` per Apple identity BEFORE deleting — best-effort, logged, never blocks the delete. The audience list is the per-provider switch; revocation unconfigured = sign-in works and the boot line logs an ERROR (a submission in that state is rejectable). `appleClientId` is recorded from the token's `aud` because `/auth/revoke` needs the exact client id and the audience list has two.
- ✅ **Env (names only; values from Apple Developer / Google Cloud; documented in `DEPLOY.md`):** `APPLE_OAUTH_AUDIENCES` (bundle id + Services ID) · `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_IDS` (web + iOS + Android) · `APPLE_TEAM_ID` · `APPLE_KEY_ID` · `APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY` (Secret Manager) · `APPLE_REFRESH_TOKEN_ENC_KEY` (Secret Manager; rotating it orphans stored tokens — logged, deletion proceeds). BUG-263's boot line validates all six; the no-leakage test covers them.
- ✅ **Reuse:** signup's transaction body and stage 2 moved to `lib/authAccount.ts` (`createAccountInTx` / `finishClaimAfterCommit`) — password signup and login were already two near-identical copies; the OAuth routes are callers three and four; the Test Kitchen claim rides them unchanged (new user → copy preferences + complete onboarding; returning → claim only).
- ⚠️ **Process, worth the line:** `git restore` on a still-UNTRACKED file is a silent no-op — CC's post-restore hash caught it and it restored by the Edit tool. The hash check is the restore check (§27.4), not the command's exit.
- 🔵 **Owed to the client block:** the nonce encoding above; `expo-apple-authentication` returns the name only once — forward it. **Still open for 1.1 scoping:** card-upfront vs no-card trial · post-trial state · Play's External Content Links enrollment (D-WS9-267).
- 🔵 **Server follow-up found by the client block:** `exchangeAppleAuthorizationCode` sends no `redirect_uri`, and Apple requires it for a code issued to a Services ID — so a WEB Apple sign-in's code cannot be exchanged today and the client deliberately does not forward it; a web-only Apple account therefore has no refresh token to revoke at `DELETE /me`. Fix: pass `redirect_uri` (the same value as `EXPO_PUBLIC_APPLE_WEB_REDIRECT_URI`) when the token's `aud` is the Services ID, then the client forwards the web code. Rides the next server lane (Stripe S1).
- ✅ **`redirect_uri` follow-up DONE — Stripe S1 Part F (`692ed63`, September 27):** optional env pair `APPLE_SERVICES_ID` + `APPLE_WEB_REDIRECT_URI`; when the verified token's `aud === APPLE_SERVICES_ID` the code exchange sends `redirect_uri`; both unset = today's behaviour with one boot-line note. The Services ID must ALSO be in `APPLE_OAUTH_AUDIENCES`. ⚠️ **S1 also found `.env.example` did not list the six OAuth vars this block added (BUG-318, fixed in the same commit).**
- Owner: ✅ server · ✅ client (D-WS9-269). Status: ✅ BUILT both halves (dev only; production at the 1.1 deploy) — ✅ the `redirect_uri` follow-up (S1).
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-267 · D-WS9-257 (`DELETE /me`) · D-WS9-259 / 263 (the claim) · D-WS9-248 (the verifier's origin) · PRD §3.3 · roadmap row 9.

### D-WS9-270 — Stripe billing, the September 27 rulings: read-only after the trial with NO AI of any kind; a fresh 14-day trial for every existing account at cutover; PAY EARLY, GET MORE (subscribe during the trial → first charge at trial end + 14 bonus days); $9.99 / $99.99; Stripe Tax on; Google's native button label stays Google's; D-WS9-143 closed — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 27, 2026; scope `claude/kiwi_stripe_scope.md` v2 §4a, §5a, §12)

- Tags: `[BUSINESS]` `[MONETIZATION]` `[STRIPE]` `[FEATUREGATES]` `[1.1]` `[RULED]`
- Source: chat-Claude's scope v1 (seven recommendations) → Hans: *"that all looks good"*, with two refinements below. Closes D-WS9-020's sub-decisions (2) and (4); (1) and (3) closed on D-WS9-267.
- ✅ **1. Post-trial state = READ-ONLY, and "No Pay / No Trial = No AI."** Hans asked whether any *"fraction of a penny"* AI calls could stay on for lapsed accounts so the app functions. Ruled: none. The app functions without AI — cookbook, saved plans and recipes with their steps, the grocery list (deterministic), Instacart (no model call), catalog search. The cheap call is the door to the expensive one, a free key needs its own ceiling, and one sentence beats a whitelist. **Kept revisitable with numbers:** the entitlement matrix is one table (`ENTITLEMENTS: Record<EntitlementKey, "paid" | "free">` — a key goes free in one server line, no store review), and S1 reports the median `costEstimateUsd` per `promptKey` from `llm_call_logs` (30 days) so the small calls are named with a measured price. Entitled statuses: `trialing`, `active`, `past_due`; locked: `none`, `canceled` (402 `subscription_required`; reads still work). The Test Kitchen is unaffected (D-WS9-261).
- ✅ **2. Cutover:** every existing `trialing` row with an expired `trialEndsAt` gets `cutover + 14 d`; staff and reviewer accounts a far-future date (no `comped` enum). Enforcement sits behind `BILLING_ENFORCED` (default OFF) and is flipped by Hans after 1.1 is live and Stripe is commissioned — S1 can deploy with zero lock-out risk.
- ✅ **3. PAY EARLY, GET MORE (Hans's refinement, an experiment):** *"sign up after the first meal plan or grocery generation or instacart call, and if you buy now you get the rest of your trial + 2 weeks applied to the end of your subscription term."* Mechanism: a trialing user's Checkout Session carries `subscription_data.trial_end = trialEndsAt + BILLING_EARLY_PAY_BONUS_DAYS` (env, default 14) — card on file, **first charge on that date**, the paid term starts then; to Stripe it is a trial with a card (no proration, no credits; Stripe's own trial-ending reminder email stays ON — card-network and FTC rules want a reminder before a card on file is first charged). After the trial lapses there is no bonus. **Moments (S2):** the upsell sheet after the FIRST plan, the first grocery list, the first Instacart handoff — a config list, once each, dismissible, never blocking — plus Settings and the trial banner. `GET /me/subscription` returns `earlyPayBonusDays` + `firstChargeDateIfSubscribedNow` so no client does the date math. `earlyPayBonusApplied` on the row measures the experiment. Accepted risk: take the offer day 1, cancel before the charge = 28 free days, bounded by the same AI ceilings.
- ✅ **4. Prices:** $9.99 monthly · $99.99 annual (PRD §14.2 redline confirmed).
- ✅ **5. Stripe Tax ON at launch** (`automatic_tax`, prices tax-exclusive) **+ an accountant on the Massachusetts registration** (MA taxes SaaS); other states' economic nexus is a later-volume question.
- ✅ **6. Google's native button = Google's rendering, "Sign in with Google"** (D-WS9-269 option (a)); no hand-rolled row.
- ✅ **7. D-WS9-143 CLOSED:** the trial row keeps `planCode = free`; `planCode` follows the Stripe price once a subscription exists; entitlement reads status only.
- ✅ **Also standing from scope v1, unobjected:** the trial is Kiwi's (`trialEndsAt`; no Stripe object until checkout), the webhook is the truth for everything after; `none` is DERIVED on read (no nightly job); grace = Stripe's 7-day Smart Retries then cancel (no second timer); promo codes = Stripe Promotion Codes in Checkout, Kiwi's `PromoCode` table dormant (row 17 decides); trial-abuse guard on the web rails = the existing guards + the ceilings, accepted for launch; `DELETE /me` cancels a live Stripe subscription before deleting (best-effort, logged).
- 🔵 **Owed at S3 (Hans, after the 1.0 approval):** Stripe live mode + two Products/Prices · webhook endpoint + signing secret · Customer Portal config (plan switch + cancel; trial-ending emails on) · Stripe Tax registration · Play External Content Links enrollment timing (D-WS9-267) · the seven env values on Cloud Run · the cutover SQL, then `BILLING_ENFORCED=true`.

### D-WS9-272 — What a LAPSED account sees where AI used to run: saved macros are never overwritten, an existing grocery list is never wiped by a forced reconcile, and a premium notice replaces silence — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 27, 2026, on reading the S1 report)

- Tags: `[STRIPE]` `[FEATUREGATES]` `[UX]` `[1.1]` `[RULED]`
- Source: Hans, verbatim, on S1's graceful-denial design (D-WS9-271): *"when macros stop calculating, like an expired user clicking the day button on a meal which calls the macro calculation. if they have saved macros it either shouldn't update, or it should flip to 'macros are a premium feature, upgrade to get unlimited access to all features' or something like that so there's no confusion. similarly, when grocery lists are generated, the user should see what they had. if they edit a meal, it forces a grocery reconciliation, which might wipe the old list. I'd rather just alert the user 'list was generated during your trial and may not reflect changes in your plan. upgrade to get unlimited access to all features'."*
- ✅ **Rule 1 — never destroy a saved value to enforce a gate.** A `none`/`canceled` account keeps every macro figure and every grocery list it already has. No gated path may write zeros over saved macros or replace a list with an empty/partial one. **Server check owed (S2's lane, or a tiny S1b if it needs the server):** every route that today "saves at zero with a warn" (`meal_macro_estimate` on `POST /me/meals` / `/me/dishes`, BUG-274's path) must, for an EDIT of a meal that already has macros, leave the stored macros untouched; a NEW meal with no macros yet saves with macros absent/null, never a fabricated zero. `plan_macro_recalc` (402) changes nothing on the plan. `grocery_list_reconcile` already keeps the prior state (`reconciled: false`, stamp untouched) — that stays; `grocery_list_generate` (402) never clears an existing list.
- ✅ **Rule 2 — silence is a bug; the user is told, in the place they looked, and offered the upgrade.** Copy, ruled in shape (Hans's words, S2 may tighten): macros — *"Macros are a premium feature. Upgrade to get unlimited access to all features."* where the figure would have updated (the day button, the meal's macro strip, the plan's macro recalc); grocery — *"This list was generated during your trial and may not reflect changes to your plan. Upgrade to get unlimited access to all features."* on a list whose `reconciled: false` was caused by the gate, and the same on any attempt to generate a new list. Each notice carries the upgrade action (opens the paywall sheet). ⚠️ **The server must let the client tell the two apart:** a reconcile skipped for ENTITLEMENT vs a reconcile that FAILED is the same `reconciled: false` today — S2's server touch adds a reason (`reconcileSkipped: "subscription_required"` or equivalent) so the trial notice never shows to a paying user whose reconcile merely errored.
- ✅ **General form, for every graceful denial in D-WS9-271's table:** keep what exists · do not pretend the call ran · say why in place · offer the upgrade. `find_similar_ai`'s cuisine-only fallback gets the same one-line notice on the results ("Kiwi's smart matches are a premium feature — these are cuisine matches. Upgrade…").
- Owner: S2 client lane (+ its small server touch). Status: ✅ RULED · ✅ BUILT in S2 (D-WS9-273) — with two honest amendments: macros cannot be "absent" (the columns are non-nullable `@default(0)`), so the wire carries `macrosSkipped` instead; and the meal EDIT path was never gated, pinned by test.
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-270 · D-WS9-271 · BUG-274 · `claude/kiwi_stripe_scope.md` v3 §4 / §13a.

### D-WS9-277 — Shortcut (swappable-component) paths: show whichever path EXISTS; the web Cookbook gets the shortcut toggle when row 3c ships it ("a great selling point"); the app's recipe-payload fix rides the grocery pass — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 28, 2026)

- Tags: `[3C]` `[COMPONENTS]` `[WEBSITE]` `[RULED]`
- Source: Hans on the Cookbook Block 2 audit: *"agreed - if no shortcut, or no from scratch, just show that's there. but to your specific point, if only shortcut, show shortcut. once we get to shortcut toggling, I want that in the web UI so users can see it. it's a great selling point, and can alleviate concerns about 'oh, all these meals require a LOT of steps and cooking' vs. 'oh, I just toggle to something easy for me'."*
- ✅ **Rule 1 — show the path that exists.** A component with BOTH paths: from-scratch by default. A component with ONLY bought (shortcut) steps: show the shortcut steps — they are the recipe (fixes Sopes `380a9de3` and Breakfast Burritos `3342a6ed`, and the eight harmless no-scratch cases). A component with only scratch: scratch. Applies to the web generator AND the app's recipe payload.
- ✅ **Rule 2 — the web shows the toggle.** When row 3c builds shortcut toggling in the app, the Cookbook pages get it too: a visible per-component choice ("Make it from scratch" / "Shortcut: store-bought …") that swaps the steps (and, when 3c tags them, the ingredients) on the page. Static pages can carry both paths and a tiny script to switch; the JSON-LD stays the from-scratch recipe. Marketing framing, Hans's: it answers "these meals are a LOT of cooking."
- ✅ **Rule 3 — the app fix is small and goes first:** the recipe payload (`composeMealDetail` / `composeLoadedMealDetail`, `api-server/src/routes/meals.ts`) calls the existing `selectDefaultPathSteps()` (from `cookingScheduler.ts`) extended with Rule 1, so the member meal / dish screens and the Test Kitchen stop showing both paths on 1,083 meals. **Rides the grocery-list pass (server; no store review; deploys after approval).** Row 3c then builds the toggle UI on top.
- ✅ **Rule 3 BUILT on DEV (grocery B3, `43dd340`, September 29):** the payload returns base + one path; the scheduler falls back to bought when only bought exists (BUG-121). The client accepts the path fields in grocery block C.
- Owner: grocery pass (Rule 3 + Rule 1 in the app) · next Cookbook touch (Rule 1 on the web) · row 3c (Rule 2, both surfaces). Status: ✅ RULED.
- Cross-ref: BUG-322 · D-WS9-066 (Block 3.7 tagging) · D-WS9-276 · roadmap rows 3c, 14.

### D-WS9-278 — The Cookbook's daily run adds a QUICK-DINNER slot: 10 ranked pages + 1 dinner of 30 minutes or less, until they run out — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 28, 2026; the form is chat-Claude's call, delegated)

- Tags: `[WEBSITE]` `[COOKBOOK]` `[SEO]` `[RULED]`
- Source: chat-Claude found on the live site that only 3 of 110 pages pass the "30 minutes or less" filter and recommended publishing quick dinners sooner. Hans: *"agreed on the 30 minute dinners. or we just do 11 per day and include 1 per day instead of 1 of the 10. your call."*
- 🔴 **Correction to chat-Claude's own premise, measured on the queue the same hour:** the "95 thirty-minute meals" do not exist. The `km30` supplement was TARGETED at 30 minutes; its honest times run 15–75 minutes and **only 21 of the 95 are ≤ 30**. **The whole catalog holds 35 publishable dinners ≤ 30 minutes** (14 spined + 21 `km30`), 3 of them live. And the drip was not "months away" from the supplement: the daily run draws one page from each decile, and the tail decile IS the supplement, so one `km30` meal publishes most days — mostly ones over 30 minutes.
- ✅ **The ruling:** **11 a day** — the ten decile picks unchanged, plus ONE quick-dinner pick = the highest-ranked ELIGIBLE unpublished meal with `estimatedTimeMinutes` ≤ 30 (same eligibility as the draw: next version of its family, family spacing respected, not flagged, not excluded; never the same family as a decile pick that day). **No eligible quick dinner → no extra page** (the slot switches itself off when they run out, and wakes for any new one the catalog gains). Why 11 rather than 1 of the 10: it leaves the ruled popularity drip (D-WS9-274) untouched.
- Expected drain: ~27 eligible now, about four weeks; the rest follow as family spacing releases them.
- Owner: Cookbook Block 3. Status: ✅ RULED, unbuilt.

### D-WS9-279 — 🔴 NO over-the-air update to the 1.0 binaries from `next`: both branches resolve to runtimeVersion "1.0.0", and `next` carries three native modules the 1.0 binary does not have — client-side grocery fixes ride 1.1; `version` goes to 1.1.0 on `next` before any `eas update` is ever run — ✅ RULED (chat-Claude, delegated technical call, September 28, 2026; Hans's objection window open)

- Tags: `[RELEASE]` `[OTA]` `[FREEZE]` `[RULED]`
- Source: the grocery census Part A8 (branch facts), verified by chat-Claude against `app.json` / `eas.json` on `next` the same hour.
- **The facts:** `next` is a strict fast-forward descendant of `ws7-in-progress` (31 commits ahead; the grocery engine files are byte-identical on both). Both declare `runtimeVersion: { policy: "appVersion" }` over `version: "1.0.0"`, the same `updates.url` and project id, and `eas.json`'s production profile puts every build on channel `production`. **So an `eas update --channel production` published from `next` today would be SERVED to the 1.0 store binaries** — and `next` adds `expo-apple-authentication`, `@react-native-google-signin/google-signin` and `expo-crypto` (native, plus the Apple Sign-In entitlement). The failure would arrive at runtime as a missing native module on the screens that import them (or at launch, if the import is hoisted); `expo-updates` rolls back only on a launch crash.
- ✅ **Rule 1: nothing is ever published over the air to the 1.0 binaries.** The roadmap's "grocery pass ships OTA beside 1.1" is amended: **server-side fixes deploy to Cloud Run after approval (additive, 1.0-compatible); client-side fixes ride the 1.1 binary.** An OTA line for 1.0 would need its own branch off `ws7-in-progress` with no new native modules; the 1.0 window is short and the client fixes are small, so it is not worth a second branch.
- ✅ **Rule 2: before the first `eas update` of any kind, `version` on `next` is 1.1.0** (the 1.1 build carries it anyway). With `appVersion` policy that makes every future update target runtime 1.1.0 and the 1.0 binaries never match. This is one line in `app.json`; it lands with the 1.1 packaging commit, and it is on the after-approval chain as a gate.
- ⚠️ **Not knowable from the repo, recorded so nobody re-derives it:** which commit the 1.0 binaries were built from (no tags, no build record; `appVersionSource: "remote"` keeps build numbers on EAS). `2720485` says the expo patch drift "rides the first post-submission update".
- Owner: the after-approval chain (`kiwi_go_live_todos.md` §G) · the 1.1 packaging prompt. Status: ✅ RULED.
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-249 · D-WS9-258 · roadmap "Tier 1" · `claude/kiwi_grocery_pass_scope.md` §6.

BUG-329; BUG-326's range guard; R3's annotated recurring line once B2 makes it reachable) · **D — BUG-320** · **E — the corpus re-run + a numbered device pass.** Client parts ride 1.1 (D-WS9-279).
- 🔴 **THE R2 TOLERANCE, AS FIRST PROPOSED, WAS WRONG — HANS CAUGHT IT (September 28), VERBATIM:** *"I don't want users to not have enough. and on vegetables, I don't want them to have to throw out 3/4 head of cilantro because they needed a little more than their head. so the 1/4 unit rule on produce could work fine. but if one recipe needs a head of cabbage and another needs 2 cups, they need more than 1 head of cabbage. And iceberg probably shreds to 4 cups. I think the issue may be more about converting prep to purchased sizes than rounding logic."* ⚠️ Chat-Claude's "cabbage 1 head + 2 cups stays 1 head" forgave a whole recipe's cabbage — a quarter-pack tolerance is an under-buy dressed as thrift. **The reframe is his and it is right: the conversion is the work, not the rounding.** Revised proposal (awaiting his yes): **(1) a prep-to-purchase YIELD table for produce sold whole (cups shredded per head, cups chopped per bunch …) is the deliverable — authored as data, reviewed by class, reversible; the census showed the existing CSV is unit-incoherent for several foods; (2) convert every need through it, sum in pack units, ROUND UP — never under-buy; (3) the only forgiveness is a garnish: an eighth of a pack or less, fresh herbs and produce only** (1 bunch + 2 tbsp cilantro → 1 bunch; 1 head cabbage + 2 cups → 2 heads; 2 cups iceberg → 1 head). The build prints every produce row with its computed packs as a numbered list for Hans to read — the boundary is tuned there, on data, not in chat.
- ✅ **RULED (Hans, September 28): *"agreed on the updated rule. that's great."*** And the reuse constraint, verbatim: *"we do have a matching table and logic already, so be on the lookout before we build another. I think the table just created the 'whack a mole' testing issues because we would solve 'chipotles in adobo' ordering 2 cans because a recipe asked for 3 peppers + 2 tbsp sauce. that's ONE can, but two pieces of the can. we had similar issues for a while with cilantro, where it was breaking it out into stems, leaves, and 'head' of cilantro."* 🔴 **So R2 builds NO new table.** The homes exist: `IngredientRelation` component edges with `yieldQuantity` / `yieldUnit` / `coHarvestable` + the pool pass `poolComponentNeeds` (D-WS9-182 · 189 · 195) for *two rows, one purchase* (peppers + sauce; stems + leaves + whole); the per-ingredient pack yield (D-WS9-225 — the garlic `subUnit` ladder generalised; Hans's September 7 figures are its first rows: a bunch is ~1 oz, 2 cups leaves / 1 cup chopped, celery 8 stalks, pineapple 4 cups) for *one row, two units* (cilantro in cups against a bunch). **What made it whack-a-mole was feeding the table one food at a time. B1 feeds it BY CLASS in one pass: every "part" (brine, stems, leaves, zest, tops, fronds, rind) gets its co-harvest edge, every count-sold produce gets its yield, reviewed by exception on one numbered list.** The chipotle code fix (parent already on the list wins) landed September 11 and held in the census; jalapeño brine + slices ordering two jars is the same shape with no edge yet — the class sweep covers it.

### D-WS9-281 — Intellectual property before launch: ™ on "Kiwi" and "Kitchen Wizard" now, no rename; a PROVISIONAL patent on the recipe-to-purchase conversion, filed by Hans before he presses release in either store — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 28, 2026)

- Tags: `[LAUNCH]` `[LEGAL]` `[IP]` `[RULED]`
- Source: Hans asked what to copyright, patent or mark before launch; chat-Claude answered (not legal advice). Hans, verbatim: *"recipe to purchase is actually kind of unique. it may be worth applying for for $65-$130. let's go with the TM marks for now. I'm not going to rename at this point, so if I can't get an R after I'll have to live with it. is the patent application something you can draft and I can file after reviewing?"*
- ✅ **Marks:** ™ on the app and site now (free, no filing); ® never until a registration issues. **No rename** — "Kiwi" is crowded (a live KIWI registration exists for downloadable mobile apps, a keyboard app, Class 9, Reg. 5,116,802); a registration attempt is optional and later ($350 per class at the USPTO). The © line names the legal entity once the Delaware entity exists.
- ✅ **Patent: a PROVISIONAL application** (12-month placeholder; never examined; establishes a priority date only for what it DESCRIBES — so the description must be complete). **Subject: the recipe-to-purchase conversion** — turning a week of recipe demands in preparation units (cups chopped, cloves, tablespoons of juice, a jar's brine) into a shopping list of whole retail packs: identity and synonym folding with never-fold vetoes; component pools where derived parts ride with their source (`max` across co-harvestable parts, sum across exclusive ones); per-ingredient pack yields converting a measured need into packs once, after summing; round-up with a garnish forgiveness only for fast-perishing bunch-sold produce; the generic line with a specific qualifier; the order hand-off with pack counts. **Chat-Claude drafts; Hans reviews and files through USPTO Patent Center as the inventor.** Micro entity ($65) if Hans's own 2025 gross income was under $262,380 and he has been named on ≤ 4 prior US applications (form SB/15A); otherwise small entity ($130). Cover sheet SB/16.
- 🔴 **Timing is the whole reason it is urgent:** releasing the app (or opening UAT, or any public demo of the list) is a public disclosure — it starts the one-year U.S. grace period and ends patent rights in most other countries. **File BEFORE pressing release in either store.** Hans controls that date (Apple manual release; Play managed publishing).
- ⚠️ **Inventorship:** only people can be inventors; AI is a tool (USPTO revised guidance, November 26, 2025). The conceptions here are Hans's (his rulings are recorded verbatim on D-WS9-182, 188, 200, 220, 280); drafting help does not change inventorship.
- ⚠️ **Not legal advice.** A patent attorney's review before filing is cheap insurance ($2k–$4k for a provisional); a provisional filed without one is legal and common. A non-provisional (the real application, $4k–$25k with an attorney) is due within 12 months or the date lapses.

Hans reviews for accuracy and anything missing, then files; an attorney's read is optional and recommended.

### D-WS9-282 — The generic/specific fold, RULED by Hans on September 28, 2026 (third and final form that evening): buy what the recipe says; a plain name with an everyday default joins the default; a plain name with no default stays generic and CARRIES the called-out varieties in whole counts ("5 bell peppers, at least 2 red and at least 2 yellow"); never a share in a measure — ✅ RULED

- Tags: `[GROCERY]` `[SPEC]` `[RULED]`
- **Hans, verbatim (message 1):** *"4lb chicken thighs, at least 1 3/4 lb boneless skinless isn't correct. recipes should be calling for what they need (bone-in, or boneless skinless). if a recipe calls for generic Chicken Thighs, I would assume it means bone-in. red/white/yellow onions are unique to each other. … I want to be sure we're not doing like "1 bunch parsley, at least 1/2 cup broad leaf parsley"."*
- **Hans, verbatim (message 2, the ruling):** *"I think chicken thighs should be "boneless skinless" or "bone in" … I think peppers can actually be on separate lines. ONLY if there's a meal that says "bell peppers" would we do '5 bell peppers, at least 2 red and at least 2 yellow.' and that's only because we don't know what the other bell pepper should be and the recipe didn't tell us. which avoids 1 line for red bell peppers, 1 line for yellow bell peppers, and another line for 1 bell peppers. I think the big piece is that we do buy what the recipe says, but if it's generic it says "get whatever generic, but be sure you get these specific varieties because your recipes called those out"."* And: *"this is the hard stuff that we spent a couple weeks going in circles on."*
- **Why it came up:** the B2 NAMES Part A audit (`16d9813`) found the dry run folding sibling varieties with no generic demand and, on `f5556c19`, turning 1 yellow + 3 red + 2¼ cups white onion into `1 medium red onion (at least one red; …) (6¼ cup)` — a 7→1 under-order the preview could not see because it bypassed pack resolution. Chat-Claude's first two answers (F1–F3: generic line + shares in the buy unit; then G1–G7: an interchangeable pepper set) were each corrected by Hans within the hour. ⚠️ **The lesson, in Hans's words: buy what the recipe says.** The list is not an optimiser; the only fold that invents anything is the one where the RECIPE left the choice open.
- ✅ **H1 — buy what the recipe says.** Named varieties, colors, cuts and states are bought as named; different ones never merge with each other (onion and pepper colors; bone-in vs boneless; skin-on vs skinless; potato/apple/tomato/chili varieties; dried/fresh/frozen; seasoned; hot vs mild; flavored sauces).
- ✅ **H2 — a plain name with a ruled everyday DEFAULT joins the default's line, named as the default** (chicken thighs → boneless skinless chicken thighs; chicken breast → boneless skinless — both ruled September 28, the thighs default flipped from bone-in the same evening, see below). Defaults are data Hans rules from a short numbered list; NONE is always safe.
- ✅ **H3 — a plain name with NO default stays generic and carries the called-out varieties** — ONLY when a recipe demanded the generic itself: `5 bell peppers, at least 2 red and at least 2 yellow`. Shares are whole units of the line's buy unit, never a measure. When the shares cover the whole count, or the line is one package, the line takes the variety's name (¼ cup parsley + ½ cup flat-leaf → `1 bunch flat-leaf parsley`). **This is D-WS9-224's rendering, kept for exactly this case.**
- ✅ **H4 — a plain name is NEVER upgraded to a specific** (Hans, message 3: *"if the recipe is specific, we honor it. but in lieu of that, we go generic. so "1 tbsp parsley" => "parsley" whereas "1 tbsp italian parsley" => "italian parsley". my big concern … is the user just needing some parsley, the flavor won't be significantly different for most cooks using parsley, flat leaf, or italian, and I don't want them unable to find or shop for something more rare and specific."*). When both appear, H3 carries the specific in whole counts; only a single package takes the specific's name. ⛔ The earlier "buy the specific for the whole amount" rule is withdrawn. Hedge words that are not products (ripe, about 1-inch, finely chopped) are stripped, not treated as varieties.
- ✅ **H5 — weight- and volume-sold generics never carry shares:** a default or separate lines.
- ✅ **H6 — after any fold, B1's arithmetic runs on the group total** (never a member's pack count).
- ✅ **H7 — the retailer hand-off keeps the constraint:** product words stay in the search term (`boneless skinless chicken thighs`); an H3 line is sent as separate items (2 red, 2 yellow, 1 any).
- ✅ **Also ruled at the audit (chat-Claude, delegated):** every grocery preview runs the full pipeline + the client compose with an automatic packs × size ≥ need gate; romaine → hearts relabelled `synonym`; cooking by-products take the never-order flag; `basmati` lowercased; BUG-160's shopper-line half goes to block C.

- ✅ **PART A2 AUDITED PASS (September 28; `c72bca0` · `eb4f195`, nothing written).** The dry run now runs the real pipeline through pack resolution (its BEFORE matches B1's Part E: `3 heads Garlic (25 cloves)`); Gates: 0 new under-orders, 0 "at least" with a measure, 0 mixed-variety lines. **Blast radius on 20 lists: 317 rows change — 276 casing, 30 buy names, 4 residue, and SEVEN folds: two H3 rider lines (`6 bell peppers, at least 2 green`; `2 yellow onions, at least 1 large`) and one single-bunch collapse (`1 bunch flat-leaf parsley`).** H1 does nearly all the work, which is what "buy what the recipe says" means. - Tags: `[GROCERY]` `[RECURRING]` `[RULED]`
- Source: grocery B3 Part A (`150ce1f`, dev; a full-pipeline gated dry run over the 20 census plans: 176 rows changed, 1,045 → 1,031 rows, 96 → 96 recurring marks, Gates 1–4 clean).
- **What Part A measured:** recurring items are a bare free-text list on the user's preferences; the match was exact equality against catalog canonicals, so no recurring text ever met a plan row (0 of 96 in the census); a synthetic's pack came from the typical-purchase table or a per-generation Haiku guess that nothing stored. On dev: 18 distinct texts across 13 users — 13 resolve; 4 foods do not (paper towels, toilet paper, pet treats, coffee). D-WS9-228's `milk → whole milk` already lives in the alias table.
- ✅ **The rules:**
  1. **Resolve at every generation; store nothing per user (no migration).** Through the lookup that never creates a catalog row — never the upserting resolver, which would mint paper towels as ingredients. Per-user quantities wait for the day a user can write one on a recurring item (Hans's D-WS9-188 framing: *"write down what the user clarified … so it never asks twice"*) — that is where a migration belongs, not here.

### D-WS9-285 — Grocery block C (the client) rulings, and one wire contract: the server's whole-pack count travels as `packCount`; the phone never re-derives a count it was sent — ✅ RULED (chat-Claude, delegated; September 29, 2026)

- Tags: `[GROCERY]` `[CLIENT]` `[WIRE]` `[RULED]`
- Source: block C Part A (read-only, on the B3 after-state corpus) and B4 Part A, the same day.
- 🔴 **The finding that forced a contract (M1):** the pack display's leading number means two things — the SIZE of one pack (`1.5 lb pack`) or the COUNT the server already scaled to (`4 can (14.5 oz)`) — and `purchaseQuantity` carries the same ambiguity; the phone divides by it. Today the collision is fenced only by accident (the phone cannot relate can↔cup), and the one client rule that would fix broth's under-order (reading a parenthetical `oz` as fluid) is UNSAFE: 305 rows move, nine absurdly (a 5-oz bag of salad greens against 4 cups → seven bags), because `oz` on a label is weight for most solids and no string rule can tell.
- ✅ **Ruled:** **`packCount: number | null` on every grocery-list item** — the server's whole-pack count for the summed need when it could compute one (pack yield, sub-unit ladder, same-unit), else null; additive (the 1.0 client strips it); Instacart's payload uses it directly. **The client trusts `packCount` when present and parses the display only when it is null.** Server half in B4; client half in C.
- ✅ **Client rules:** range pack sizes read as their LOWER bound (R2: the lower figure buys more); `ct`/`cnt`/`ea` are `each`; weight-oz-as-fluid is refused and pinned by a test. BUG-329 (`quantity <= 1`) lands BEFORE the plural engine is wired into the ingredient line, or "½ heads" ships. The web's measure-unit plural table ports back verbatim (abbreviations unpluralised). A range span in step text keeps its authored text under scaling (BUG-326). ### D-WS9-286 — `packCount` AS BUILT (grocery B4 · C, `70d1bd8`): a render count the phone trusts, NEVER the Instacart multiplier — D-WS9-285's payload clause is withdrawn — ✅ BUILT and CORRECTED (September 29, 2026)

- Tags: `[GROCERY]` `[WIRE]` `[BUILT]` `[CORRECTION]`
- Source: B4 Part C (N14) and block C Part B (M15), the same afternoon; both lanes cite this ID in code.
- ✅ **Built:** `GroceryListItem.packCount Int?` (migration `20260929180000_grocery_b4_pack_count`, dev), emitted by `resolvePurchaseFields` — the one place that knows which branch it took (pack yield · sub-unit ladder · same-unit). 696 of 1,021 corpus rows carry one. The phone renders it and never re-derives a count it was sent (D-WS9-285); Gate 1's unverifiable rows fell 638 → 297 across B4 (the same-unit rule + 88 label-derived yields).
- 🔴 **Withdrawn — D-WS9-285's clause "Instacart's payload uses it directly":** `purchaseQuantity === packCount` is a COINCIDENCE on 579 rows, not an invariant; the per-pack SIZE of a scaled row exists only inside `purchaseDisplay`, so one field cannot serve both readings. Trusting it ordered 2 lb against a 2¼–3¾ lb need (an under-order B4 introduced and reverted the same Part), and the client half would have sent 5 cans as 25 (M15: a count fed into a multiply built for a size). **The Instacart order path keeps its own arithmetic (correct for both shapes); `packCount` is for consumers that RENDER a count.** Pinned by a break in each lane.
- ✅ **Two rules that came out of the build:** (1) `oz` on a label means fluid ounces only on a bottle, carton or jug; everywhere else it is net weight; where both readings are admissible the LOWER wins (17 fl oz of oil = 2.125 cups is right; a 5-oz bag of lettuce at ⅛ cup per ounce is not) — density is not the discriminator (honey is a liquid at 340 g/cup, salt a solid at 273). (2) **Whoever writes the count owns its plural:** the server's scaled display now inflects its lead word (`2 cans`), because the client pluralises only when it scales.
- ✅ **Also:** the H3 rider's `buyUnitsForNeed` was NOT reused for the pack count (a "3 peppers" pack against three peppers is three buy units and one pack — 52 rows) — `packsForRow` asks the pack question; N12's same-unit rule lives there.
- Owner: built. Status: ✅ BUILT on dev (server) + read by the 1.1 client (block C); production with the post-approval deploy and runbook §B4.
- Cross-ref: D-WS9-285 · D-WS9-284 · D-WS9-221 · BUG-333 · `claude/kiwi_row8_instacart_build_spec.md` (the order path).

They are the Block 1c migration's backfill of user-authored meals with no image (D-WS9-248), 242 of them on Hans's demo account. **And a live path keeps minting them:** a fork COPIED `failed` from its parent, so every plan built from a backfilled meal was born imageless — the Apple reviewer account's 8 meals, created one minute after signup on September 25, are exactly this. ### D-WS9-289 — Kitchen timers notify when they finish: permission asked at the first timer start, a local notification at the timer's end, shipped in 1.1; "time to start cooking" reminders are the future use — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 29, 2026)

- Tags: `[COOK-MODE]` `[NOTIFICATIONS]` `[RULED]` `[1.1]`
- Source: the September 29 design review (D-WS9-291), technical audit item A5.
- **Found (CC code read, not device-verified):** Cook Mode timers are haptic-only and foreground-only. Completion fires a haptic and nothing else; there is no `AppState` handling, so backgrounding suspends the tick and completion fires late, on resume; timer state is component state inside the Cook Mode session view, so leaving the screen drops every running timer. A phone propped by a cutting board never alerts.
- ✅ **Hans, verbatim:** *"we should ask for notification permission on the next submission to the appstore and allow for notifications when timers go off. roadmap wise, we want to tell people when to start cooking, but that's not near term. just context on why we should do that overall."*
- ✅ **Chat-Claude's calls (delegated, reversible):** the permission is asked IN CONTEXT at the user's first timer start — never at signup or onboarding; a denial falls back silently to today's haptic and is not re-asked in that session; a scheduled notification SURVIVES leaving Cook Mode (the food is still cooking) and is cancelled only when the user cancels or clears the timer; "add a minute" reschedules it; the sound is the notification's own (foreground presentation on), so no audio asset ships.
- ⚠️ **Ships on `next` → the 1.1 binary.** A notifications module plus its permission text is a store-reviewed native change, and D-WS9-279 forbids an OTA to the 1.0 binaries. **Not provable on the web export or Expo Go — the proof is a development build from `next`.**
- 🔵 **Future (roadmap, not near-term):** "time to start cooking" reminders derived from the plan — the same permission covers them; never ask twice.
- **Carried, not in scope:** persisting a running timer across leaving Cook Mode (on return the chip is gone though the notification still fires).
- ✅ **AMENDED September 30 — iOS ONLY for 1.1; Android keeps today's haptic (Hans, verbatim: *"agreed with a proper iOS timer and maintaining the same in Android."*).** The design-fix Phase 0 read the module source: without `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` in the merged manifest (expo-notifications declares only `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` and `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`; its plugin adds nothing), Android 12+ takes the INEXACT branch. Android's own docs: *"On Android 12 (API level 31) and higher, the system invokes the alarm within one hour of the supplied trigger time, unless any battery-saving restrictions are in effect such as battery saver or Doze."* ⚠️ **A kitchen timer that can fire an hour late is worse than none — so on Android nothing is scheduled and no notification permission is asked.** The exact-alarm path is its own follow-up: `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is denied by default for new installs on Android 14+ (targeting 13+), so it needs a trip to the system "Alarms & reminders" screen — a second permission step at the stove, judged on Hans's phone before it ships. (`USE_EXACT_ALARM` is Play-policy-restricted to calendar / alarm-clock apps — not this app.)
- ⚠️ **Prompt correction, recorded:** the expo-notifications plugin was ALREADY in `app.json` with `{"mode": "production"}` (the September 23 packaging lane) — no native change is owed for the iOS half.
- Status: ✅ RULED · 🟡 build commissioned in the design-fix block (D-WS9-291). · Cross-ref: D-WS9-291 · D-WS9-279.

### D-WS9-292 — Fresh meat, poultry and seafood are bought BY WEIGHT, the need rounded UP to the next ¼ lb — never a stored "pack" — with three exceptions (packaged meats, whole items, count needs) — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 30, 2026; exceptions chat-Claude's, delegated)

- Tags: `[GROCERY]` `[INSTACART]` `[RULED]`
- **Source:** the grocery block E device pass, item 14. The list showed `4 lb pack boneless skinless chicken breasts (2½ pound)` and `3 lb pack boneless skinless chicken thighs (1¾ pound)`; chat-Claude's browser pass the same night added `3.5 lb pack lean ground beef (1½ pound)`.
- ✅ **Hans, verbatim:** *"I thought the ruling was on meat to order the pack as the quantity needed. they might not sell 1.5 lbs of pork shoulder, but getting 4 lbs of boneless skinless chicken breasts when I only need 2.5 and 3 lbs thighs when I need 1.75 of that is wrong. And thighs are sold in packs smaller than 3lbs … for meat, order the quantity needed. please push back if you think there are valid scenarios I'm not considering"*
- ✅ **The rule:** a fresh meat, poultry or seafood row whose need is a WEIGHT buys that weight, rounded UP to the next ¼ lb (never under-buy — R2), and reads as a weight line (*"2½ lb boneless skinless chicken breasts"*); the need parenthetical stays. Instacart receives the weight (it already sends weight totals); a counter or a shopper fills to about the weight. **This replaces D-WS9-221's smallest-normal-pack × count for this class only.**
- ✅ **Exceptions (chat-Claude's pushback, on record):** (1) **packaged meats sold only in fixed packages** keep the pack logic — bacon, sausage links, hot dogs, deli/lunch meat, pepperoni, salami, prosciutto, pancetta, canned fish; (2) **whole items are bought by count** — whole chicken, whole turkey, Cornish hen, whole ham, rack of ribs or lamb: `1 whole chicken`, whatever weight the recipe names; (3) 🔴 **AMENDED by Hans the same night — a COUNT need converts to weight:** *"a chicken breast is probably 1/2 lb on average, so 4 breasts = 2 lbs"* — pieces × an average piece weight (the typical-purchase table first; boneless skinless chicken breast ½ lb is his figure), summed with any weight need for the same food, rounded up to the next ¼ lb; a cut with no defensible piece weight stays a count. Hans's own caveat (*"they might not sell 1.5 lbs of pork shoulder"*) is the counter case and the answer is the same rule: a shopper hands over the nearest piece at or above the weight.
- ✅ **Block F Part A measured it (CC `ab32278`, 20-plan corpus): 68 meat & seafood rows — 53 by weight, 8 fixed-package, 2 whole-item, 5 count needs (which now convert), 0 unclassified.** Classification = the row's section × a weight need, minus name-keyed lists. **Chat-Claude's rulings on the lists:** the exception list is the RULED list, carried whether or not the corpus has a row today (bacon, sausage incl. breakfast, hot dogs, deli, pepperoni, salami, prosciutto, pancetta, canned fish incl. anchovy) **plus smoked salmon / lox** (sold only in small fixed packs — the ruling's own test); NOT ham steak, corned beef, crab cakes (buyable by weight, or not in the meat aisle). Rotisserie chicken stays as today (its two display forms are a names question, not this rule's).
- ✅ **BUILT on dev (block F, `f5f357f`; audited PASS):** writes no catalog row — the stored pack stops being consulted for the class, so the rule reverts by removing one block. `4 lb pack boneless skinless chicken breasts (3½ pound)` → `3½ lb …`; `3.5 lb pack lean ground beef (1½ pound)` → `1½ lb …`; 4 breasts → 2 lb. The Instacart payload carries the weights.
- Status: ✅ RULED · ✅ BUILT on dev (Cloud Run after approval). · Cross-ref: D-WS9-221 · D-WS9-280 (R2) · D-WS9-286 · D-WS9-295 · BUG-124.

### D-WS9-297 — The Prep & Cook pass, Part A rulings: the scheduler gets a LATEST bound; cues come from the step's prose in the number-neutral form; cold dishes come forward into passive windows; Cook Mode's third clock is deleted; prep quantities use glyphs; the cook day is threaded to the prep generator — ✅ RULED (chat-Claude, delegated; September 30, 2026)

- Tags: `[COOK-MODE]` `[PREP-WEEK]` `[SCHEDULER]` `[RULED]`
- **Source:** Part A census (`5fca53f`, 13 plans, $1.26). Findings on BUG-337 / BUG-338.
- ✅ **Scheduler:** a per-step max lag from its dish predecessor (rest after heat ≤ 2 min; anything after heat ≤ 5 min), under the existing two-pass anomaly guard — a meal that grows > 10% is listed, not silently accepted · the cue is *"While the X is cooking / resting / chilling / marinating"* with the state from the window step's prose, no cue when the step is neither heat nor passive, "stays warm" only for a hot hold · the same-offset tie closed by sequence index · ⚠️ **cold dishes (salsa, pico, guacamole, slaw, salad, dressing, crema) are NOT finish-aligned; they pull forward into the nearest passive window ≥ 10 min** — a design change chat-Claude rules in because a blind follower needs something to do in a 30-minute marinade and pico is meant to sit; **Hans may reverse it on device.**
- ✅ **Client:** Cook Mode's footer stops flat-summing step minutes and reads the scheduler's offsets — two clocks, never three · the 4 stale `Meal.estimatedTimeMinutes` re-stamped (dev; runbook for production).
- ✅ **Prep assembly:** `0.25` → `¼`, "each" → the noun, `1 ½` → `1½` — **the spaced mixed number's deliberate comment is retired: one app writes quantities one way (Hans ruled glyphs in the grocery pass)** · the juice step states its fruit count · a lone sub-tablespoon dry measure folds into its dish's blend step (interim; components in B2 make most of them disappear) · the join sentence names the component and never calls liquids "spices" · a demoted step's title may not command the action it forbids (prompt v10, §7).
- 🔵 **B2 — components (D-WS9-296):** `combinePrep` gains a component grouping key (dish × role: marinade / sauce / blend / garnish) derived from the steps' `amountRefs`, so the engine emits one step per component per dish and names its bowl. Sized from B1's numbers.
- 🔵 **B3 — the storage shape (P-R3), HANS DECIDES:** prerequisite threaded in B1 (`assignedDate` → `daysUntilCook` per step). Options: **(a) a second mid-week prep session** (fits the data — overruns cluster at lag 3–5 days; needs a second `PrepWeekStructure` slot and a second AI call) · (b) late-week perishables demoted to cook-day prep (cheapest; shrinks the feature for the furthest meals) · (c) freeze instructions (raw flesh only, 15 of 57). **Chat-Claude recommends (a) with (b) for the tail.** Either way the storage note becomes computed from the lag, never the model's guess.

### D-WS9-298 — Prep the Week storage: ONE session, no programming around the cook day; the storage note is the generally accepted home-kitchen window for that food, stated as guidance; "don't prep ahead" items stay demoted; raw flesh past its window gets a freeze line — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 30, 2026; the raw-flesh line chat-Claude's, pending his word)

- Tags: `[PREP-WEEK]` `[FOOD-SAFETY]` `[RULED]`
- ✅ **Hans, verbatim:** *"while it's not restaurant-food-safe to store some food from Sunday to Thursday, I think it's ok for most home kitchens to store things in an airtight container for 3-4 days without risking foodborne illness. marinading can't happen too early, cutting tomatoes to top a burger should happen when the meal is cooked not ahead of time, pico can hold up through the week but gets a little soft by Thursday... I don't want to get sued, so "airtight container for *generally accepted timeline*" is a good guide for the user, but I don't think we have to program for it if they are making pico on sunday for tacos on thursday (that seems like a reasonable choice)."*
- ✅ **So B3 is NOT (a) a second session and NOT (b) lag-driven demotion.** One prep session; the user decides. The storage note becomes **a curated window per food class** ("Airtight container in the fridge, up to 4 days"), written by the engine from a small table — never the model's guess, so it is consistent and defensible — and the existing demotion rule keeps marinade-contact, sliced tomato, cut avocado and their kind on cook day.
- ⚠️ **Chat-Claude's one addition, for Hans's yes:** raw fish, poultry and ground meat have an accepted window of 1–2 days, so a Sunday portion for Friday sits outside ANY accepted timeline. For that class only, when `daysUntilCook` (threaded in B1) exceeds the window, the note reads *"Freeze; move to the fridge the night before."* Text only — no session, no demotion — and it is the "generally accepted timeline" guide applied honestly to the one class where "a reasonable choice" is not one.
- ✅ **AMENDED the same evening — Hans's ruling on the raw-protein line, and the freeze line is OUT:** *"for fish, chicken, ground meat - I think we say something like "fish, poultry, and other meat should be cooked or consumed within 2 days of handling. prep meals ahead of time based on when you plan to cook, or save this step for when you're ready to eat" … I don't want a lot of big alerts in the app, so something clear, but subtle."* And: *"if we get [days assigned automatically], we could exclude the meat prep on "prep the week" for meals later in the week. and if users aren't sure and unassign (realistically, this will happen ad-hoc a lot when plans change throughout the week), we just tell them not to cut the chicken breasts and store the cut strips in the fridge for too long before cooking."*
- ✅ **Day assignment IS built (D-WS7-213 half 1, September 16 — perishability tier first, easiest last, first meal tomorrow; display half deferred), so the exclusion he describes costs one rule on top of B1's `daysUntilCook`.** The Proteins phase (already last, for food safety) therefore renders, per step: **cook day ≤ 2 days out** → the step with the quiet note *"Covered in the fridge — cook within 2 days."* · **cook day > 2 days out** → the step is demoted (`skipSuggested`, render-omitted like today's do-not-prep items) · **unassigned** → the step with the line *"Raw fish, poultry and meat keep about 2 days once handled — prep this the day before you cook, or leave it for cook day."* Plus one quiet line in the Proteins phase intro, always: *"Fish, poultry and meat keep about two days once handled, so this phase only preps what you'll cook soon."* Quiet tier (the existing storage-note style) — no alert, no modal. BUG-280 (seafood and meat both `Protein`) still keeps "fish first" at tier level only.
- ✅ **BUILT on dev (B3, September 30) — the table as built, first match wins, raw flesh first:** raw fish / raw meat 2 days ("Covered in the fridge — cook within 2 days.") · leafy herbs 3 (with a barely damp paper towel) · citrus juice 3 · citrus wedges 3 · cut alliums 4 · cut peppers 4 · cooked grains 4 · sauces and dressings 5 · spice blends at room temperature, weeks · **fallback 3 — the shortest window, because over-cautious wastes food and the other way makes someone ill.** Across 13 plans the raw-flesh misfires went 7 → 0; P-R3's 29 remaining are all non-flesh. **The label decides the kind, the contents decide the flesh** (a "Chicken Fajitas seasoning bowl" is not raw chicken).
- 🔵 **Left by this ruling, a judgement for Hans at the device pass:** those 29 are a 3-day herb or vinaigrette whose cook day is 4–5 days out. The ruling leaves that choice to the user; whether the note reads acceptably beside a Friday cook day is a device call, not a defect. **BUG-340** (anchovy paste read as raw flesh) is the one misfire left.
- Status: ✅ RULED · ✅ BUILT on dev (device pass owed). · Cross-ref: D-WS9-297 · D-WS7-213 · BUG-280 · BUG-338 · BUG-340 · D-WS9-296.
