### D-WS9-299 — Prep-worthiness: a prep step exists only when it saves weeknight time — a mixture of three or more measured items, two items that must sit together, or knife work; a single condiment, oil or spice measured alone is never prep — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 30, 2026)

- Tags: `[PREP-WEEK]` `[RULED]`
- ✅ **Hans, verbatim:** *"This came up previously, and it was creating steps like "measure 2 tbsp ketchup for the burgers" which no one will actually do. you don't pre-measure condiments on Sunday for a burger on Thursday. And if I just have to add 1 tsp salt to something, I don't need to pre-measure that out as part of prep. a home cook would have 30 little containers to fill up. I think the rule is really that measuring 1 thing (condiment, cooking oil, single spice), or even 2 simple things that don't need to sit and mix together, isn't part of prep. what adds time to a weeknight, especially with an unfamiliar meal, is measuring 6 things with different quantities for a mix and double checking your work, and then cleaning up a tsp tbsp 1/2 tsp, 2/3 cup, 1/4 cup measures because you had a lot to mix. on sunday, you just keep the measuring stuff out and do your dry ingredients first, so it cuts down on washing and finding stuff in the kitchen."*
- ✅ **The rule:** prep = (a) a mixture of ≥ 3 measured items, or (b) 2 items that must sit together (marinade, brine, quick pickle, soak), or (c) knife work and washing. **Not prep:** one condiment / oil / vinegar / spice alone; two simple things added at the stove; anything added straight from its container. Widens D-WS7-150's skip rule; demoted items stay render-omitted. Built in B2 Parts B–D beside the components.
- ✅ **BUILT on dev (B2 Parts B–D, September 30):** across 13 plans, 348 prep steps → 264 kept and 84 demoted; vessels 524 → 321. ✅ **CC's correction, adopted:** as first written the rule demoted every unmarinated protein as "a single item" — **proteins are EXEMPT; their rule is D-WS9-298's.**
- Status: ✅ RULED · ✅ BUILT on dev (device pass owed). · Cross-ref: D-WS9-296 · D-WS9-298 · D-WS7-150 · BUG-338.

### D-WS9-300 — The QA harness's operating rules: a quick check only when a block changes what users see or do; the full run only on Hans's word; every UI block updates the harness for the screens it changes — ✅ RULED (Hans, September 30, 2026)

- Tags: `[QA]` `[PROCESS]` `[RULED]`
- **Source:** QA harness Part A (Playwright against `localhost:9000` + the dev database, fence `artifacts/kiwi/e2e/`): five plans end to end in 9.2 minutes for $0.64, the census checkers spawned unmodified, three screen-only rules (every row on screen · R3's three sentences · the glyph ladder). It found the 81-character `stepKey` crash independently and BUG-341, which the census cannot see.
- ✅ **Hans, verbatim:** *"yes, I like that plan. I just want to be thoughtful about when the automated testing runs, like only when there are UI changes or app/web behavior changes so it doesn't run unnecessarily. and I want to approve the bigger run before spending $7.70 and 40 minutes. It's awesome we can do this, but that could add up quick over time."*
- ✅ **The rules:**
  1. **Quick check** — 5 plans, ~$0.65, ~10 minutes — runs before Hans's device test **only for a block that changes what a user sees or does** (a screen, a flow, or server logic whose output renders). **Skipped** for docs, canon, harness-only, data-only with no rendered effect, and production runbooks. Each block's prompt says which, and why.
  2. **Full run** — 20 plans × 3 generations, ~$7.70, ~40 minutes on three test accounts — **only on Hans's explicit approval, every time.** The command refuses to start without an explicit spend flag, so approval is mechanical, not remembered.
  3. ✅ **Hans's question, answered as a standing rule: the harness changes WITH the UI.** Every block that changes a screen updates that screen's harness flow and assertions in the same block, and adds stable `testID`s to the controls it touches. A UI block is not done until its quick check passes against the new screen.
  4. Dedicated test accounts (three), credentials only in `C:\Cooking App\kiwi-local-tools\` (never the repo, never chat); the harness archives the plans and lists it creates.
- Cost per surface, measured: grocery ~$0.017 a list (it scales with unknown pack sizes, not list length) · Prep the Week narration ~$0.112 · Cook Mode and `/plans/from-meals` $0.

### D-WS9-301 — Prep the Week, the rules re-cut holistically: a container is the set of ingredients that enter the pot TOGETHER; dry blends and finished wet mixes of 3+ items; one shared container per chopped ingredient, not one per dish; ground meat untouched; herbs stay in prep; 10–15 containers, said up front — ✅ RULED (Hans, October 1, 2026)

- Tags: `[PREP-WEEK]` `[RULED]` `[SUPERSEDES-IN-PART]`
- **Source:** Hans's device pass (items 10–12) and chat-Claude's browser walk of the week-of-Sep-30 plan: 28 steps, ~30 containers, ~2 hours — "Measure the rice cumin" (½ tsp alone), "Get out five small containers, one per dish" for garlic, the taco seasoning with diced onion in it, the lemon-herb marinade split across two phases, ground beef portioned into tubs.
- ✅ **Hans, verbatim, the goal:** *"maybe my 'full mis en place' target was too much for a home chef's sunday prep. I'd like to get there if it's clear and easy for a home cook to have a stack of 10-15 containers on Sunday (or even more within reason) and they know their week is going to be easy cooking."* And: *"a reasonable workable amount of dishes a home cook can easily dump in to a cook step without thought."* **Restated as the test: a prep step exists only if it removes thought or time from the weeknight. Not full mise en place.**
- ✅ **THE RULES:**
  1. **A container = the ingredients that enter the cooking process at the SAME MOMENT (the same cook step).** Hans: *"the key there is when they go into the cooking process they go in at the same time… the key piece there is making sure the containers are supposed to be combined or separated at cook time."* Slow-cooker herbs + onion + chicken all go in together → one container is right. Tacos: onion is sautéed first, spices go in after browning → two containers (or the onion stays whole, rule 4). **This supersedes D-WS9-296's "one bowl per component" where a component's parts enter at different moments**, and it is what the lemon-herb marinade got backwards: all its parts enter together (into the marinade), so it is ONE container finished in ONE step — the lemon's zest and juice are prepped inside that step, not deferred to the produce phase.
  2. **Dry blend:** 3+ dry items for one dish → one shelf-stable container, named by dish and use ("chili spice blend", "taco seasoning", "burger seasoning blend"). Dry only; garlic, onion and fresh herbs never join it (they would send a shelf jar to the fridge).
  3. **Wet mix** (marinade, dressing, piccata-style liquids): 3+ items, or 2 that must sit together → one container, finished in one step. Hans: herbs in oil are fine ("herbs in oil work well if they stay in there for a while"); piccata's four liquids are "borderline beneficial" and allowed. **Never pre-measured alone:** cooking oil, a glaze, a single condiment or spice (D-WS9-299 stands).
  4. **Knife work on produce and WHOLE proteins is prep** (cube, trim, skin, peel shrimp, cut strips). **Ground meat is never touched** — not portioned, not formed, not moved out of its package until the pan (Hans: *"ground meat shouldn't be touched until it's ready to cook"*). The "Portion the ground beef" step is gone.
  5. **A chopped ingredient used by several dishes goes in ONE container, labelled with its dishes** ("minced garlic — chili, enchiladas"), never one container per dish; the cook portions at the stove. This is the single largest cut (18 containers → 5 on the sample plan).
  6. **Herbs STAY in prep** (Hans, overruling chat-Claude's proposal to defer delicate herbs): *"if I have a lot of cilantro to cut I'd rather cut it ahead if I want. and arguably a pre-made garnish will easily elevate the meal and might be skipped when things get busy."* Cut citrus (wedges, rounds) may be prepped but is low-value — first to drop under rule 7.
  7. **Target 10–15 containers.** The screen states the container count and total time up front ("12 containers · about 40 minutes"). When a plan runs over, the engine drops the lowest-value steps first — single-dish garnish portions, citrus wedges — rather than splitting further. A plan may exceed 15 "within reason" (Hans) when every step clears the test.
  8. **Containers are "containers"**, named by dish + use, never "bowl 1" / "dish A" (Hans: *"'chicken fajita seasoning dish' and 'asada marinade dish' or 'burger seasoning blend'"*).
- **What stands unchanged:** the storage table and the protein day rule (D-WS9-298); prep-worthiness for lone items (D-WS9-299); the K-rules.
- Status: ✅ RULED · 🔵 build = Prep & Cook Part H. · Cross-ref: D-WS9-296 (superseded in part by rule 1) · D-WS9-298 · D-WS9-299 · BUG-338 · BUG-346.
